4	
5	<p align="center"><strong>Run your coding agent unattended, and trust the result.</strong></p>
6	
7	<p align="center">
8	DeadReckon is a harness around the agent CLI you already use.<br>
9	A separate watchdog process, not the agent, decides when the work is actually done.<br>
10	You get a signed, auditable artifact instead of a chat transcript you have to take on faith.
11	</p>
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Get started
16	
17	Install the latest release (macOS / Linux):
18	
19	```bash
20	curl -fsSL https://deadreckon.sh/install.sh | sh
21	```
22	
23	This downloads the release installer, verifies it against `SHA256SUMS`, and installs `deadreckon`. Pin a version with `DEADRECKON_TAG=v0.1.0-rc.1`.
24	
25	Or build from source:
26	
27	```bash
28	cargo build --release          # binary at ./target/release/deadreckon
29	```
30	
31	Then the whole tool is five commands:
32	
33	| Command | What it does |
34	|---|---|
35	| `deadreckon start "build the app"` | Kick off a supervised run. Walk away. |
36	| `deadreckon attach latest` | Watch it work live. `Ctrl-D` leaves it running. |
37	| `deadreckon status` | What happened, and the one thing to do next. |
38	| `deadreckon list` | Find recent runs and plans. |
39	| `deadreckon finish latest` | Apply it to your branch, or export it. |
40	
41	For a higher-level read while it runs, `deadreckon attach latest --view narrative` shows cited prose plus an evidence-backed visual map.
42	
43	<p align="center">
44	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/claude-logo.png" alt="Claude Code" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
45	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/openai-logo.png" alt="Codex" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
46	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/gemini-logo.png" alt="Gemini CLI" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
47	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/github-logo.png" alt="GitHub Copilot CLI" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
48	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/opencode-logo.png" alt="OpenCode" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
49	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/pi-logo.svg" alt="Pi" height="34">
50	</p>
51	
52	<p align="center"><sub>Supervises the agent CLI you already use: Claude Code · Codex · Gemini · Copilot · OpenCode · Pi · or any Anthropic / OpenAI-compatible API.</sub></p>
53	
54	Everything else (budgets, undo, multi-step chains, provider routing) is optional power you reach for later. No API keys? `deadreckon run "hello" --smoke --sandbox none` exercises the whole harness against a faked provider.
55	
56	> [!TIP]
57	> DeadReckon is on the production-release track. The core lifecycle (isolated runs, signed gates, durable state, undo, docs, orchestration, and apply) is implemented and tested; release notes call out any compatibility migrations.
58	
59	## Why it's different
60	
61	- **It can't fake the finish.** A separate watchdog (`dr-gate`) holds a secret the agent process can't read and signs the result with it. No valid signature, no "done." The agent literally cannot mark its own work accepted.
62	- **Walk away for real.** Every turn is saved to disk. Close your laptop, lose the network, kill the model, then attach from another terminal and resume from the last completed turn.
63	- **Evidence, not a transcript.** Each accepted run promotes to a reviewable artifact: what changed, why, which prompt touched which file, what it spent.
64	
65	→ The full story (the loop, the mental model, and how it compares) is in **[Concepts & How It Works](docs/CONCEPTS.md)**.

76	| **[V1 Candidates](docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md)** | Deferred features and roadmap |
77	
78	DeadReckon is maintained as production-release software. The core lifecycle is implemented and tested, alongside multi-agent orchestration (`plan` / `fork` / `merge`), autonomous chains, the provider flight recorder with `rewind`, and a local self-improvement loop (`learn` / `improve`).

# DeadReckon Goal+Rider Survey

All files live in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/`. Each recent pair is grouped (goal + rider). The format is: (1) the user need it was designed against, (2) what success/acceptance looked like, (3) explicit non-goals/deferrals.

---

## PART 1 — RECENT GOALS (2026-05-24 and later)

### 1. provider-done-setup (2026-05-24-1426) — "Prepared"
- **Need:** "Today the pieces work, but each surface resolves providers, prompts, models, doc providers, and acceptance specs in its own local way" — `init`, `config provider`, `run`, `orchestrate`, doc polish, and `def-done` each carried separate setup logic, so the user got inconsistent previews, refusal wording, and help.
- **Success:** One shared provider-setup resolver (route, model, source, credential/install state, warnings, `try:` lines) and one shared done-criteria resolver used by all named surfaces; smokes prove `init --no-confirm` and `config provider` agree on wording, and `run --preview`/`orchestrate --preview` show the same done-criteria source. Behavior-compatible with existing routing, gate invariants, and orchestration semantics.
- **Non-goals (rider "Out of scope"):** full output-layout facade; command-family alias removal; new provider descriptor schema for ranking/benchmarks; automatic provider selection by quality/cost/latency; new durable plan/run schema fields; making custom done criteria mandatory; web/cloud setup wizard.

### 2. provider-flight-recorder (2026-05-25-2238) — "Recoverable"
- **Need:** "`cli:*` providers stop looking like one opaque DeadReckon turn" — DeadReckon snapshotted only before/after a CLI subprocess, so provider-native work inside a `claude`/`codex` invocation was invisible and un-rewindable. Explicitly tied back to the original unmet-needs report (`/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md` — "undo, provenance, observability, spend/context pain").
- **Success:** Per-run `flight-events.jsonl` + `flight-manifest.json`; live recorder sidecar tailing provider logs and emitting working-tree checkpoints; delta checkpoints under `<run_root>/checkpoints/`; `show --flight`/`show --file <path>`; `rewind --to-turn|--to-provider-event|--to-checkpoint --preview|--apply` with hash guards. Smoke: fake CLI provider writes JSONL + edits; rewind preview shows exact changes; apply restores only guarded files.
- **Non-goals:** forcing CLI providers into the one-action JSON protocol; rewriting provider-owned transcripts or transcript undo; exact subturn rewind without a checkpoint; web/desktop dashboard; remote/team sharing of flight events; rewinding exported dirs; applying superseded resume-attempt checkpoints; full AST-aware/semantic undo.

### 3. self-improvement-loop (2026-05-26-1325) — "Improving"
- **Need:** Prior run evidence (runstate, traces, provenance, gates, plan events, flight logs, docs) was inert; turn it into "a cautious learning loop rather than model training" — proposals from real friction, candidates run against DeadReckon itself, PRs only after an evidence gate.
- **Success:** New verbs `learn index/report/propose` and `improve self` work; evidence gate for PR opening requires opt-in, clean base, isolated worktree, non-weak done criteria, accepted candidate run, green verification, no redaction findings, and a stimulus→proposal→diff→verification→rollback evidence chain; high-risk changes (sandbox, gate/signature, credentials, release/CI, acceptance policy, privacy weakening) refuse auto-PR. `--pr-dry-run` proves the path with no network.
- **Non-goals:** training/fine-tuning models from runs; cloud telemetry/background sync/shared remote learning stores; auto-applying changes to `main`; live PR opening in tests; imported-only bundles opening PRs without local corroboration; multi-candidate evolutionary search; provider-routing learning that changes defaults; semantic replay/AST rewind; a learning TUI dashboard; cryptographically tamper-proof audit logs.

### 4. guided-experience (2026-05-26-1510) — "Guided"
- **Need:** "The substrate is strong, but the user must still learn too much command topology before the first serious run." Also an identity gap: make immediate that "DeadReckon is for people who already trust agent CLIs and need unattended, sandboxed, auditable work with a real definition of done" — the harness around those harnesses (isolation, done criteria, lifecycle, logs, evidence, recovery, promotion).
- **Success:** `deadreckon start "<goal>"` resolves provider, done criteria, source mode, and run-vs-orchestrate, then starts or previews. "Friendliness as a verifiable contract": one command from an ordinary repo either starts work or ends with concrete `try:` lines; every preview says who works, where, how done is checked, how to watch/stop, what finishes it. Smokes cover missing-provider, non-git, and review-mode preview recovery.
- **Non-goals/anti-promise:** not a chat app, cloud IDE, provider replacement, "magic autonomous employee," or unsupervised deploy tool. Deferred to V1 (rider P11): durable profiles, LLM mode classification, personalized onboarding, provider-specific wizards.

### 5. narrative-attach (2026-05-26-1546) — "Narrated"
- **Need:** "`attach` is strong for debugging, but multi-agent work can feel like machinery" — operators couldn't understand one run or many orchestrated agents without reading raw logs, diffs, or JSONL.
- **Success:** `attach --view narrative` with cited prose + evidence-backed architecture/agent/file maps; every provider claim cites immutable evidence (run event, trace id, flight event, checkpoint, file path, plan event, task id, child run id); event-driven cadence; explicit staleness; deterministic fallback when the summarizer is unavailable/over budget/refused. Stop conditions: works for running and completed runs and multi-child plans; raw activity stays one key away; outage/redaction/missing-evidence/narrow-terminal cases degrade cleanly.
- **Non-goals:** narrative is a projection, never a source of truth (no prose into `flight-events.jsonl`/`plan-events.jsonl`); no graph crates unless depth tests prove need. Deferred (rider P11): long-lived narrator daemon, richer trace DAG, learned summary preferences, richer graph layout, cloud/shareable observer views, historical analytics.

### 6. tui-responsiveness (2026-05-26-1924) — "Responsive"
- **Need:** "`attach` can feel frozen because blocking provider calls and full-file/full-tree reads share the loop that draws frames and handles `q`/`n`/`v`/`r`." Diagnosed concretely: narrative refresh awaits provider subprocess in the UI loop; each tick reloads full state/spend/traces/flight files; `inventory_files` walks `node_modules`/`.git`/Chrome `.tmp` trees; chain attach rereads the full event file each tick.
- **Success:** `q/Esc/Ctrl-D/n/v/j/k/Tab` responsive even with a pending provider refresh; `r` starts/coalesces a background refresh and never blocks detach; at most one auto-refresh in flight per attach target; panes may show stale data with age labels; cached/incremental collectors. Smokes: live narrative refresh detachable; large `.tmp` tree doesn't freeze live files; chain attach with large event file usable.
- **Non-goals:** daemonized attach service shared across terminals; remote/web attach UI; full async ratatui rewrite; new graph/visualization crate; replacing JSONL with a database; changing provider transcript formats; schema changes for convenience.

### 7. start-picker (2026-05-27-1032) — "Picker"
- **Need:** "TTY users still mostly accept heuristics or type flags, and the only true prompt is a numeric non-git source fallback" — make the happy path "feel like a normal terminal wizard."
- **Success:** Interactive pickers for mode, provider, done criteria, source, and final confirmation; defaults appear first with a reason; provider choices usable ephemerally without a config write; every mutation previewed with an equivalent manual `try:` command; non-TTY/`--json`/`--plain`/`--quiet` never prompt. Stop conditions include "selected providers flow into run/orchestrate dispatch without requiring a config write."
- **Non-goals:** no durable launch profiles, LLM mode classification, provider-specific setup wizard, cloud state; `start` stays a thin decision layer and never becomes an alternate-screen TUI. V1 keeps durable profiles / LLM classification / provider wizards as separate candidates.

### 8. production-command-model (2026-05-27-1152) — "Production"
- **Need:** "First-screen help and docs expose too many peer verbs before the user has a mental model" — the harness was powerful but its surface read as implementation topology.
- **Success:** A small default model — `start, attach, status, list, finish, doctor, kill, resume, cleanup` (Begin/Watch/Orient/Keep/Repair/Control/Continue/Done framing) — while `help-all`, per-command help, completions, and hints keep every other verb findable. Done-criteria prompts always show/evaluate/update criteria, "never ask users to accept an opaque gate." Smokes: `--help` shows the model; repo-history `start` can extend/orchestrate; completion intact.
- **Non-goals:** removing/renaming callable commands; durable launch profiles; automatic prior-run selection in non-TTY start; turning `extend` into a multi-agent primitive; a 1.0 declaration/SemVer policy/installer promotion; full output-layout facade; new discovery TUI screens; provider onboarding wizards; anything requiring state migration.

### 9. plan-doc-consolidation (2026-05-28-0943) — "Consolidated"
- **Need:** "A finished plan's merged/apply artifact still shows an empty synthetic wrapper" — child docs and task summaries existed, but the zero-turn `deadreckon:orchestrate-apply` run had templated docs and merge/apply copy rules skipped them, masking the plan story (the `4ca07d2a` pattern).
- **Success:** Completed plans get consolidated `PLAN-NARRATIVE.md`, `PLAN-AS-BUILT.md`, `PLAN-DECISIONS.md` + child index; merged library and apply/export artifacts carry them; wrapper runs say they are wrappers and cross-link; provider-backed consolidation validates citations (no invented paths, no uncited omissions, no secrets) with a deterministic fallback when the provider is missing/over budget/fails validation. Stop: plan id, merged result id, and synthetic apply id all resolve to the same docs.
- **Non-goals:** web publishing/deployment of docs; editing child docs in place; re-running child agents to improve docs; replacing run-level `RUN-*` docs; a plan-doc daemon; cloud storage/collaboration; bulk historical migration (a manual refresh suffices); making provider docs authoritative over source evidence.

### 10. tamper-evident-gate (2026-05-28-1556) — "Tamper-evident"
- **Need:** The headline anti-self-attestation gate "honestly signs a hollow pass: an agent can delete `tests/auth_test.rs`, or append `|| true` to a shell check, and the gate signs because the checks really do pass. The signature is real; the thing it vouches for is not." Called "the only credible attack on the headline feature."
- **Success:** Refuse (no marker, non-terminal failure, corrective loop continues) when the acceptance spec was edited this run or a suppression pattern (`|| true`, `; true`, `--no-verify`, `--exit-zero`) hits; sign-with-caveat when a check-covered file was modified; clean runs sign as today. Per-check verdicts + "tests modified this run: yes/no" on status, exit card, `--why-failed`; honest subscription spend (no `~$0.000000`). P1 must reproduce the hollow pass RED first; forged tamper files fail marker-signature validation.
- **Non-goals (explicit V1 candidates):** causal proof that a covered-file edit caused a pass; language-aware test detection beyond Rust heuristics; a separate signed tamper/audit log; fleet/plan-level aggregate tamper reporting; sandboxing the checks' own filesystem writes. Posture: tamper-*evidence* (heuristic, surfaced), not tamper-proof.

### 11. campaign (2026-05-28-1841) — "Campaign"
- **Need:** "Let one task spawn N orchestrators" — the existing `fork`→`merge` pattern lifted exactly one level, so a root goal can decompose into 2–6 independent sub-orchestrators composed into one promoted run, without nesting "quietly eroding the §35 tamper-evident gate."
- **Success:** `campaign <goal> --n <2..=6>` previews then launches; hard depth cap of 2 (depth-2 invocation refused, RED-first); cycle guard; tree-wide spend ceiling; gate-verdict roll-up — "clean only if every leaf run signed clean; any refused leaf fails the campaign" (the "no-laundering invariant is sacred"); `attach`/`kill`/`--why-failed` work for campaigns.
- **Non-goals (V1):** depth >2 / arbitrary recursion; cross-sub dependency edges and cross-level merge-repair; recursive live attach with a hierarchical event tree; planner-chosen per-sub breadth and provider roles; tree-budget strategies beyond even split; sharing campaign records across machines.

### 12. effortless (2026-05-28-2032) — "Effortless"
- **Need:** "The engine is powerful but the *first ten seconds*, the *return after walking away*, and the *vocabulary* still ask too much." Make the friendly path the default everywhere without touching core mechanism.
- **Success:** P1 friction audit codifying friendliness as a tested contract (auto-detect don't ask; preview before state change; refuse with a `try:` line; one-command rollback; one verdict + ONE primary action; lifecycle hints); `deadreckon try` — a zero-arg, keyless smoke run that signs the gate and prints a proof block in ~10s; self-bootstrapping `start` adopting a detected subscription CLI; opt-in notifications; advisory provider-backed goal routing (run vs orchestration vs campaign) with deterministic fallback; "verified run" vocabulary; "5 verbs to live by, ~12 via help-all"; every refusal carries a `try:` line.
- **Non-goals (V1):** themable palettes/extra `NO_COLOR` work; localization; a card template engine; a long-lived notifier daemon/push service; LLM routing beyond the single bounded classification call (multi-turn clarification, learned routing, per-sub provider planning); any change to gate/sandbox/promotion/provider/campaign mechanism. The classifier "is advisory, bounded, and never authoritative... never auto-launches a campaign."

### 13. navigable (2026-05-29-1354) — "Navigable"
- **Need:** "`attach <campaign-id>` is a dead-end plain-text dump (you must retype `attach <sub-plan-id>`)" while plan/run attach were live TUIs; a campaign is a 3-level tree the 2-level event model couldn't show.
- **Success:** A live campaign TUI — header (goal, status, roll-up, tree budget, live spend) + selectable sub-plan cards + feed + footer; Enter drills into the existing plan TUI unchanged, `b` returns; two-deep drill-and-back returns cleanly (the named key risk, P6-tested via a suspend/resume counter/stack); off-TTY/JSON fall back to the plain summary; breadcrumb gains a campaign tier. `make verify` green at every commit.
- **Non-goals (V1):** a fully-flattened 3-level event stream with ancestry tags ("the drill-in model makes it unnecessary now"); campaign narrative projection; a unified single-event-loop nav-stack rewrite of attach; mouse-driven tree expansion, collapsible nodes, graph layouts.

### 14. decompose (2026-05-29-1600) — "Decompose"
- **Need:** "The `deadreckon` binary is one 40,597-line `main.rs`... unnavigable, every change a triple-edit" — and no CLI-output characterization net existed, since tests asserted state, not stdout/stderr.
- **Success:** Behavior-preserving only: "every command's stdout/stderr, exit codes, and side effects stay byte-identical"; characterization net lands first (RED before refactor), then test modules lifted, then `commands/` + `tui/` carved behind a thin `main_inner`; `make verify` green at every commit; public-surface baseline unchanged except one justified P9 re-baseline; same test count/names after each move.
- **Non-goals — unusually explicit "Rejected as needless churn (do NOT do these)" list:** core `pub mod`→private with flat re-exports (breaks deep-path callers, rewrites ~268 baseline lines); encapsulating Chain/Plan/PlanTask fields behind transition methods (~74 call sites, high risk); `#[non_exhaustive]`/accessor insurance; splitting the 45-variant `cli.rs` Command enum; a `CommandHandler` trait; a `pub run()` facade / `deadreckon-cli` crate; `#[source]` on `ProviderError` + sysexits; reorganizing the 176-test `orchestrate.rs`. Also out of scope: any verb/flag/file/field/output-string change.

### 15. composable-seams (2026-05-31-1644) — "Composable"
- **Need:** "`policy`, `model-catalog`, `hooks`, and the `event-sink` are compiled in — change any and you fork the Rust (the monolith trap)." DeadReckon already externalized two (`cli:*` providers, `dr-gate`); generalize into one seam contract, plus close the unbounded-history gap on the direct-API path.
- **Success:** One `SeamCommand` primitive (sandboxed subprocess, JSON stdin→stdout, timeout, per-kind fail policy; no command ⇒ built-in identical); policy fail-closed and only able to narrow the sandbox; catalog fail-open; hooks/event-sink observe-only and non-fatal; deterministic context compaction on the direct-API path that never drops the goal/acceptance spec; `--no-seams` escape hatch. The gate is deliberately NOT a seam ("a swappable trust root is forgeable") — guarded by depth tests that no `[seams]` key can target it.
- **Non-goals (V1):** human-in-the-loop approval seam (deadreckon is "unattended-first"); LLM compaction summaries; persistent bus/WebSocket transport + long-lived worker registry; seam versioning/capability negotiation/published registry; routing built-in telemetry through hooks; catalog capabilities beyond context_window/pricing; a policy seam that can widen the OS sandbox ("deliberately impossible").

### 16. seam-conformance-kit (2026-05-31-1857) — "Conformant"
- **Need:** "The worker contract is still mostly implicit in Rust tests and architecture prose" — a user couldn't build a seam worker without forking deadreckon.
- **Success:** Executable example workers under `examples/seams/` (policy allow/deny, catalog override, hooks JSONL, event sink JSONL); fixtures + sample config exercising all four kinds with no network; `deadreckon seams validate` (or doctor-based) diagnostics saying what passed, what failed open/closed, what to try next; `docs/SEAMS.md` documenting protocol, fail policies, sandbox expectations, `--no-seams`; P7 proves the gate/proof trust root is unreachable through examples or validation; adversarial fixtures cannot read/mutate gate artifacts.
- **Non-goals:** no schema migrations, no worker registry/bus, no pushed branch; the gate remains "local, deterministic, and non-swappable"; prefer examples/validation/docs over new architecture.

### 17. verdict-surface (2026-06-01-1417) — (one verdict, one command, one explanation)
- **Need:** "Terminal outcomes are split across status lines, `try:` footers, lifecycle hints, `--why-failed` renderers, repair commands, JSON `next_actions`, and ad hoc command summaries" — burns down the FRIENDLINESS-AUDIT "One verdict + ONE primary action" failures.
- **Success:** Every failure/completion surface renders exactly one verdict label (completed, verified, failed, blocked, killed, paused, preview, no-op), exactly one recommended command (secondaries structurally subordinate), and one explanation panel (what happened, why this verdict, which evidence supports it); JSON stays backward-compatible/additive with a single `verdict`/`primary_action` shape; `--quiet/--json/--plain/--no-hints` semantics preserved; FRIENDLINESS-AUDIT failures burned down or reclassified.
- **Non-goals:** no durable schema changes, command removals, or broad renames; do not build the full V1 output-layout facade, template engine, localization, rich merge UI, or AST/semantic merge engine (log pressure in V1-CANDIDATES); read-only listings need no decorative cards.

### 18. release-trust (2026-06-01-1523) — "Release Trust"
- **Need:** "Official releases still depend on operator discipline: tag shape is loose, signing can skip with warnings, checksums/provenance are not first-class, npm provenance is token-based, Windows signing is unresolved, and the runbook lacks exact secret wiring."
- **Success:** Lane contract — PRs/branches plan only; RC tags build signed/notarized/checksummed/attested prereleases, never stable channels; stable tags verify tag/version/CHANGELOG, require signing/provenance, publish GitHub/Homebrew/npm. Official releases produce archives, `SHA256SUMS`, `release-manifest.json`, SBOM, attestations, npm provenance, formula checksums, verification commands. macOS signing mandatory; "never silently publish unsigned stable Windows binaries." `docs/RELEASE.md` gets a secret-free Apple Developer ID checklist. Stop: "official stable releases cannot publish unsigned or unattested artifacts."
- **Non-goals:** no runtime-state schema changes; no CLI redesign; no real publish/tag push by the agent; forks/PRs must stay usable without secrets; npm trusted-publishing operator step may remain documented rather than done.

### 19. release-trust-closure (2026-06-04-1951) — "Release Trust Closure"
- **Need:** Three loose ends Release Trust left open: "`release-verify` is narrowed to fmt+build because the workspace test suite only runs on the author's macOS (hardcoded `/Users/gdc` paths..., BSD `script` PTY...); the Windows target builds but is unsigned and never run; and the `gdc`→`gregce` re-home stopped at the gate and metadata."
- **Success:** Portable suite (nothing depends on `/Users/gdc` or BSD `script`; guard test forbids new hardcoded `/Users/`); new `ci.yml` running fmt/clippy/`cargo test --workspace` on Linux gating releases ("No release may ship on a suite that never ran"); `windows-latest` job proves `--version` and `doctor` exit 0, failing closed; stable Windows blocked without Authenticode secrets; re-home finished in `providers.rs`, `update_cache.rs`, `dist-workspace.toml` tap.
- **Non-goals:** full Windows feature parity (sandbox backends, signals) — document, don't implement; a macOS CI matrix leg (V1 candidate); real Authenticode signing or real publishing; npm/Homebrew publish-behavior changes (parent rider owns those); any schema change.

### 20. uniform-surface (2026-06-05-0009) — "Uniform Surface"
- **Need:** "The same thing renders ~four ways (two divergent `Tone` enums, per-call-site alignment, five 'next step' markers), an alignment bug short-pads colored columns, `--no-hints` is silently ignored on some surfaces, and number menus break past nine choices."
- **Success:** One `Tone` enum with derived ANSI and ratatui tables; one `display_width()` (strip ANSI, then unicode-width) behind every pad/truncate site (the `{:<N}`-on-ANSI bug gone, guard-tested); shared `kv_block` and `columns` primitives; one next-step marker; hardened prompts (multi-digit entry, Esc cancels, out-of-range feedback, validating `ask_number` that re-prompts); `--no-hints`/`DEADRECKON_HINTS=0` respected on status/campaign/inspection/doc/chain. Byte-exact render tests are the contract.
- **Non-goals:** the attach TUI chrome (deliberately split into its own sibling goal `2026-06-05-0010`); adopting comfy-table/tabled or any external prompt/styling crate (console/dialoguer/inquire/indicatif Tier-3 blocked); anstyle-wincon legacy Windows color (V1); an editable multi-char input field; any schema change. Deferred: comfy-table adoption, anstyle-wincon path.

### 21. attach-tui-uniformity (2026-06-05-0010) — "Attach TUI Uniformity"
- **Need:** "Each surface re-implements its own key dispatch, selection glyph, footer, scroll readout, and confirm behavior, so the controls change with what you attached to: paging keys work in run-attach but not plan/campaign, the highlight is `*` here and `>` there, destructive Apply/Abandon fire with no confirmation, and chain step glyphs have no ASCII fallback."
- **Success:** Principle "uniform chrome, mode-specific content": one key dispatcher with per-mode hook, one glyph, one footer builder, one scroll indicator, confirm-before-destructive (Apply/Abandon need a confirm keystroke; "a single mistyped key cannot fire them"), uniform exit/return, friendly empty states (no internal filenames), Windows ASCII glyph fallbacks; PgUp/PgDn/Home/End/g/G parity across run/plan/campaign/chain asserted by goldens.
- **Non-goals:** non-TUI rendering and one-shot prompts (sibling slice 0009); new attach target kinds or content-panel data changes; live prompts inside a ratatui frame or an editable text widget (V1); tui-input/tui-textarea/throbber crates blocked ("no call site today"); any schema change.

## PART 2 — FOUNDATIONAL GOALS: the original unmet needs (in detail)

### 2026-05-10-1400 build ("Build V0 of deadreckon")
This is the origin document. The whole harness was designed against the top 10 unmet needs from `/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md` (25 needs total; top 10 = V0 scope), with the explicit verification rule that "each of the 10 must-have needs maps to ≥ 1 module or command."

**Product framing (rider, "decided — do not redesign"):**
- "A Rust CLI agent harness whose default flow is **unattended long-running coding tasks**. The user types one goal, hits enter, and the harness drives the task across hours of model time — sandboxed, crash-resumable, spend-capped, with full provenance."
- "What it isn't: Not an editor, not a chat app, not an MCP framework, not a CI runner, not a kitchen-sink agent IDE."
- **Target user:** "Solo developers and ≤ 10-person teams currently paying $200+/month per seat across Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, opencode, and still doing manual bookkeeping for spend, undo, and multi-agent coordination."
- BYOK posture: multi-provider from day one; "the user supplies keys; the harness never bills usage."
- The name: dead reckoning = "navigation by integrating known motion from a fixed starting point — no GPS, no external check... durable state at every turn, no live human in the loop, no live model attestation, reconstructable position after any crash."

**The 10 original must-have unmet needs (rider, verbatim list):**
1. **Live Context & Spend Meter** — durable per-turn `spend.jsonl` telemetry, surfaced in TUI.
2. **Multi-Agent Worktree Coordination** — scopes + lock primitives so N agents run in parallel without conflict.
3. **Infinite Undo for Agent Edits** — per-turn `snapshots/turn-<N>/`; `deadreckon undo` to any prior turn.
4. **Prompt-to-Code Provenance Audit Trail** — `provenance.jsonl`: every file change carries `{prompt_id, model, tool_call_id, timestamp, session_id, files}`.
5. **Cross-Tool State Sharing (read-only import)** — `import claude-code|codex|cursor` reading those tools' histories; no live bridging in V0.
6. **Agent Observability** — `traces.jsonl` per run (LLM calls, tool calls, retries, latency), exportable.
7. **Disposable Sandboxes** — platform-native per run by default (`sandbox-exec` macOS / `bwrap` Linux), Docker opt-in.
8. **Billing Guardrails** — `--max-spend`; mid-run pause at cap; resume requires explicit user OK.
9. **Provider Routing / BYOK** — multi-provider with fallback chain in `config.toml`.
10. **Workspace Inventory & Run Queue** — `list/attach/kill/resume` over runstate.

**Success/acceptance:** clean `cargo build --release/test/clippy -D warnings/fmt`; smoke run completes in sandbox with provenance + spend + snapshots; undo/list/attach/kill/resume work; need-to-module grep check; DESIGN.md and demo.cast exist. Architecture adopted from the Printing Press AS-BUILT pattern: two-layer split, on-disk phase machine, locks with heartbeats + PID liveness, atomic promotion to `library/`, **anti-self-attestation gates** ("the agent cannot self-mark a gate"), sub-agent forking, bounded fix loops with rollback. User-friendliness was a V0 requirement with eight commitments (one-command first run, fix-hint errors, spend confirmation, actionable doctor, README quickstart, TUI feedback, sane defaults, time-to-first-output ≤ 5s) that "override engineering-elegance preferences."

**Non-goals — "Out of scope (forever — invariants)":** hosted billing/metering (BYOK invariant); phone-home telemetry/analytics SDKs (local-first invariant); GPL/AGPL in core deps; authoring an MCP server framework (consume, don't author); desktop GUI (TUI + CLI only). V2+ deferred: skills marketplace; cloud telemetry export to user-owned sinks only.

### 2026-05-11-1400 primary-flow ("Complete deadreckon's primary agentic loop. Build something REAL.")
- **Need:** Honesty gap after V0 scaffolding: "`deadreckon run` is a hardcoded shell-script fallback — no LLM, no tool loop." The need was a *real* provider-driven turn→tool-call→sandboxed-exec→result loop, plus **CLI sub-agent providers** (`cli:claude-code`, `cli:codex`) for subscription-BYOK — the genesis of the harness-around-harnesses idea. "All artifacts derive from real provider activity."
- **Success:** three-tier verification — Tier A (keyless mock HTTP provider: ≥3 turns/traces/spend lines, ≥2 tool-driven provenance lines; kill cancels within 2s; resume preserves history), Tier B (code shape: no `coding_turn_script|hardcoded_smoke` greps; both CLI provider modules present), Tier C (live, gated on `claude`/`codex` presence). Also introduced the separate **`dr-gate` binary** writing `proofs/turn-acceptance.json` validated against `run_id` — the anti-self-attestation gate as a running component. Every `provenance.jsonl` `tool_call_id` must match `traces.jsonl`.
- **Non-goals:** `--smoke` keeps the keyless fallback but labeled; no `git push`; V0 invariants (dependency policy, sandbox defaults, UX commitments) must still pass.

### 2026-05-11-1400 usability ("Close deadreckon's lifecycle gap")
- **Need:** Two ergonomic holes: "(1) completed artifacts stay trapped in `library/<scope>/<run-id>/` with no way to land at a user path; (2) `resume` refuses completed runs, so a finished app can't be extended with a new prompt." This is the original "return after walking away" need that later goals (effortless, production-command-model) kept refining.
- **Success:** `materialize` (copy library to a user dest, refuse non-empty without `--force`, lineage markers) and `extend` (new run seeded from a Completed parent's library, parent summary prepended to history); named tests including `materialize_then_extend_roundtrip`; `list`/`show`/post-run hints wired; explicitly **no new `PipelineState` fields** — lineage lives in files (`parent.json` + synthetic trace entry), the earliest appearance of the "files, not fields" discipline that every later rider repeats.
- **Non-goals:** no schema changes; hints suppressible with `--no-hints`; prior rider invariants hold.

### 2026-05-11-1400 robust ("Harden deadreckon — replace scaffolding with robust implementations")
- **Need:** "The retrospective flagged ten thin areas that are scaffolding rather than finished systems. Deepen each. **No new features** — depth, not breadth." Robust means: "each thin area gets a targeted depth test that exercises real edge cases (mid-turn kill, partial traces, concurrent runs, adversarial prompts)... Happy-path-only tests don't count" — the origin of the depth-tests-first discipline in all later riders.
- **The ten thin areas:** TUI streaming; resume from partial traces; hierarchical cancellation (10-start/10-kill storm test); wall-clock spend for CLI providers (subscription→wall-time mapping); sandbox hardening (adversarial `~/.ssh/` read blocked); exhaustive actionable doctor; import normalization (Claude/Codex JSONL + Cursor SQLite round-trip); **acceptance spec** (`dr-gate` reads `acceptance.yaml` — tests/file-exists/content-match/build-success; "self-attest attempt refused"); multi-run coordination (lock ordering, scope no-bleed); atomic crash-recoverable promotion.
- **Success:** per-area depth tests pass; stress (5 concurrent runs, 10 min, no lock leaks/state bleed); adversarial gates (sandbox-escape prompt fails; forged self-attest marker refused); "V0" nomenclature removed — "the product is just deadreckon at the `alpha` tier."
- **Non-goals:** explicitly out of scope V1 pain points — sub-agent forking CLI, hooks, MCP client, search/embeddings, cost-aware routing.

---

## Cross-cutting observations

- **One throughline:** every recent goal traces back to the original report's quartet — undo, provenance, observability, spend/context — plus the anti-self-attestation gate. Flight-recorder cites the report directly; tamper-evident-gate, campaign roll-up, and seam non-swappability all defend the gate; effortless/guided/start-picker/production-command-model/verdict-surface all attack the same "user must learn too much before the first serious run" need from different layers.
- **Recurring discipline (present in nearly every rider):** depth test first and RED before implement; "files, not fields" (no `PipelineState`/`Plan` schema changes); no `git push`; eleven phases with per-phase conventional commits + CHANGELOG; P11 always updates AS-BUILT/V1-CANDIDATES; "no silent scope expansion — anything beyond the phases goes to V1-CANDIDATES.md."
- **Posture shift visible in the dates:** goals through 2026-05-27 say "Stays `alpha`"; from plan-doc-consolidation (2026-05-28) onward they say "Production-release track," culminating in the release-trust pair and the two 2026-06-05 uniformity slices aimed at 0.1.0 readiness.

Key file paths: goals and riders all under `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/`; the original needs report at `/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md`; deferral ledger at `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`; architecture record at `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md`.

# deadreckon — Architecture + Reliability Assessment

## 1. Crate layout (workspace: 5 crates, `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/Cargo.toml`)

| Crate | Role |
|---|---|
| `crates/deadreckon` | The CLI binary + TUI. `src/main.rs` (13,718 lines — by far the largest file), `src/cli.rs` (clap definitions), `src/commands/*` (one module per command family: run, start, plan, campaign, chain, lifecycle, attach, learning, import, doctor, providers, acceptance...), `src/tui/*` (ratatui attach UI), `src/cards/*`, `src/verdict_surface.rs` (structured "verdict" output blocks), `src/bin/dr-gate.rs` (a separate gate-checker binary). |
| `crates/deadreckon-core` | Durable state engine: `state.rs` (PipelineState, atomic JSON writes), `paths.rs` (`~/.deadreckon` layout), `lock.rs` (fs2 file locks + pid heartbeats), `cancel.rs` (cancel marker files), `plan.rs`/`campaign.rs`/`chain.rs` (multi-run orchestration state), `gate.rs` (tamper-evident acceptance gate), `artifacts.rs` (spend/trace/provenance JSONL), `flight.rs` (flight-recorder data model), `learning.rs` (self-improvement loop), `git.rs`, `promotion.rs`, `events.rs`. |
| `crates/deadreckon-runtime` | The agentic engine: `turn_loop.rs` (3,342 lines — the bounded mutation loop), `flight.rs` (ProviderFlightRecorder that tails CLI-provider session logs), `seam.rs` (governance hook commands), `compaction.rs` (history compaction for direct-API providers), `polish.rs` (doc generation). |
| `crates/deadreckon-providers` | Provider seam: `router.rs` (fallback-chain router), `http.rs` (Anthropic/OpenAI/OpenAI-compatible HTTP adapter), `cli_claude_code.rs`, `cli_codex.rs`, `cli_generic.rs` (descriptor-driven generic CLI providers), `registry/mod.rs` + `descriptors/*.toml` (builtin: anthropic, openai, openai-compatible, smoke, cli:claude-code, cli:codex, cli:gemini, cli:opencode, cli:copilot, cli:pi), `smoke.rs` (deterministic scripted provider for tests). |
| `crates/deadreckon-sandbox` | Sandbox backends (`backend.rs`, `policy.rs`, `spec.rs`), `process.rs` (spawn + SIGTERM→2s→SIGKILL cancellation), `doctor.rs`. |

Architecture model (per `docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md`): the binary owns deterministic state/paths; providers are subprocess or HTTP "turn" executors; everything durable is files under `$DEADRECKON_HOME`.

## 2. CLI command surface (`crates/deadreckon/src/cli.rs:534-2487`, clap derive)

Top-level `Commands` enum (cli.rs:549), grouped by `next_help_heading`:

- **Setup**: `init` (alias `setup`; `--provider --api-key --base-url --max-spend --sandbox auto --no-confirm --no-completion`), `config get/set/provider/remove-provider/model/validate` (alias `settings`), `help-all` (alias `commands`), `completion`
- **Done criteria**: `def-done` (plain-English criteria; `--provider --model --overwrite --spec --against`), hidden `acceptance` (init/draft/refine/explain/check, presets)
- **Run lifecycle**: `try` (keyless smoke proof), `start` (goal or `@file`; `--mode`, `--provider`, `--n 2..6`, `--planner-provider`, `--coder-provider`, `--reviewer-provider`, `--preview`, `--yes`, `--no-seams`, `--fresh`, `--worktree`, `--plain`, `--json`), `run` (the workhorse: `--fresh --worktree --from --in-place --base --branch --allow-dirty --init-git --yes --preview --no-seams --plain --prevent-sleep --quiet --max-spend --max-wall-seconds --sandbox --provider --model --doc-provider --acceptance --skill --smoke --i-know-its-a-lot --no-confirm --no-hints --no-docs --doc-skill`), `resume` (`--from-turn`, `--max-wall-seconds`), `extend`, `kill` (`--force`), `undo`, `rewind`
- **Multi-run**: `orchestrate` (full-plan/review subcommands; per-child caps, `--no-merge-repair`), `campaign` (N sub-orchestrators; planner/child provider routes, repair flags), `plan`, `fork`, `merge`, `chain` (sequenced goals with hooks)
- **Inspection**: `list`, `show`, `status`, `history`, `attach` (TUI), `report`, `grep`, `index`, `doc`, `seams`, `detect`, `providers`, `doctor`
- **Finishing**: `finish`, `materialize`, `apply`, `abandon`, `cleanup`, `library`
- **Learning/self-improve**: `learn propose/export/import-bundle`, `improve self <proposal-id> --preview/--yes/--pr-dry-run/self-run`, `import` (cross-tool session import, sqlite3-based)
- **Maintenance**: `update` (axoupdater self-update, feature-gated)

Sub-enums at cli.rs:1750 (`OrchestrateCommand`), 1765 (`CampaignCommand`), 1912/1935/2007/2029/2152/2192/2226/2244/2274 (history/learn/improve/acceptance/config/seams/providers/completion/library).

## 3. Provider integration & failure handling

**Spawning.** CLI providers run as one subprocess per turn: `cli_common.rs:55-178` (`run_cli_with_options`) either delegates to the sandbox (`deadreckon-sandbox/src/process.rs`) or spawns directly with piped stdout/stderr, writes a pid file under `<run_root>/child-pids/provider-turn-N.pid`, and `tokio::select!`s the wait against a `CancellationToken`. Claude Code is invoked as `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions -p <prompt>` (`cli_claude_code.rs:43-47`). Generic providers render argv from TOML descriptor templates (`cli_generic.rs:render_args`).

**Routing/fallback.** `router.rs:232-245`: routes are tried in order (default → fallback list, or built-in default chain at router.rs:276-282); a route without a credential is skipped; a failed route falls through to the next; all-failed yields `ProviderError::NoRoute` with joined failure strings. **One attempt per route — no per-route retry, no backoff.**

**Failure detection.** Exit-code based: `ensure_success` (cli_common.rs:295-306) treats nonzero exit as `ProviderError::Cli` containing stdout+stderr. HTTP providers check status (`http.rs:141-146`). A provider error in the turn loop is **fatal to the run**: `turn_loop.rs:249-254` returns `Err(provider_error(...))` — no retry, no state transition to Failed inside the loop (see weak points).

**Timeouts.** There is **no per-turn timeout anywhere**. `run_cli` has no deadline; `reqwest::Client::new()` at http.rs:39 has no timeout configured. The only time controls are: `--max-spend` (checked after each turn, turn_loop.rs:327-339) and `--max-wall-seconds` (checked after each turn and **only for subscription-billed turns**, turn_loop.rs:340-353). A hung provider process/HTTP call blocks forever unless the user runs `kill` (cancel marker) from another terminal.

**Retries.** A retryability taxonomy exists (`providers/src/error.rs:31-47`, `core/src/error.rs:31-53`, `sandbox/src/backend.rs:22-36` — `is_retryable()`/`is_fatal()` with comments saying "the watchdog should escalate") but **no caller anywhere invokes it and no watchdog exists**. It is documented-but-unimplemented machinery.

**Crash recovery / resume.** Genuinely well designed:
- `resume` (main.rs:8890-9019) reacquires the scope lock, clears failure/pause/cancel state, and re-enters the turn loop with `max_turns: 12`.
- History reconstruction (`turn_loop.rs:1318-1404` + `docs/RESUME-SEMANTICS.md`): `traces.jsonl` is read line-by-line, partial trailing JSON entries are discarded (and the file rewritten sanitized), and tool-result history is rebuilt from complete `tool.*` traces; `--from-turn N` truncates history, `traces.jsonl`, `spend.jsonl`, and snapshot dirs past N (turn_loop.rs:1406-1457).
- Kill path: `kill` writes a `cancel.marker` (core/cancel.rs) which a 50ms polling task inside the run process observes (turn_loop.rs:843-861); the sandbox sends SIGTERM, waits 2s, SIGKILLs (process.rs:56-67); plan/campaign kill cascades over coordinator/children pids (main.rs:8638+), with discovery fallbacks via launch-dir `run-id` files and scope scans.
- Locks: fs2 exclusive lock + JSON heartbeat (pid, phase, updated_at); successors reclaim if pid dead or heartbeat older than 30 min (`lock.rs:13,127-139,196-202`).

**Child-orchestrator failure detection** (plan/orchestrate, plan.rs:2543-2632): the coordinator spawns `current_exe() run ...` per task, busy-polls `try_wait()` at 100ms, and discovers the child's run id **by parsing the child's human-readable stdout** (`parse_started_run_id`) — a fragile output-format coupling. Nonzero child exit becomes an error embedding captured output.

## 4. State persistence

Everything lives under `$DEADRECKON_HOME` (env override) — `paths.rs:34-194`: `runstate/<scope>/runs/<run_id>/state.json`, `runstate/<scope>/current/<task_key>.json` (pointer), `locks/`, `plans/<id>/{plan.json,coordinator.json,messages.jsonl,plan-events.jsonl,worker-specs,summaries,merge-*}`, `chains/`, `library/` (promoted artifacts), `learning/`.

Per-run root also holds `history.json`, `traces.jsonl`, `spend.jsonl`, `events.jsonl`, `sandbox.toml`, `snapshots/turn-N/`, `gate/nonce`, `cancel.marker`, `child-pids/`, `turns/turn-N/provider.out`.

**Write discipline:**
- `state.json` and the current pointer: atomic — `NamedTempFile` in the same dir, `sync_all`, then rename (`state.rs:445-465`). Good.
- JSONL appends: `append_json_line` opens with `append`, writes one line, `sync_all` (state.rs:467-482). Torn trailing lines are tolerated/healed at resume (turn-loop reconstruction discards/rewrites incomplete tail lines).
- State is saved at every turn boundary and on every status transition ("harness owns the bounded mutation loop", turn_loop.rs:118-119); worktree mode additionally commits the working tree per turn (`commit_worktree_turn`, turn_loop.rs:1691-1711).
- **Not atomic**: `history.json` is a plain `std::fs::write` (`turn_loop.rs:1302-1312`) — a crash mid-write leaves invalid JSON, and `load_or_reconstruct_history` (1318-1328) hard-fails on it instead of falling back to trace reconstruction (the fallback only triggers when the file is *missing*). Likewise `sandbox.toml` (1050), lock-state writes (`lock.rs:277-283`, in-place truncate+rewrite), and various `let _ = fs::write(...)` pointer files.

**On interruption:** state.json on disk remains `Executing` with a dead pid (no process reconciles status at crash); the design intentionally relies on pid-liveness checks in `lock_status` and stale-lock reclaim, plus `resume`'s replay-from-last-complete-tool-boundary semantics. There is a test pinning this (`state.rs:528-560`).

## 5. Test coverage shape

~**1,410** `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` functions:

- `deadreckon/tests` (integration): 801 — orchestrate (7,081 lines), chain (4,315), lifecycle, agentic_loop, codebase, campaign, self_documenting, coherence, friendliness/cards (output-contract tests), npm_wrapper, release_plan, public_surface, hygiene_config, smoke_invariant.
- `deadreckon/src` (unit, in-binary): 361 — including `tui_tests.rs` (5,342 lines: attach-loop budget/refresh/coalescing/quit semantics, ratatui `TestBackend` render assertions), navigation, acceptance render/integrity, campaign spawn argv pinning.
- core: 103 + 18; runtime: 68 (turn_loop has substantial async tests: seam timeouts fail-closed, resume re-resolves seams, resume-deterministic compaction, cancellation); providers: 16 + 34 (`mock_server.rs` spins an axum mock for HTTP providers; `cli_providers.rs` uses fake binaries); sandbox: 9.

**Well covered:** turn-loop semantics, resume/replay, locks, kill cascades, CLI output contracts ("friendliness"/verdict surfaces), orchestrate/campaign happy and failure paths with the smoke provider, TUI loop model and rendering via TestBackend.

**Thin/untested:**
- Real provider seams: everything runs against `smoke`, fake CLI scripts, or the axum mock; no tests for hung subprocesses, partial stdout, non-UTF8 output, or HTTP timeout behavior (there is no timeout to test).
- The retry/watchdog taxonomy (unused code, untested by definition).
- TUI raw-mode teardown on panic; sandbox backends beyond the basics (sandbox crate has only 9 tests).
- The 126-error clippy debt (below) shows `make verify` (fmt+clippy+tests) is not currently green.

## 6. Reliability weak points (specific)

**Hardcoded developer-machine paths compiled into the binary (highest severity for a distributed tool):**
- `deadreckon-core/src/paths.rs:6-7` — `DEFAULT_DEADRECKON_HOME: &str = "/Users/gdc/.deadreckon"` and `SOURCE_ROOT: &str = "/Users/gdc/deadreckon"`. `DeadreckonPaths::discover()` (paths.rs:15-20) falls back to this literal when `DEADRECKON_HOME` is unset — i.e., on any other machine the tool writes to a non-existent user's home path. `SOURCE_ROOT` is also used to locate skills at run creation (`state.rs:198`) and chain hooks (`commands/chain/mod.rs:1639`).
- `deadreckon-providers/src/config.rs:10` — `DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH = "/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml"`.
- `deadreckon-providers/src/cli_common.rs:63` — cwd fallback is literally `PathBuf::from("/Users/gdc/deadreckon")`.
- `deadreckon-runtime/src/turn_loop.rs:1734` — error-context path hardcoded to `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/target`.

**Lint debt / panic paths despite "no-unwrap" policy:** the workspace denies `unwrap_used`/`expect_used`, but `cargo clippy -p deadreckon` currently fails with **126 errors** (verified in this session), including ~106 non-test `.expect("... verdict surface must be valid")` panic sites on user-facing render paths — e.g. `tui/render.rs:356`, `main.rs:8920` (resume no-op card), `commands/start.rs:2336,2868`, `commands/plan.rs:404,811,1496,1831`, `commands/completion.rs:122`. These can panic inside the raw-mode TUI; I found no panic hook that restores the terminal.

**Potential panic on HTTP error path:** `http.rs:279-286` `trim_for_error` slices `&body[..240]` by byte offset — panics if byte 240 is not a UTF-8 char boundary (error bodies can contain multibyte text). This fires precisely while reporting a provider HTTP failure.

**No timeouts:**
- `http.rs:39` — `reqwest::Client::new()` with no `.timeout(...)`; a stalled API connection hangs the turn loop indefinitely (cancellation token is the only escape, and the in-process run has `cancellation_token: None` at main.rs:8993).
- `cli_common.rs:55-178` — no deadline on CLI provider subprocesses; `--max-wall-seconds` is only checked *between* turns and only when `response.spend.subscription` is true (turn_loop.rs:340-343), so API-billed runs have no wall cap at all and a single hung turn is uncapped for everyone.

**Retry machinery is dead code:** `is_retryable()`/`is_fatal()` defined in three crates (providers/error.rs:31-47; core/error.rs:31-53; sandbox/backend.rs:22-36) with comments referencing a watchdog that does not exist; zero call sites. Provider failures are one-shot per route, then the run errors out.

**Run left in `Executing` on provider error:** `turn_loop.rs:249-254` returns `Err` without saving a Failed status or failure_reason; in `resume_command` (main.rs:9012) the `?` also skips `lock.release()` (Drop unlocks the fd but leaves the lock file, relying on pid-staleness for reclaim) and skips `state.child_pids.clear()`/save. `deadreckon list` will show a dead run as Executing until something probes pid liveness.

**Non-atomic, hard-failing history file:** `save_history` (turn_loop.rs:1302-1312) plain-writes `history.json`; `load_or_reconstruct_history` (1318-1328) only falls back to trace reconstruction when the file is *absent*, so a torn write bricks resume with a JSON parse error. Also `--from-turn` truncates history by entry count (`history.truncate(from_turn as usize)`, line 1330) while history accrues multiple entries per turn (refusal lines pushed at 509, 534, 673, 700) — index-vs-turn mismatch can silently replay the wrong context.

**Silent error swallowing (118 `let _ =` sites in non-test code):** notable ones — `commands/campaign.rs:112` (sub-orchestrator result sidecar write swallowed: meta-coordinator may never learn the sub finished), `commands/plan.rs:2613,2645` (`launch/run-id` pointer write swallowed; kill/attach discovery depends on it), `main.rs:8606` (cascaded campaign sub-kill errors ignored), `commands/lifecycle.rs:896,941,991` (kill results ignored during cleanup), `cli_common.rs:151,168` (pid-file removal — benign but means stale pid files).

**Polling/race-prone loops:** cancel-marker watcher polls `.exists()` every 50ms (turn_loop.rs:843-861); plan coordinator busy-polls `child.try_wait()` + `try_recv` at 100ms (plan.rs:2569-2591); attach TUI polls events + reloads state every 250ms tick (attach.rs:360,552); flight recorder polls provider log files every 500ms (runtime/flight.rs:71-75). Child run-id discovery by **scraping child stdout** (plan.rs:2611) races against output buffering and breaks if the "started run" line format changes — there is a mitigation (the `run-id` file + scope scan in kill_plan_command, main.rs:8669-8688) but the primary channel is string-parsing.

**Spend accounting blind spot:** CLI providers report `input_tokens: 0, output_tokens: 0, cost_usd: 0.0, subscription: true` (cli_claude_code.rs:61-67,116-126), so `--max-spend` is a no-op for cli:claude-code/codex/copilot etc.; the only budget there is wall-clock, with the gaps above.

**Lock TOCTOU edge:** `acquire_lock` (lock.rs:111-139) can reclaim a lock whose holder pid is alive but whose heartbeat is >30 min old (`stale || !alive` is OR'd in `lock_is_stale`, lock.rs:196-202) — a long-blocked-but-alive holder can be silently usurped, after which both processes mutate the same scope state.

**Overall:** the durable-state core (atomic state.json, JSONL healing, resume replay, pid-checked locks, kill cascade) is thoughtfully engineered and heavily tested; the soft spots are the unfinished retry/watchdog seam, missing timeouts at every provider boundary, the hardcoded `/Users/gdc/...` constants that make the binary non-portable as-built, the current clippy-red panic-path debt, and child coordination via stdout scraping.

# Findings

## (a) Acknowledged-open gaps and limitations, by source doc

### `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/GAP-ANALYSIS.md` (audit 2026-05-11)
All ten primary-flow findings are marked **Resolved** (provider-driven loop, model-to-tool protocol, CLI sub-agent providers, kill/resume, anti-self-attestation gate, provenance-trace linkage, real demo cast, keyless agentic tests, V0 first-run UX). Remaining acknowledged caveats:
- API keys are not required for Tier A/B verification; keyless paths are the mock provider and `--smoke`.
- `asciinema` is not installed; `demo.cast` is generated from captured output, not a live recording.
- Cross-process attach cannot consume an in-memory Tokio broadcast, so attach replays durable `events.jsonl` at 100 ms cadence (a design workaround, stated as such).
- HTTP provider live pings in `doctor` are gated behind `DEADRECKON_DOCTOR_PING=1`.

### `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md` (the project's explicit deferred backlog)
Grouped highlights of acknowledged-open items:

## (c) Conceptual model a user must understand (docs/CONCEPTS.md)

- **The loop is the product**: the agent CLI does the coding; deadreckon owns the boundary and decides when "done" actually means done.
- **Done contract in English**: `def-done` compiles a plain-English sentence into executable checks (`cargo_test`, `file_exists`, `content_match`, `build_success`, `shell`) in `acceptance.yaml`. Default when unconfigured: working dir exists and `cargo test` passes (if `Cargo.toml` present).
- **Anti-self-attestation watchdog**: a separate process, `dr-gate`, holds a run-local secret the agent process can't read and signs the acceptance marker; the agent literally cannot forge "done." Check failures mean another turn, not termination.
- **Isolation**: runs default to an isolated `git worktree` on a `dr/...` branch inside a sandbox; the real checkout changes only on `deadreckon apply`.
- **Durable runstate**: every turn writes state, spend, traces, provenance, snapshots — enabling attach from another terminal, kill, resume (from last completed tool boundary), per-turn undo, and audit.
- **Promoted artifact, not transcript**: accepted runs promote atomically to `RUN-NARRATIVE.md`, `RUN-DECISIONS.md`, `RUN-AS-BUILT.md`, `provenance.jsonl`, `manifest.json`.
- **Bring your own agent**: routes `cli:claude-code`, `cli:codex`, `cli:gemini`, `cli:copilot`, `cli:opencode`, `cli:pi`, plus BYOK `anthropic`/`openai`/`openai-compatible`, and keyless `--smoke`; `import` ingests other tools' history read-only.
- **Scaling shapes**: `chain` for ordered multi-step goals (each step has its own signed gate, stops at first failure); plans/orchestrate for parallel children; campaigns for N orchestrators on one task (depth-capped at 2).
- **The name is the contract**: dead reckoning — navigate by evidence, don't trust the final answer.

1	GOAL: Make DeadReckon feel obvious, welcoming, and hard to misuse by landing a guided front door for running or orchestrating goals plus a sharper product identity. Today the substrate is strong, but the user must still learn too much command topology before the first serious run. This goal makes the answer immediate: DeadReckon is for people who already trust agent CLIs and need unattended, sandboxed, auditable work with a real definition of done. Headline word: **Guided**.
2	
3	**Read first.**
4	
5	- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md` - substrate and CLI surface.
6	- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-05-26-1510-deadreckon-guided-experience-rider.md` - launcher behavior, copy contract, depth tests.
7	- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/design/USER-FACING-MATRIX.md` - UX deferrals.
8	- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/README.md` and `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/HOWTO.md` - current public framing and first-run path.
9	- Prior setup, orchestration, coherence, event bus, and self-improvement riders - invariants hold.
10	
11	**Posture.** Stays `alpha`. No `PipelineState` schema changes. Prefer shared renderers and ephemeral launch decisions over durable state. Do not weaken safety invariants. No `git push`. Edits stay inside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`. Major product or schema decisions go to `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
12	
13	**Audience contract.**
14	
15	- Primary users: builders, maintainers, founders, and engineering leads who already use agent CLIs for longer, riskier work.
16	- DeadReckon is the harness around those harnesses: it owns isolation, done criteria, lifecycle, logs, evidence, recovery, and promotion.
17	- Not the promise: chat app, cloud IDE, provider replacement, magic autonomous employee, or unsupervised deploy tool.
18	- This framing must appear in top help, README, HOWTO, and setup recovery copy.
19	
20	**Guided front door.**
21	
22	- Add `deadreckon start "<goal>"` as the recommended new-user path. It resolves provider setup, done criteria, source mode, and run-vs-orchestrate choice, then starts or previews the selected flow.
23	- Existing `run` and `orchestrate` remain canonical power-user commands.
24	- `start` defaults to no provider flags: use configured defaults, detect installed providers only when defaults are missing, and print exact `try:` lines when setup is incomplete.
25	- `start --mode auto|run|review|full-plan`, `--preview`, `--yes`, `--plain`, `--quiet`, and `--json` follow existing output contracts.
26	- Auto mode names the selected path, reason, and override flag.
27	
28	**Friendliness as a verifiable contract.**
29	
30	- One command from an ordinary repo must either start a run/plan or end with concrete `try:` lines.
31	- Missing provider, no done criteria, non-git directory, dirty repo, sandbox limits, or high budget must lead to guided recovery.
32	- Every start/run/orchestrate preview says who works, where it runs, how done is checked, how to watch/stop it, and what finishes it.
33	- JSON/plain/quiet behavior stays coherent and covered.
34	
35	**Phases.** Eleven (P1-P11) in the rider. Each: depth test first -> implement -> focused verification green -> conventional local commit -> CHANGELOG. P11 updates AS-BUILT, README, HOWTO, and V1-CANDIDATES.
36	
37	**Verification.**
38	
39	- Focused tests only by default: command parsing, help/catalog snapshots, preflight builders, start auto-resolution, shared output, JSON/plain/quiet, and docs copy assertions.
40	- Smokes: `deadreckon start --preview "goal"`, missing-provider recovery, non-git recovery, and `start --mode review --preview` produce actionable output without provider-specific flags.
41	- Do not run `make verify`, release builds, stress tests, broad smoke suites, or full-workspace tests by default while executing this goal unless the human explicitly asks.
42	
43	**Stop when** focused verification passes, docs make the audience and first path obvious, the guided launcher works in preview and recovery cases, AS-BUILT and CHANGELOG record alpha limits, and the work is committed locally.
44

2	
3	## Guided first-use follow-ups
4

6	- Richer multi-piece goal classification: the production path has one bounded provider-backed goal-shape recommendation with deterministic fallback. V1 can add deeper LLM-backed multi-piece classification/decomposition once evidence limits, cost policy, explainability, and fixtures are explicit.
7	- Personalized onboarding: adapt setup copy and examples to a user's observed provider/source/done-contract patterns without adding telemetry or background profiling by default.
8	- Provider-specific setup wizards: offer richer guided configuration for individual CLIs or APIs once their install/auth flows are stable enough to document without making `start` brand-specific.

10	- Production command release policy: after the default model proves itself, decide whether advanced verbs stay flat forever, move under namespaces, gain stronger aliases, or get deprecation windows. The production-release command model keeps every command callable and discoverable through `help-all`.

12	## Effortless follow-ups

Today `attach` is strong for debugging, but multi-agent work can feel like machinery. Land a cited narrative plus visual architecture map that explains current work, system evolution, blockers, risks, and next steps while keeping raw activity one key away. Headline word: **Narrated**.
2	
3	**Read first.**
4	
5	- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md`.
6	- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-05-26-1546-deadreckon-narrative-attach-rider.md` - full contract.

11	**Posture.** Stays `alpha`. No `PipelineState` schema changes. Narrative and maps are projections over events, flight, traces, docs, and plan state, not sources of truth. Do not write prose into `flight-events.jsonl`, provider activity, or `plan-events.jsonl`. No `git push`. Edits stay inside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`. V1 decisions go to `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
12	
13	**User contract.**
14	
15	- `deadreckon attach <id> --view narrative` opens a calmer operator view for a run, plan, or plan child.
16	- The main pane shows prose; the side pane shows an evidence-backed architecture, agent, file, or evidence map when width allows.
17	- `--view activity` preserves raw activity; `--view split` may show narrative plus raw evidence or map. Keys: `n` toggles narrative/activity, `v` cycles visuals, `r` refreshes.
18	- Off-TTY/plain attach prints the latest snapshot with citations and staleness. JSON output is structured.
19	- Staleness is explicit: if the summarizer is unavailable, behind, over budget, or refused for privacy, the run continues and the UI shows deterministic facts.
20	
21	**Narrative agent.**
22	
23	- Add a bounded summarizer sidecar that builds evidence windows, redacts sensitive material, then asks a provider for structured claims only when cadence and budget allow.
24	- Cadence is event-driven, not constant streaming: refresh on meaningful deltas, blockers, test pass/fail, agent handoff, plan child completion, quiet threshold, or manual `r`.
25	- Every claim cites immutable evidence: run event, trace id, flight event, checkpoint, file path, plan event, task id, or child run id.
26	- The architecture map is built deterministically from changed files, symbols, tasks, deps, and citations; LLMs may label nodes but not invent them.
27	
28	**Visual posture.**
29	
30	- Reuse existing `ratatui`, `crossterm`, `pulldown-cmark`, `tokio`, `ui.rs`, and `PlanEventBus`.
31	- Use semantic color, focused borders, compact badges, connectors, progress rails, and tasteful status flourishes from the existing palette.
32	- Keep ASCII fallback, `NO_COLOR`, and non-color labels. Avoid graph crates unless the rider depth tests prove they are needed.
33	
34	**Phases.** Eleven (P1-P11) in the rider. Each: depth test first -> implement -> focused verification green -> conventional local commit -> CHANGELOG. P11 updates AS-BUILT, docs, and V1-CANDIDATES with limits.

39	- Smokes: fake CLI provider with flight events; fake two-child plan; completed run with `RUN-NARRATIVE.md`; summarizer failure. Each must show a useful narrative.

 `./docs/RESUME-SEMANTICS.md`

```text
1	# Resume Semantics
2	
3	deadreckon resumes from durable runstate, not model memory.
4	
5	Ordering:
6	
7	1. Load `state.json`.
8	2. Read `traces.jsonl` line by line and keep only complete JSON entries.
9	3. Reconstruct tool-result history from complete `tool.*` trace entries when `history.json` is missing or `--from-turn` is supplied.
10	4. If `--from-turn N` is supplied, truncate history to turn `N`, set `state.turn = N`, and continue with turn `N + 1`.
11	5. Ignore any partial trailing trace entry. The next turn replays from the last complete tool boundary.
12	
13	This makes a kill between provider response and tool dispatch recoverable: the partial trace is treated as advisory residue, never as completed work.
14
```
</details></tool-use>

15	- Run attach awaits `refresh_run_narrative_with_provider*` inside `attach_tui_with_parent`; manual `r` and automatic narrative refreshes can block input until `claude`/`codex` exits.
16	- Plan attach does the same through `refresh_plan_narrative_with_provider*`.
17	- Each run tick reloads `state.json`, full `spend.jsonl`, full `traces.jsonl`, full flight/provider activity, acceptance files, and a working-tree inventory.
18	- `collect_attach_live` calls `inventory_files` before filtering `node_modules`/`.git`, so large ignored trees are still walked; Chrome profile `.tmp` trees and build output can dominate a tick.
19	- Narrative rendering can touch projection files during render.
20	- Chain attach rereads full `chain-events.jsonl` each tick.
21	
22	**User contract.**
23	
24	- `q`, Esc, Ctrl-D, `n`, `v`, `j/k`, and `Tab` remain responsive even while a narrative provider refresh or provider-log scan is pending.
25	- Pressing `r` starts or coalesces a refresh, shows an in-flight notice, and never blocks detach.
26	- Automatic event/quiet refreshes are background jobs with at most one in flight per attach target.
27	- Panes may show slightly stale data with age/status labels.
28	- Completed-run attach, run attach, plan attach, child attach, and chain attach share the same responsiveness posture.
29	
30	**Phases.** Eleven (P1-P11) in the rider. Each: depth test first -> implement -> focused verification green -> conventional local commit -> CHANGELOG. P11 updates AS-BUILT, V1-CANDIDATES, and CHANGELOG.
31	
32	**Verification.**
33	
34	- Focused tests: nonblocking narrative refresh, coalescing, cancellation on detach, incremental JSONL readers, inventory pruning, provider-log throttling, render purity, and stale-data labels.
35	- Smokes: live run narrative `r` remains detachable; plan attach with slow child feed remains detachable; large `.tmp/chrome-profile` tree does not freeze live files; chain attach with large event file remains usable.
36	- Do not run `make verify`, stress suites, or broad release checks by default unless the human asks.
37	
38	**Stop when** focused verification passes, manual/automatic refresh work is off the UI loop, expensive collectors are cached/incremental or throttled, AS-BUILT/CHANGELOG document the alpha responsiveness contract, and the work is committed locally.
39
