```text
I have a complete picture. Here is the assessment.

# DeadReckon first-run / setup / usability assessment

## Overall shape

The project has unusually strong *internal* attention to CLI ergonomics — there is a six-clause "friendliness contract" with a full per-command audit (`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/FRIENDLINESS-AUDIT.md`), a `VerdictSurface` system that gives every command one verdict + one Recommended action, a guided `start` front door, `init`, `doctor`, `try`, `completion install`, and footer hints in the TUI. The *design* of the first-run path is genuinely good. The blocking problems are almost all about the gap between "works on gdc's machine" and "works for a new user who installed a release binary."

---

## 1. Showstopper: hardcoded `/Users/gdc/...` paths compiled into the binary

The single biggest first-run failure for any user who is not `gdc`:

- `crates/deadreckon-core/src/paths.rs:6-7` — `pub const DEFAULT_DEADRECKON_HOME: &str = "/Users/gdc/.deadreckon";` and `pub const SOURCE_ROOT: &str = "/Users/gdc/deadreckon";`. `DeadreckonPaths::discover()` (line 15-20) uses `DEADRECKON_HOME` env var or falls back to this literal path. **There is no `$HOME` resolution and no build.rs generating these** (verified: no build.rs exists in any crate). A new user installing via `curl ... install.sh` or Homebrew gets a binary whose config, runstate, library, locks, plans, and learning state all try to live in `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon` — which will fail with permission errors (or worse, silently succeed on a machine that happens to have that path writable) unless they discover and export `DEADRECKON_HOME` first. Nothing in README's "Get started" mentions this requirement.
- `crates/deadreckon-providers/src/config.rs:10` — `DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH: &str = "/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml"` (exported from `lib.rs:20`).
- `crates/deadreckon-providers/src/cli_common.rs:63` — sandboxed CLI runs fall back to `PathBuf::from("/Users/gdc/deadreckon")` as cwd when `current_dir()` fails.
- `crates/deadreckon/src/commands/chain/mod.rs:1638` — chain hook resolution probes `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/hooks/chain` as the final fallback.
- `crates/deadreckon-core/src/learning.rs` (lines 587, 1968, 2269, 2473, 2550) and `crates/deadreckon/src/commands/learning.rs:878` — the self-improvement loop targets the repo at `/Users/gdc/deadreckon` literally.

By contrast, the import paths do it right (`commands/import.rs:372,418` use `$HOME`), proving the rest is an oversight, not a pattern.

## 2. Installation / distribution

Three channels, generally well built:

- **Shell installer** (`README.md:19-23`, `release/install.sh`): `curl -fsSL https://deadreckon.sh/install.sh | sh`. The script verifies SHA256SUMS (warns-and-continues if unavailable — soft-fail), and ends with a genuinely good "next" block: `doctor`, `try`, `start "make a small safe change"`. Friction: it pins `tag="v0.1.0-rc.1"` as the *default* (`install.sh` line 5), so new releases require updating the script or users get the RC forever.
- **cargo-dist** (`dist-workspace.toml`): shell/powershell/homebrew installers, 5 targets, installs to `~/.local/share/deadreckon/bin` — note `install-path` here is correct/portable, unlike the runtime paths above.
- **npm** (`npm/deadreckon/package.json`): standard optionalDependencies-per-platform wrapper with `bin/deadreckon.js` launcher and postinstall. Fine.
- **Security side-finding**: `RELEASE.md` says "This file is `.gitignored` — keep it that way" but **`git ls-files` shows `RELEASE.md`, `Certificates.p12`, `developerID_application.cer`, and the CSR are all tracked in the repo**, and `RELEASE.md:33` contains a real Apple app-specific password (`lbyn-dvnh-xnif-pyjh`, flagged in the file itself as needing rotation). This is committed secret material, not just a usability issue.

## 3. Configuration

- Config lives at `<home>/config.toml`, read in `crates/deadreckon-providers/src/config.rs:12-35`. **Missing config is non-fatal** — `read_config` returns an empty `ProviderConfigFile` on `NotFound`, and provider entries are synthesized from built-in descriptors (`provider_entry_from_descriptor`, lines 66-103) with default models, pricing, binaries, and `api_key_env` names. Providers ship as embedded TOML descriptors (`crates/deadreckon-providers/src/registry/mod.rs:21-49`: anthropic, openai, openai-compatible, smoke, cli:claude-code, cli:codex, cli:gemini, cli:opencode, cli:copilot, cli:pi) with a user override dir at `<home>/providers.d` (`registry/mod.rs:309-321`). So very little *must* be authored by hand.
- `deadreckon init` (`crates/deadreckon/src/commands/init.rs`) auto-detects an installed subscription CLI (`preferred_init_subscription_cli_provider`, line 133), prompts for provider/API key only when needed, writes config, runs a doctor summary, auto-installs shell completion, and prints a verdict with one Recommended next step. Defaults: $10 spend cap, 3600s wall clock, sandbox `auto` (HOWTO.md:290).
- Env-var friction is modest: `DEADRECKON_HOME` (required in practice for non-gdc users, see #1), `OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL`/`OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_MODEL` for the compatible route (`config.rs:70-78`), `DEADRECKON_DOCTOR_PING=1` to enable live pings.

## 4. First-run experience

- **No args** runs `status` (`main.rs:582-587`), not a wall of help — good. There's also a curated `print_top_help` (`main.rs:1872`) with a "Production flow" section, plus `help-all` for the full map.
- **`deadreckon try`** (`main.rs:3051`) is a keyless smoke run in a throwaway dir under `<home>/try` — an excellent zero-credential proof path, surfaced by the installer.
- **`deadreckon doctor`** (`crates/deadreckon/src/commands/doctor.rs`) is thorough: config presence/parseability, per-provider credential or binary checks, sandbox backends with versions, disk space, runstate writability, OS, sleep prevention, and claude/codex subscription binaries — each finding carries a concrete `deadreckon ...` action, aggregated into one verdict with one primary action (tested at `doctor.rs:736-760`).
- **Gap — login state vs binary presence**: `has_credential` for `cli:claude-code` only checks the binary exists (`cli_claude_code.rs:112-114`); doctor's CLI provider check likewise (`doctor.rs:411-436`). A user with `claude` installed but *not logged in* passes init/doctor/preflight, and failure surfaces only at run time as `ProviderError::Cli { "subprocess exited with {code}: {stdout}{stderr}" }` (`cli_common.rs:295-306`) — raw subprocess output mid-run rather than a "claude is not logged in; run `claude login`" refusal up front.
- `start` is the guided front door: TTY prompts for mode/provider/done-criteria/source; non-TTY refusals print `try:` lines (HOWTO.md:37-41; setup refusal machinery in `crates/deadreckon/src/setup.rs`, e.g. `setup_refusal_for_provider_error` at line 360).

## 5. TUI

- Launch is `deadreckon attach <run-id|latest>` (or alias `watch`); the TUI is read-only by design — "The TUI does not start, kill, resume, or undo runs" (HOWTO.md:399).
- Discoverability is footer-driven: a uniform footer builder (`tui/render.rs:277`) and state-aware key hints (`footer_for_state`, `render.rs:2029`) including completion actions, focus, scroll, and detach. Destructive actions (apply/abandon) require a two-step `y` confirm (`commands/attach.rs:950-979`).
- **Gap — no `?` help overlay**: searched the entire TUI (`tui/`, `tui_events.rs`, `commands/attach*.rs`); there is no help overlay or `?` binding. Everything must fit in (and be read from) the footer, which the code itself notes gets truncated on narrow terminals (`render.rs:2043-2046`).
- **Inconsistency — abandon key**: the TUI deliberately moved Abandon to `x` so `b` means "back" (`attach.rs:951-953`, test `back_and_abandon_are_distinct_keys`), but the *CLI* completion prompt still offers `b abandon` (`main.rs:10903`: `"completed action [a apply, b abandon, d docs, s show, q quit]"`), and **HOWTO.md:363 still documents the TUI key as `b abandon`** — stale doc plus a cross-surface keybinding mismatch.

## 6. Other friction points

- **HOWTO.md is written for gdc's machine, not a user's**: literal `/Users/gdc/...` paths throughout (lines 96-107, 143, 152-158, 178, 571-575), `make alias-zsh` editing `/Users/gdc/.zshrc` (Makefile:89), import default roots shown as `/Users/gdc/.claude/projects/`. README points new users at HOWTO as "Practical usage: setup" (README.md:73), so this is the documented setup surface.
- **README never mentions `init` or `doctor`** in "Get started" — it jumps straight to `start`. The installer's printed next-steps (`doctor`, `try`, `start`) are actually the better onboarding, and `start` does catch missing setup, so this mostly works — but README and HOWTO disagree on the canonical first command (`start` vs `init`+`doctor`).
- **Done-criteria authoring**: the default gate when no acceptance spec exists is minimal (dir exists + `cargo test` if `Cargo.toml` present, HOWTO.md:505), and `def-done` in English requires a working provider; short packs (`build`, `node`, `playwright`...) are the no-provider fallback (HOWTO.md:517-527). Runs "prompt before starting when no project acceptance file exists" (HOWTO.md:529) — a sensible nudge, but a new user's very first `start` stacks provider selection + done-criteria + source-mode decisions.
- **Goal/rider docs are not a user requirement** — goals are plain CLI strings or `--goal-file` (with `~` expansion and empty-goal validation, `main.rs:493-557`); the "rider" referenced in RELEASE.md is an internal dev-workflow artifact.
- **Stale default tag in install.sh** (see #2) and the soft-fail checksum path (warn-and-continue when SHA256SUMS is missing) slightly undercut the "verified against SHA256SUMS" claim in README.md:23.

## Summary verdict

The first-run UX *design* (init → doctor → try → start, verdict surfaces, try: refusal lines, keyless smoke path) is well above average and clearly deliberate. But the tool as compiled is currently **not installable-by-strangers**: the hardcoded `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon` home (`paths.rs:6`) defeats every distribution channel the repo has carefully built, the user-facing HOWTO is machine-specific, CLI-provider login state is never validated before a run, and the TUI's abandon keybinding has drifted between code, CLI prompt, and docs. Fixing `DEFAULT_DEADRECKON_HOME`/`DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH` to derive from `$HOME`, scrubbing `/Users/gdc` from HOWTO.md, adding a login-state probe for `claude`/`codex` to doctor, and reconciling the abandon key would close most of the real new-user gap. Separately and urgently: `RELEASE.md` (with a live Apple app-specific password) and `Certificates.p12` are tracked in git despite the file claiming otherwise.

14	
15	- A run that edits `acceptance.yaml`, or whose compiled checks contain a suppression pattern (`|| true`, `; true`, `--no-verify`, `--exit-zero`), is **refused**: no marker, the gate fails non-terminally, the loop continues with a corrective reason.
16	- A run that modified a file an acceptance check covers (a `file_exists`/`content_match` target, or a test file a `cargo_test`/`shell` check exercises) is **signed with a caveat**, surfaced loudly, never silently passed.
17	- A clean run signs exactly as today.
18	- `status`, the exit card, and `--why-failed` show a per-check verdict (`gate: FAILED 1/4 — cargo_test x (auth::tests::expired_token)`) and `tests modified this run: yes/no`; caveats render with `Warn` tone.
19	- Subscription turns never print `~$0.000000`; spend reads `not metered (subscription) · wall <s>s · <n> turns`.
20	
21	**Policy (decided; rider is the spec).** **Refuse** = spec edited this run or a suppression-pattern lint hit (no marker). **Caveat** = agent modified/deleted a check-covered file (modifying tested *production* code is normal; touching the *test or contract* is the danger — rider heuristics draw the line). Touched files = `provenance.jsonl` union first-snapshot vs final working-dir diff (catches deletions). Forged tamper files fail marker-signature validation.
22	
23	**Phases.** Eight (P1-P8) in the rider. Each: depth test first -> implement -> focused tests green -> conventional local commit -> CHANGELOG. P1 reproduces the hollow pass (RED). P8 adds an AS-BUILT section and logs deferrals.
24	
25	**Verification.**
26	
27	- Every rider depth test present and passing; `cargo fmt --check`; `git diff --check`.
28	- Smoke: a run that deletes a covered test file is **refused** (no marker; never `Completed`).
29	- Smoke: a clean run **signs** and promotes as today; a caveat run signs and the exit card shows the caveat with `Warn` tone.
30	- No edits outside the repo; no `git push`; no `PipelineState`/`Plan` schema changes.
31	
32	**Stop when** verification passes, the hollow pass is refused, caveat and per-check verdicts render, honest subscription spend renders, AS-BUILT and CHANGELOG record the behavior, deferrals are in V1-CANDIDATES, and the work is committed locally.
33

1	GOAL: Let one task spawn N orchestrators. Add `deadreckon campaign <goal> --n <2..=6>`: a **meta-coordinator** that decomposes a root goal into N independent sub-goals, launches each as its own full orchestrator (`orchestrate full-plan`) in an isolated scope, then composes the N merged results into one promoted run. It is the existing `fork`->`merge` pattern lifted exactly one level: each child is a sub-orchestrator whose merged result is itself a normal run, so the meta-merge reuses the same compose primitives. Bounded by a **hard depth cap of 2**, a **tree-wide spend ceiling**, a **cycle guard**, and a **gate-verdict roll-up** so nesting cannot quietly erode the §35 tamper-evident gate. Headline word: **Campaign**.
2	
3	**Read first.**
4	
5	- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md` — §30 plans/orchestration, §35 tamper-evident gate.
6	- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-05-28-1841-deadreckon-campaign-rider.md` — full contract.
7	- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon-core/src/plan.rs`, `.../src/tamper.rs`.
8	- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs` — `fork_command`, `run_plan_child`, `merge_command`, `compose_plan_merge_working`, `resolve_plan_result_run`, `kill_command`.
9	- Prior riders in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/` — invariants hold.
10	
11	**Posture.** Production-release track. Files-not-fields: meta-plan, lineage, and roll-up are new files under `~/.deadreckon/plans/<campaign-id>/`; **no** `Plan`/`PlanTask`/`PipelineState`/provider schema changes. Child work stays normal `deadreckon` subprocesses (§30.1). Depth **hard-capped at 2** — sub-orchestrators cannot fan out again. No `git push`. Edits inside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/`. Depth>2, cross-level dependencies/merge-repair, recursive live attach → `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
12	
13	**User contract.**
14	
15	- `deadreckon campaign <goal> --n <2..=6>` previews mode, N, depth cap, tree budget, and provider roles, then (with `--yes`) launches N independent sub-orchestrators and composes their results.
16	- A campaign invoked from inside a sub-orchestrator (depth would reach 2) is **refused**; no meta-plan is written. A sub-goal resolving to an ancestor's `task_key`/scope is **refused** (cycle guard).
17	- `--max-spend` is a **tree ceiling**: split across sub-orchestrators, aggregate spend tracked across every leaf run; the meta refuses to launch more once exhausted.
18	- The campaign result reports **clean only if every leaf run signed clean**; any refused leaf fails the campaign, any caveat leaf surfaces a caveat (roll-up over §35 verdicts).
19	- `attach <campaign-id>` shows the N sub-plan rows with a breadcrumb; `kill <campaign-id>` cascades to sub-coordinators and their children; `show <campaign-id> --why-failed` explains a failed campaign.
20

26	- Smoke (smoke provider, `--sandbox none`): a 2-sub-goal campaign launches two sub-orchestrators, composes one promoted result, and `campaign-rollup.json` records both leaf verdicts.
27	- Smoke: a campaign attempted at depth 2 is **refused** (no meta-plan, clear reason).
28	- Smoke: one leaf refused (hollow pass) makes the **campaign fail**, never `Completed`; one leaf caveat surfaces a caveat on the meta summary.
29	- No edits outside the repo; no `git push`; no `Plan`/`PlanTask`/`PipelineState` schema changes.

1	# deadreckon HOWTO
2	
3	This repo builds a Rust CLI named `deadreckon` for unattended coding runs.
4	The CLI is the control plane; the TUI is an attachable live dashboard.
5	
6	DeadReckon is for people who already use agent CLIs and need unattended,
7	sandboxed, auditable work with a real definition of done. It is the harness around
8	those harnesses: provider CLIs do the coding while DeadReckon owns isolation,
9	done criteria, lifecycle, logs, evidence, recovery, and promotion. It supervises
10	agent CLIs instead of replacing them.
11	
12	For a first serious run:
13	
14	```bash
15	deadreckon start "build the app"
16	deadreckon attach latest
17	deadreckon status latest
18	deadreckon list
19	deadreckon finish latest
20	```
21	
22	## New User Path
23	
24	Use `start` when you want DeadReckon to choose the right first path and tell you
25	exactly what is missing:
26	
27	```bash
28	deadreckon start "build the app"
29	deadreckon attach latest
30	deadreckon status latest
31	deadreckon list
32	deadreckon finish latest
33	```
34	
35	In a TTY, `start` presents selection prompts for mode, provider, missing done
36	criteria, source mode, and final confirmation. For scripts, pass explicit flags
37	with `--yes`, `--plain`, `--quiet`, or `--json` so it never waits for input.
38	
39	If setup is incomplete, `start` stops before launching work and prints concrete
40	`try:` lines for setup, done criteria, or source mode. Paste the suggested
41	commands, then run the same `deadreckon start "build the app"` command again.
42	
43	If this repo already has completed deadreckon history, TTY `start` can offer a
44	follow-up from the latest extendable run, a new review pass, or a new full-plan
45	pass. For scripts, use preview first:
46	
47	```bash
48	deadreckon start "add settings" --preview --plain
49	deadreckon extend <run-id> "add settings"
50	deadreckon start "add settings" --mode review --yes
51	deadreckon start "add settings" --mode full-plan --yes
52	```
53	
54	When done criteria already exist, TTY `start` shows the current criteria and
55	offers keep, view, check, update, or cancel before launch. You can inspect or
56	change the same contract directly:
57	
58	```bash
59	deadreckon def-done show
60	deadreckon def-done check
61	deadreckon def-done "what should count as done"
62	```
63	
64	## Normal Single Run
65	
66	Use `run` directly when you already know this should be one supervised coding
67	run:
68	
69	```bash
70	deadreckon run "goal"
71	deadreckon attach latest
72	deadreckon finish latest
73	```
74	
75	`run` is still the canonical power-user command for source-mode flags, spend
76	caps, sandbox overrides, and one-run scripting.
77	
78	## Multi-Agent Work
79	
80	Use `orchestrate` directly when the goal needs a coder/reviewer pass or a
81	planner-led split into child runs:
82	
83	```bash
84	deadreckon orchestrate review "goal" --yes
85	deadreckon orchestrate full-plan "goal" --n 4 --yes
86	deadreckon attach latest
87	deadreckon finish latest
88	```
89	
90	`start --mode review` and `start --mode full-plan` route through the same
91	orchestration machinery when you want the guided front door first.
92	
93	## Build And Install Alias
94	
95	```bash
96	cd /Users/gdc/deadreckon
97	make build
98	make alias-zsh
99	source /Users/gdc/.zshrc
100	deadreckon --help
101	```
102	
103	The alias points to:
104	
105	```bash
106	/Users/gdc/deadreckon/target/release/deadreckon
107	```
108	
109	## Shell Tab Completion
110	
111	`deadreckon init` installs shell completion automatically when it can detect
112	your shell. To install or repair it later:
113	
114	```bash
115	deadreckon completion install
116	```
117	
118	That writes the generated script to the normal location for your shell. For zsh
119	it also adds a managed `.zshrc` block that loads `~/.zsh/completions`.
120	
121	Override detection or print a raw script:
122	
123	```bash
124	deadreckon completion install --shell zsh
125	deadreckon completion zsh > ~/.zsh/completions/_deadreckon
126	```
127	
128	## Make Targets
129	
130	```bash
131	make help             # list targets
132	make build            # cargo build --release
133	make verify           # release build, tests, clippy, fmt check
134	make smoke            # keyless local smoke run
135	make doctor           # run deadreckon doctor
136	make stress           # 5 concurrent runs; defaults to 10 minutes
137	make clean-runtime    # remove repo-local smoke state
138	```
139	
140	Override runtime locations or stress duration:
141	
142	```bash
143	DEADRECKON_HOME=/tmp/deadreckon-home make smoke
144	STRESS_SECONDS=30 make stress
145	```
146	
147	## Runtime State
148	
149	By default, deadreckon writes runtime state to:
150	
151	```bash
152	/Users/gdc/.deadreckon
153	```
154	
155	For disposable tests, set:
156	
157	```bash
158	export DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.try-deadreckon
159	```
160	
161	Per-run artifacts include:
162	
163	```text
164	state.json
165	history.json
166	events.jsonl
167	traces.jsonl
168	spend.jsonl
169	provenance.jsonl
170	snapshots/turn-<N>/
171	proofs/turn-acceptance.json
172	working/ or library/<scope>/<run-id>/
173	```
174	
175	Completed accepted runs are promoted to:
176	
177	```bash
178	/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/library/<scope>/<run-id>/
179	```
180	
181	The directory where you launch `deadreckon run` is recorded as `launch-dir`.
182	In a git repo, the normal default is a separate worktree on a `dr/...` branch.
183	Your checkout is left unchanged until `deadreckon apply <run-id>`.
184	
185	## First Run
186	
187	Interactive setup:
188	
189	```bash
190	deadreckon init
191	deadreckon doctor
192	```
193	
194	Non-interactive examples:
195	
196	```bash
197	deadreckon init --provider cli:codex --sandbox auto --max-spend 10 --no-confirm
198	deadreckon init --provider anthropic --api-key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" --sandbox auto --max-spend 10 --no-confirm
199	deadreckon init --provider openai --api-key "$OPENAI_API_KEY" --sandbox auto --max-spend 10 --no-confirm
200	```
201	
202	Inspect or edit config:
203	
204	```bash
205	deadreckon config get defaults.provider
206	deadreckon config provider
207	deadreckon config provider cli:codex
208	deadreckon config model
209	deadreckon config model gpt-5.1-codex --provider cli:codex
210	deadreckon config set defaults.max_spend 15
211	deadreckon config set defaults.sandbox auto
212	deadreckon config set providers.anthropic.api_key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
213	```
214	
215	## Keyless Smoke Run
216	
217	Use this to prove the harness works without provider keys:
218	
219	```bash
220	export DEADRECKON_HOME=/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.try-deadreckon
221	rm -rf "$DEADRECKON_HOME"
222	
223	deadreckon run "tiny hello rust" --smoke --sandbox none --max-spend 1
224	deadreckon list
225	deadreckon status
226	```
227	
228	The default list is compact, project-scoped, and shows eight-character run IDs.
229	Commands accept unique prefixes, so `deadreckon show 861c51bf` works when that
230	prefix is unique. Most run-id arguments also accept `latest` or `last`, resolved
231	to the latest run for the current project. Use `--all` for global history and
232	`show` when you need full paths, IDs, traces, docs, and next actions.
233	
234	Inspect the latest run:
235	
236	```bash
237	deadreckon show latest
238	```
239	
240	Then attach to or finish it:
241	
242	```bash
243	deadreckon attach latest
244	```
245	
246	## Normal Single Run Details
247	
248	After `init`, the normal path in a git repo is:
249	
250	```bash
251	deadreckon run "make a full task productivity tracker in nodejs that allows me to manage my day"
252	deadreckon attach latest
253	deadreckon status
254	deadreckon finish latest
255	deadreckon apply latest --autostash --cleanup
256	```
257	
258	`run` prints the run id and attach command as soon as state is created:
259	
260	```text
261	started run <short-id> (<full-id>)
262	attach: deadreckon attach <short-id>
263	```
264	
265	Before it creates state or files, `run` prints a preview. In a clean git repo,
266	the preview shows `mode: worktree`, the `dr/...` branch, the base ref, and the
267	worktree path. Use `--yes` to skip the confirmation in scripts or `--preview`
268	to print the block and exit.
269	
270	Mode overrides:
271	
272	```bash
273	deadreckon run "goal" --fresh                         # old empty working dir
274	deadreckon run "goal" --from .                        # gitignore-aware copy
275	deadreckon run "goal" --worktree                      # force git worktree
276	deadreckon run "goal" --base main --branch-name dr/my-task # customize worktree branch
277	deadreckon run "goal" --allow-dirty                   # seed dirty files into worktree
278	deadreckon run "goal" --in-place --i-know-its-a-lot   # edit current dir directly
279	```
280	
281	Outside git, interactive `run` offers git init, copy mode, or cancel.
282	Non-interactive runs outside git need an explicit mode:
283	
284	```bash
285	deadreckon run "goal" --from . --yes
286	deadreckon run "goal" --fresh --yes
287	git init && deadreckon run "goal" --yes
288	```
289	
290	The default config from `deadreckon init` supplies the provider, sandbox, `$10` spend cap, and `3600` second wall-clock cap. Use flags only when overriding those defaults:
291	
292	```bash
293	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:codex
294	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:codex --model gpt-5.1-codex
295	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:claude-code
296	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:claude-code --model sonnet
297	deadreckon run "goal" --provider anthropic
298	deadreckon run "goal" --provider openai
299	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox sandbox-exec
300	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox none
301	deadreckon run "goal" --max-spend 5
302	deadreckon run "goal" --max-wall-seconds 1800
303	```
304	
305	`deadreckon run --preview "goal"` prints the provider and model before creating
306	state. `--model` is per-run; `deadreckon config model ...` makes the model
307	default for that provider. For CLI providers, `provider default` means
308	deadreckon delegates model choice to Codex or Claude Code unless you pass
309	`--model`.
310	
311	Run docs use their own provider route. By default deadreckon uses
312	`defaults.doc_provider`, then an installed subscription CLI (`cli:codex` before
313	`cli:claude-code`), then the run provider. Override it per run when needed:
314	
315	```bash
316	deadreckon run "goal" --doc-provider cli:codex
317	deadreckon config set defaults.doc_provider cli:codex
318	```
319	
320	Spend above `$50` requires confirmation:
321	
322	```bash
323	deadreckon run "large goal" --max-spend 75 --i-know-its-a-lot
324	```
325	
326	## TUI
327	
328	Open the dashboard:
329	
330	```bash
331	deadreckon attach <run-id>
332	```
333	
334	The TUI shows:
335	
336	```text
337	run id, status, phase, goal
338	working directory
339	per-turn timer
340	compact spend/context telemetry
341	wide center-left tool-call/provider activity stream
342	narrow center-right live files being generated
343	bottom supervised process/status panel
344	completed-run Markdown docs view
345	provider activity from live Codex session logs
346	```
347	
348	Keys:
349	
350	```text
351	Ctrl-D   detach without killing the run
352	q        quit
353	Esc      quit
354	Tab      move focus between panels
355	j/k      scroll focused panel
356	PgUp/PgDn scroll focused panel by a page
357	```
358	
359	After a run completes, the TUI footer adds lifecycle actions:
360	
361	```text
362	a        apply a completed worktree run
363	b        abandon/discard a completed worktree run
364	d        toggle formatted RUN-NARRATIVE.md docs in the main panel
365	m        export a completed copy/fresh artifact
366	e        extend a completed copy/fresh run with a follow-up goal
367	s        show run details
368	```
369	
370	The docs view uses a Markdown parser and ratatui styles for headings, bullets,
371	inline code, fenced code blocks, links, horizontal rules, and task lists. Press
372	`d` again to return to provider activity. Scroll it with the same `j/k`,
373	arrow-key, page-key, and mouse-wheel bindings.
374	
375	## Generated Docs
376	
377	Every run writes `.deadreckon/docs/_incremental.jsonl` at turn boundaries and
378	emits a `docs_checkpoint` event. Completion then runs the doc polish step unless
379	you passed `--no-docs`.
380	
381	```bash
382	deadreckon doc latest
383	deadreckon doc latest --kind as-built
384	deadreckon doc latest --kind decisions
385	deadreckon doc latest --polish --overwrite
386	deadreckon doc latest --polish --doc-provider cli:codex --max-spend 0.25
387	```
388	
389	`deadreckon doc latest --kind decisions` prints the implementation decision
390	ledger: design decisions, deviations, tradeoffs, open questions, and
391	multi-alternative decision details. The live working copy for those sections is
392	`implementation-notes.html` in the run working directory.
393	
394	The polish preview lists the provider, why it was selected, the four narrator
395	subskills, token budget, max spend, and inputs hash. `--no-confirm` skips the
396	prompt for scripts. Results are recorded in `polish.json` with one status line
397	per subskill.
398	
399	The TUI does not start, kill, resume, or undo runs. Use CLI commands for those controls.
400	
401	## Completion Actions
402	
403	Completed `run` and `extend` commands show the same lifecycle actions in the CLI:
404	
405	```text
406	completed action [a apply, b abandon, d docs, s show, q quit]:
407	completed action [m export, e extend, d docs, s show, q quit]:
408	```
409	
410	Worktree runs use `a` to squash-apply changes to the current branch or `b` to
411	abandon the worktree and temporary branch. Copy/fresh runs use `m` to export the
412	library artifact into a normal directory, `e` to start a child run from the
413	completed artifact, `d` to read `RUN-NARRATIVE.md`, or `s` to inspect state and lineage. Pass `--no-hints` to
414	`run` or `attach` when scripting.
415	
416	The CLI aliases use friendlier lifecycle names:
417	
418	```bash
419	deadreckon finish latest                            # choose apply or export from run mode
420	deadreckon def-done "builds and passes tests"           # write done criteria
421	deadreckon export latest --dest ./finished-project   # copy an artifact to a normal directory
422	deadreckon keep latest --autostash --cleanup         # alias for apply
423	deadreckon abandon latest                            # remove a temporary worktree/branch
424	deadreckon status                                    # latest state and next action
425	deadreckon watch latest                              # alias for attach
426	deadreckon stop latest                               # alias for kill
427	deadreckon continue latest                           # alias for resume
428	deadreckon inspect latest                            # alias for show
429	deadreckon docs latest                               # alias for doc
430	deadreckon prune --completed                         # alias for cleanup
431	```
432	
433	`extend` is still available for completed worktree runs from the CLI. It creates
434	a new `dr/...` branch from the parent run's branch, so the follow-up keeps the
435	parent changes without applying them to your checkout first:
436	
437	```bash
438	deadreckon extend <worktree-run-id> "continue with the next change"
439	```
440	
441	## List, Show, Kill, Resume
442	
443	```bash
444	deadreckon list
445	deadreckon list --all
446	deadreckon status
447	deadreckon show <run-id>
448	deadreckon show latest
449	deadreckon inspect latest
450	deadreckon finish latest
451	deadreckon finish latest --dest ./finished-project
452	deadreckon finish latest --autostash --cleanup
453	deadreckon apply <run-id>
454	deadreckon apply <run-id> --autostash
455	deadreckon apply <run-id> --cleanup --no-confirm
456	deadreckon apply <run-id> --git-strategy merge
457	deadreckon apply <run-id> --git-strategy cherry-pick --no-confirm
458	deadreckon keep <run-id> --autostash --cleanup
459	deadreckon abandon <run-id>
460	deadreckon abandon <run-id> --keep-branch
461	deadreckon cleanup --completed
462	deadreckon cleanup --stale --escalate
463	deadreckon cleanup --all-scopes --completed --no-confirm
464	deadreckon prune --completed
465	deadreckon kill <run-id>
466	deadreckon stop <run-id>
467	deadreckon kill <run-id> --escalate
468	deadreckon resume <run-id>
469	deadreckon continue <run-id>
470	deadreckon resume <run-id> --from-turn 2
471	deadreckon resume <run-id> --max-wall-seconds 3600
472	```
473	
474	`finish` is the easiest completion command. For a worktree run it routes to
475	`apply`; for a fresh/copy run it routes to `export`; for an in-place run it
476	prints review, docs, and undo guidance.
477	
478	Re-running `deadreckon apply <run-id>` after the changes are already on the
479	target branch is safe: deadreckon reports `already applied` instead of creating
480	or failing an empty commit. Add `--cleanup` to remove the temporary worktree and
481	branch in that already-applied state.
482	
483	`resume --from-turn N` truncates reconstructed history to turn `N` and continues with turn `N + 1`.
484	
485	## Undo
486	
487	Restore the previous turn snapshot:
488	
489	```bash
490	deadreckon undo --run <run-id>
491	```
492	
493	Restore a specific turn:
494	
495	```bash
496	deadreckon undo --run <run-id> --turn 1
497	```
498	
499	Undo restores the run working directory from `snapshots/turn-<N>/` and records
500	an undo trace. For in-place runs, undo restores the original source path because
501	the agent edited that directory directly.
502	
503	## Done Criteria
504	
505	If a run has no custom acceptance spec, `dr-gate` checks that the working directory exists and runs `cargo test` when `Cargo.toml` is present.
506	
507	The normal path is English first:
508	
509	```bash
510	deadreckon def-done "build, load in a browser, and show no console errors"
511	deadreckon def-done add "users can save drawings"
512	deadreckon def-done check
513	deadreckon run "goal"
514	```
515	
516	`def-done` asks the configured provider to convert plain-English criteria into `.deadreckon/acceptance.yaml`. Short pack names are available without a provider when they fit:
517	
518	```bash
519	deadreckon def-done add build
520	deadreckon def-done add node
521	deadreckon def-done add static-site
522	deadreckon def-done add browser
523	deadreckon def-done add playwright
524	deadreckon def-done add vite
525	deadreckon def-done add nextjs
526	deadreckon def-done add python
527	```
528	
529	Runs and chains prompt before starting when no project acceptance file exists. Helper scripts generated by packs or drafts live under `.deadreckon/acceptance/` and are copied into the run workspace before `dr-gate` executes.
530	
531	The compiled YAML looks like this:
532	
533	```yaml
534	name: notes check
535	checks:
536	  - kind: file_exists
537	    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
538	  - kind: content_match
539	    path: "{working_dir}/notes.md"
540	    pattern: "dead reckoning"
541	  - kind: build_success
542	    cwd: "{working_dir}"
543	```
544	
545	Supported check kinds:
546	
547	```text
548	cargo_test
549	file_exists
550	content_match
551	build_success
552	shell
553	```
554	
555	`content_match` treats `pattern` as a regex when valid, with substring fallback for simple text. Shell, build, and cargo checks record duration plus clipped stdout/stderr so failures are readable.
556	
557	The acceptance marker is signed with a run-local nonce. A marker written by the agent is refused.
558	
559	## Import Existing Tool History
560	
561	Read-only imports:
562	
563	```bash
564	deadreckon import claude-code
565	deadreckon import codex
566	deadreckon import cursor
567	```
568	
569	Default source roots:
570	
571	```text
572	/Users/gdc/.claude/projects/
573	/Users/gdc/.codex/sessions/
574	/Users/gdc/.cursor/chats/
575	```
576	
577	Override source roots for testing:
578	
579	```bash
580	DEADRECKON_IMPORT_CLAUDE_ROOT=/tmp/claude deadreckon import claude-code
581	DEADRECKON_IMPORT_CODEX_ROOT=/tmp/codex deadreckon import codex
582	DEADRECKON_IMPORT_CURSOR_ROOT=/tmp/cursor deadreckon import cursor
583	```
584	
585	Imports create synthetic `imported-<hash>` runs with normalized traces and provenance.
586	
587	## Sandboxes
588	
589	Backends:
590	
591	```text
592	auto
593	sandbox-exec
594	bwrap
595	docker
596	none
597	```
598	
599	Examples:
600	
601	```bash
602	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox auto
603	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox sandbox-exec
604	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox docker
605	deadreckon run "goal" --sandbox none
606	```
607	
608	Use `none` only for explicit local verification. `doctor` reports which sandbox binaries are available.
609	
610	## Doctor
611	
612	```bash
613	deadreckon doctor
614	```
615	
616	Checks include:
617	
618	```text
619	config present and parseable
620	provider credentials or CLI binaries
621	sandbox binaries and versions
622	disk space
623	runstate write permissions
624	OS/kernel sanity
625	Claude/Codex subscription CLI availability
626	```
627	
628	HTTP provider pings are conservative. Enable live ping behavior explicitly:
629	
630	```bash
631	DEADRECKON_DOCTOR_PING=1 deadreckon doctor
632	```
633	
634	## Stress And Verification
635	
636	Full normal verification:
637	
638	```bash
639	make verify
640	```
641	
642	Ten-minute 5-run stress:
643	
644	```bash
645	make stress
646	```
647	
648	Short stress while developing:
649	
650	```bash
651	STRESS_SECONDS=30 make stress
652	```
653	
654	The stress test asserts completed states, unique scopes, provenance identity, and no leftover lock files.
655	
656	## Configuration
657	
658	Runtime config lives at `~/.deadreckon/config.toml`. Set `DEADRECKON_HOME` to
659	relocate all runtime state (config, runstate, library) for isolated local runs
660	or tests.
661	
662	Switch providers, models, or defaults:
663	
664	```bash
665	deadreckon init --provider cli:codex --sandbox auto --max-spend 10
666	deadreckon init --provider anthropic --api-key "$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"
667	deadreckon config provider cli:claude-code
668	deadreckon config model sonnet --provider cli:claude-code
669	deadreckon config set defaults.max_spend 15
670	```
671	
672	Override per run:
673	
674	```bash
675	deadreckon run "goal" --provider cli:codex --model gpt-5.1-codex
676	deadreckon run --preview "goal"     # show route and model, don't start
677	```
678	
679	### Sandbox Backends
680	
681	| Backend | What it is |
682	|---|---|
683	| `auto` | Picks the right native sandbox for your OS (default) |
684	| `sandbox-exec` | macOS native |
685	| `bwrap` | Linux native (bubblewrap) |
686	| `docker` | Opt-in container sandbox |
687	| `none` | Off (unsafe for real unattended work) |
688	
689	Check what your machine supports with `deadreckon doctor`. See
690	[Sandboxes](#sandboxes) above for run examples.
691	
692	## Full Command Reference
693	
694	The production model is a small set of verbs; every other command stays
695	findable through `deadreckon help-all`, `<command> --help`, and completion.
696	
697	Default production model:
698	
699	```text
700	start         begin supervised agent work
701	attach        open the live dashboard
702	status        latest run and next action for this project
703	list          find runs and plans
704	finish        choose apply or export from completed work
705	doctor        check config, providers, sandboxes, disk, runtime
706	init          create local config
707	def-done      compile English "done" criteria into checks
708	kill          stop a live run, chain, or plan
709	resume        continue an interrupted run
710	cleanup       clean abandoned, stale, or completed worktrees
711	help-all      show every advanced and compatibility command
712	```
713	
714	Power-user and advanced commands:
715	
716	```text
717	run           start one unattended coding run directly
718	orchestrate   one-command review / full-plan multi-agent runs
719	chain         plan and run ordered multi-step work
720	plan          write an orchestration plan (no child runs yet)
721	fork          start a plan's ready child runs
722	merge         compose plan children into one promoted artifact
723	apply         apply a completed worktree run to your branch
724	export        copy a completed artifact to a normal directory
725	extend        continue from a completed run
726	show          inspect state, lineage, spend, files
727	doc           print or export run documentation
728	rewind        preview or apply a provider flight checkpoint
729	history       search durable traces and provenance
730	library       query promoted run artifacts
731	providers     list provider routes (detect probes availability)
732	detect        probe registered providers
733	config        inspect or edit config keys
734	update        check for or apply self-updates
735	learn         index run evidence and propose improvements
736	improve       run evidence-gated self-improvement candidates
737	import        normalize histories from other coding tools
738	undo          restore a previous turn snapshot
739	abandon       remove a worktree run and temporary branch
740	completion    install shell tab-completion
741	```
742	
743	Aliases: `keep` → `apply`, `materialize` → `export`, `discard` → `abandon`,
744	`prune` → `cleanup`, `follow-up` → `extend`, `continue` → `resume`,
745	`stop` → `kill`, `next` → `status`.
746	
747	## Troubleshooting
748	
749	Run:
750	
751	```bash
752	deadreckon doctor
753	deadreckon list
754	deadreckon show <run-id>
755	```
756	
757	Common fixes:
758	
759	```bash
760	deadreckon init
761	deadreckon config set defaults.provider cli:codex
762	deadreckon config set defaults.sandbox auto
763	deadreckon kill <run-id> --escalate
764	deadreckon resume <run-id>
765	```
766	
767	If the alias does not exist in the current shell:
768	
769	```bash
770	source /Users/gdc/.zshrc
771	alias deadreckon
772	```
773
```

2	  <img src="docs/assets/deadreckon-wordmark.png" alt="deadreckon logo" width="640">

4	
5	<p align="center"><strong>Run your coding agent unattended, and trust the result.</strong></p>
6	
7	<p align="center">
8	DeadReckon is a harness around the agent CLI you already use.<br>
9	A separate watchdog process, not the agent, decides when the work is actually done.<br>
10	You get a signed, auditable artifact instead of a chat transcript you have to take on faith.
11	</p>
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Get started
16	
17	Install the latest release (macOS / Linux):
18	
19	```bash
20	curl -fsSL https://deadreckon.sh/install.sh | sh
21	```
22	
23	This downloads the release installer, verifies it against `SHA256SUMS`, and installs `deadreckon`. Pin a version with `DEADRECKON_TAG=v0.1.0-rc.1`.
24	
25	Or build from source:
26	
27	```bash
28	cargo build --release          # binary at ./target/release/deadreckon
29	```
30	
31	Then the whole tool is five commands:
32	
33	| Command | What it does |
34	|---|---|
35	| `deadreckon start "build the app"` | Kick off a supervised run. Walk away. |
36	| `deadreckon attach latest` | Watch it work live. `Ctrl-D` leaves it running. |
37	| `deadreckon status` | What happened, and the one thing to do next. |
38	| `deadreckon list` | Find recent runs and plans. |
39	| `deadreckon finish latest` | Apply it to your branch, or export it. |
40	
41	For a higher-level read while it runs, `deadreckon attach latest --view narrative` shows cited prose plus an evidence-backed visual map.
42	
43	<p align="center">
44	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/claude-logo.png" alt="Claude Code" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
45	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/openai-logo.png" alt="Codex" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
46	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/gemini-logo.png" alt="Gemini CLI" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
47	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/github-logo.png" alt="GitHub Copilot CLI" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
48	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/opencode-logo.png" alt="OpenCode" height="34">&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;
49	  <img src="docs/assets/providers/pi-logo.svg" alt="Pi" height="34">
50	</p>
51	
52	<p align="center"><sub>Supervises the agent CLI you already use: Claude Code · Codex · Gemini · Copilot · OpenCode · Pi · or any Anthropic / OpenAI-compatible API.</sub></p>
53	
54	Everything else (budgets, undo, multi-step chains, provider routing) is optional power you reach for later. No API keys? `deadreckon run "hello" --smoke --sandbox none` exercises the whole harness against a faked provider.
55	
56	> [!TIP]
57	> DeadReckon is on the production-release track. The core lifecycle (isolated runs, signed gates, durable state, undo, docs, orchestration, and apply) is implemented and tested; release notes call out any compatibility migrations.
58	
59	## Why it's different
60	
61	- **It can't fake the finish.** A separate watchdog (`dr-gate`) holds a secret the agent process can't read and signs the result with it. No valid signature, no "done." The agent literally cannot mark its own work accepted.
62	- **Walk away for real.** Every turn is saved to disk. Close your laptop, lose the network, kill the model, then attach from another terminal and resume from the last completed turn.
63	- **Evidence, not a transcript.** Each accepted run promotes to a reviewable artifact: what changed, why, which prompt touched which file, what it spent.

```text
1	# deadreckon: Concepts & How It Works
2	
3	The narrative companion to the [README](../README.md). If the README tells you
4	*what to type*, this explains *what deadreckon is doing and why you can trust
5	it*. For step-by-step usage, see [HOWTO](../HOWTO.md).
6	
7	## How it works
8	
9	1. **You write "done" in plain English.** deadreckon compiles it into executable checks: tests that must pass, files that must exist, scripts that must succeed.
10	2. **The agent runs in an isolated worktree**, inside a sandbox. Your real checkout is never touched.
11	3. **Every turn is saved** (state, spend, traces, file provenance, snapshots) so you can attach, kill, resume, undo, or audit any moment.
12	4. **A separate watchdog process (`dr-gate`) decides when the work is done.** It holds a secret the agent process cannot read, and signs the result with that secret. The agent cannot forge the signature, so it cannot mark its own work as accepted.
13	5. **If the checks fail, the loop keeps going.** The agent gets another turn. When the watchdog finally signs off for real, the run is atomically promoted to a reviewable artifact: narrative, decisions, file provenance, full audit trail.
14	
15	The loop is the product. The agent CLI does the coding. deadreckon decides when "done" actually means done.
16	
17	## Why this matters
18	
19	**The agent does the coding. deadreckon decides when it's done.**
20	
21	- **It can't fake the finish.** The watchdog (`dr-gate`) holds a secret the agent process can't read and signs the result with it. No valid signature, no "done." The agent literally cannot forge its own acceptance.
22	- **Walk away for real.** Every turn is saved to disk: state, spend, file lineage, a full snapshot. Close your laptop, lose the network, kill the model, then attach from another terminal and resume from the last completed turn. Nothing replays, nothing is lost.
23	- **You get evidence, not a transcript.** Each accepted run promotes to a reviewable artifact: what changed, why, which prompt touched which file, what it spent. Auditable on disk, not scrolled back in a chat window.
24	- **Bring the agent you already trust.** Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, OpenCode, Pi, or a raw API key: deadreckon supervises any of them. It owns the boundary, not the intelligence.
25	
26	## Bring your own agent CLI
27	
28	deadreckon owns the run boundary; the CLI does the coding. Route any turn through the agent you already trust:
29	
30	| | Agent CLI (subscription) | Route |
31	|---|---|---|
32	| <img src="assets/providers/claude-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **Claude Code** | `cli:claude-code` |
33	| <img src="assets/providers/openai-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **Codex** | `cli:codex` |
34	| <img src="assets/providers/gemini-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **Gemini CLI** | `cli:gemini` |
35	| <img src="assets/providers/github-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | `cli:copilot` |
36	| <img src="assets/providers/opencode-logo.png" alt="" width="22"> | **OpenCode** | `cli:opencode` |
37	| <img src="assets/providers/pi-logo.svg" alt="" width="22"> | **Pi** | `cli:pi` |
38	
39	Prefer your own keys? Route directly to **Anthropic** (`anthropic`), **OpenAI** (`openai`), or any **OpenAI-compatible** endpoint (`openai-compatible`, e.g. OpenRouter, llama.cpp, local models). No keys at all? `--smoke` runs the whole harness against a faked provider.
40	
41	Already have history in another tool? `deadreckon import claude-code | codex | cursor` ingests it read-only as a run you can inspect.
42	
43	## The two things that make it different
44	
45	### Write "Done" In English, Verified By A Watchdog The Agent Can't Fool
46	
47	Tell deadreckon what success looks like in plain language. It compiles your sentence into executable checks that an independent watchdog runs:
48	
49	```bash
50	deadreckon def-done "build, load in a browser, and show no console errors"
51	deadreckon def-done add "users can save drawings"
52	deadreckon def-done check
53	deadreckon run "finish the app"
54	```
55	
56	**Why the watchdog matters.** `dr-gate` holds a run-local secret the agent process cannot read, and stamps the result with it. Without a valid stamp, the run can't terminate, and the agent can't produce the stamp itself. If the checks fail, the run doesn't end; the agent gets another turn with a corrective hint.
57	
58	If no acceptance file is configured, the default is "the working directory exists and `cargo test` passes" (when `Cargo.toml` is present). Supported check kinds are `cargo_test`, `file_exists`, `content_match`, `build_success`, and `shell`. Full reference, packs, and the compiled YAML format: [HOWTO § Done Criteria](../HOWTO.md#done-criteria).
59	
60	### Get An Auditable Artifact, Not A Transcript
61	
62	deadreckon records which model/tool call touched which files, then promotes each accepted run to a review packet:
63	
64	- `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` explains what happened.
65	- `RUN-DECISIONS.md` records the decision ledger: design decisions, deviations, tradeoffs, open questions.
66	- `RUN-AS-BUILT.md` captures the subsystem shape after the run.
67	- `provenance.jsonl` links every changed file back to the turn, tool call, and model that produced it.
68	- `manifest.json` records what was built and from what.
69	
70	Agentic CLIs usually leave you with a patch and a transcript. deadreckon turns the session into a local published artifact you can inspect, export, extend, or apply. Doc kinds and the TUI docs view: [HOWTO § Generated Docs](../HOWTO.md#generated-docs).
71	
72	## What else it does
73	
74	Each of these is a first-class capability; usage lives in [HOWTO](../HOWTO.md):
75	
76	- **Your checkout is never touched.** Runs default to an isolated `git worktree` on a `dr/...` branch; your real checkout changes only when you `deadreckon apply`. Copy, fresh, and explicit in-place modes are available too.
77	- **Crash-proof.** Every turn writes durable state. If the terminal dies, attach from another; if the run crashes, resume from the last completed turn.
78	- **Budgets and time limits.** `--max-spend 15` and `--max-wall-seconds 1800` cap a run, then walk away. High spend requires explicit confirmation.
79	- **Undo a single bad turn.** Snapshot-based rollback to any turn (`deadreckon undo --run <id> --turn 3`), recorded in the run trace, not just a `git reset`.
80	- **Resume, kill, extend, or export any run.** Runs are lifecycle objects, not one terminal session.
81	- **Autonomous chains for multi-step work.** Break a big goal into ordered steps, each with its own signed gate; the chain stops on the first gate failure.
82	
83	## The mental model
84	
85	```text
86	your repo
87	  |
88	  | deadreckon def-done "what 'finished' looks like, in English"
89	  | deadreckon run  "what to build"
90	  v
91	isolated worktree or copy   ◄── your real checkout untouched
92	  |
93	  | provider route: cli:codex, cli:claude-code, cli:gemini, anthropic, openai, ...
94	  v
95	sandboxed turn loop         ◄── agent works here
96	  |
97	  | every turn: trace, spend, provenance, snapshot, docs
98	  | check fails? agent gets another turn
99	  v
100	dr-gate watchdog            ◄── separate process, holds hidden nonce
101	  |                              agent CANNOT produce a valid marker
102	  | checks pass + signature valid?
103	  v
104	promoted artifact           ◄── narrative, decisions, file lineage
105	  |
106	  | inspect, doc, apply, discard, extend, export, cleanup
107	  v
108	your branch or library
109	```
110	
111	For multi-step work, `deadreckon chain` wraps this whole loop and runs N of them in order, stopping on the first gate failure. The agent owns the coding. deadreckon owns the boundary.
112	
113	## Compared with agentic coding CLIs
114	
115	deadreckon doesn't replace Claude Code, Codex, or the rest; it supervises them. Use it when the task is too long, risky, or expensive to "run the agent in my checkout and hope I can reconstruct what happened."
116	
117	| Operational concern | Agentic CLI alone | deadreckon supervising the CLI |
118	|---|---|---|
119	| Workspace safety | Often runs where you start it | Isolated worktree by default; your checkout untouched |
120	| Long-running attach | Tied to the current terminal | Durable state; attach from another terminal later |
121	| Spend control | Varies by provider | Tracks totals; enforces spend and wall-clock caps |
122	| Undo | git-level or manual | Snapshots every turn; restores a specific turn |
123	| Done criteria | The agent may declare itself done | Requires a signed `dr-gate` marker before promotion |
124	| Output | A patch and a transcript | A promoted, auditable artifact with file provenance |
125	
126	Use the agentic CLI for intelligence. Use deadreckon for isolation, supervision, evidence, recovery, and promotion.
127	
128	## Why "deadreckon"?
129	
130	Dead reckoning is navigation without perfect visibility: track every move so you know where you are now. Unattended agents are the same problem: long task, partial context, the terminal may be gone when you look back. The name is the contract: don't trust the final answer, navigate by evidence.
131
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# DeadReckon Seams
2	
3	Seams let you replace four governance workers with JSON-over-stdio subprocesses:
4	policy, model catalog, hooks, and event sink. They are configured in
5	`config.toml` under `[seams]`. The acceptance gate is deliberately not a seam.
6	
7	## Example Kit
8	
9	The runnable conformance examples live here:
10	
11	- `examples/seams/config.toml`
12	- `examples/seams/fixtures/policy-allow.json`
13	- `examples/seams/fixtures/policy-deny.json`
14	- `examples/seams/fixtures/catalog-request.json`
15	- `examples/seams/fixtures/hook-event.json`
16	- `examples/seams/fixtures/event-sink-event.json`
17	- `examples/seams/workers/policy-allow.sh`
18	- `examples/seams/workers/policy-deny.sh`
19	- `examples/seams/workers/catalog-minimal.sh`
20	- `examples/seams/workers/hooks-jsonl.sh`
21	- `examples/seams/workers/event-sink-jsonl.sh`
22	
23	Run examples from the repository root:
24	
25	```sh
26	deadreckon seams validate policy --config examples/seams/config.toml --fixture examples/seams/fixtures/policy-allow.json --sandbox none
27	deadreckon seams validate catalog --config examples/seams/config.toml --fixture examples/seams/fixtures/catalog-request.json --sandbox none
28	deadreckon seams validate hooks --config examples/seams/config.toml --fixture examples/seams/fixtures/hook-event.json --sandbox none
29	deadreckon seams validate event-sink --config examples/seams/config.toml --fixture examples/seams/fixtures/event-sink-event.json --sandbox none
30	```
31	
32	For live runs, prefer absolute worker paths or commands on `PATH`; a run
33	workspace may not have the repository root as its working directory.
34	
35	## Config
36	
37	```toml
38	[seams.policy]
39	command = ["sh", "examples/seams/workers/policy-allow.sh"]
40	timeout_ms = 1000
41	
42	[seams.catalog]
43	command = ["sh", "examples/seams/workers/catalog-minimal.sh"]
44	timeout_ms = 1000
45	
46	[seams.hooks]
47	command = ["sh", "examples/seams/workers/hooks-jsonl.sh"]
48	timeout_ms = 1000
49	
50	[seams.event_sink]
51	command = ["sh", "examples/seams/workers/event-sink-jsonl.sh"]
52	timeout_ms = 1000
53	```
54	
55	Allowed kinds are `policy`, `catalog`, `hooks`, and `event_sink`. Unknown kinds
56	are config errors. `[seams.gate]` is rejected because the gate is the local
57	trust root.
58	
59	## Worker Protocol
60	
61	Each worker receives one JSON object on stdin and should write one JSON object
62	to stdout before exiting. Workers run without network access through the
63	configured sandbox backend. `timeout_ms = 0` is invalid.
64	
65	Policy receives tool-decision context such as `function_id`, `command`, and
66	`working_dir`. It must return:
67	
68	```json
69	{"decision":"allow"}
70	```
71	
72	or:
73	
74	```json
75	{"decision":"deny","reason":"explain the denial"}
76	```
77	
78	Policy is fail-closed. Timeout, non-zero exit, invalid JSON, or any unknown
79	decision blocks the action.
80	
81	Catalog receives a catalog request object and returns model metadata:
82	
83	```json
84	{"models":[{"id":"local-scripted-smoke","context_window":4000}]}
85	```
86	
87	Catalog is fail-open. Invalid output is visible in validation, but the runtime
88	falls back to the built-in catalog.
89	
90	Hooks observe tool lifecycle events. Event sink observes run events. Both are
91	fail-safe: failure is visible, but neither can control acceptance or tool
92	decisions.
93	
94	## Validation
95	
96	Use `deadreckon seams validate` before putting a worker in a run:
97	
98	```sh
99	deadreckon seams validate policy --config examples/seams/config.toml --json --sandbox none
100	```
101	
102	Plain output includes kind, command, fixture, sandbox, outcome, fail policy, and
103	`try:` lines on failure. JSON output is intended for focused tests and scripts.
104	
105	`event-sink` is the CLI spelling; `event_sink` is the TOML key.
106	
107	## Sandbox and Gate Boundary
108	
109	Seam subprocesses inherit the seam sandbox, run without network, and get only
110	their JSON request through stdin plus a minimal environment. The runtime denies
111	seam access to the run's `gate/` and `proofs/` subtrees. The conformance
112	validator uses the same dispatch path.
113	
114	`dr-gate` remains local and deterministic. A seam can observe or narrow
115	behavior, but it cannot issue, redirect, or sign an acceptance marker.
116	
117	## Disabling Seams
118	
119	Use `--no-seams` to force all built-in behavior for one launch:
120	
121	```sh
122	deadreckon run "goal" --no-seams
123	deadreckon start "goal" --no-seams
124	```
125	
126	`deadreckon doctor` reports configured seam commands and their fail policies.
127
```
</details></tool-use>

93	# One-time setup steps (procedure)

95	### 1. Apple Developer Program ($99/yr)
96

98	- Use a long-lived Apple ID — this becomes `APPLE_ID`. **It must be the Apple ID

100	- **Individual** enrollment is instant-ish after payment; **Organization** needs
101	  a D-U-N-S number and takes 1–14 days. Individual is fine for a personal CLI;
102	  the cert shows your name in Gatekeeper output.
103	
104	### 2. Create the CSR (Keychain Access)
105	
106	- Keychain Access → menu bar **Certificate Assistant → Request a Certificate
107	  From a Certificate Authority**.
108	- User Email Address: the Apple ID email. Common Name: any label.
109	- CA Email Address: blank. Select **Saved to disk**.
110	- Produces a `.certSigningRequest`; the private key is created in the login
111	  keychain.

116	  **Developer ID Application** (not "Apple Development", not "Developer ID
117	  Installer", not any "Mac App"/"Distribution" variant).

119	- Upload the CSR, download the `.cer`, double-click to install into the login
120	  keychain.

126	```bash
127	curl -fsSL -o /tmp/DeveloperIDG2CA.cer \
128	  https://www.apple.com/certificateauthority/DeveloperIDG2CA.cer
129	security import /tmp/DeveloperIDG2CA.cer -k "$HOME/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db"
130	security find-identity -v -p codesigning
131	```
132	
133	### 5. Export the `.p12` for CI
134	
135	- Keychain Access → My Certificates → expand "Developer ID Application: …" so the
136	  nested private key shows → select **both** rows → right-click → **Export 2
137	  items… → Personal Information Exchange (.p12)**.
138	- Set an export password → this is `APPLE_CERT_PWD`.
139	
140	```bash
141	base64 -i Certificates.p12 | tr -d '\n' | gh secret set APPLE_CERT_P12
142	# or: ... | pbcopy  and paste into the GitHub secret
143	```
144	
145	### 6. App-specific password for `notarytool`
146	
147	- https://appleid.apple.com → Sign-In and Security → App-Specific Passwords →
148	  `+` → name "notarytool deadreckon".
149	- Generate it while signed in as the **membership-owning Apple ID**.
150	- Apple shows the 19-char password **once**. Save as `APPLE_APP_PWD`.
151	
152	### 7. Team ID
153	
154	- From the certificate name (`… (4GRQMF5T5U)`) or
155	  https://developer.apple.com/account → Membership Details → "Team ID".
156	
157	### 8. Set the GitHub secrets
158	
159	```bash
160	base64 -i Certificates.p12 | tr -d '\n' | gh secret set APPLE_CERT_P12
161	gh secret set APPLE_ID         # gregce@gmail.com
162	gh secret set APPLE_TEAM_ID    # 4GRQMF5T5U
163	gh secret set APPLE_APP_PWD    # the app-specific password
164	gh secret set APPLE_CERT_PWD   # the .p12 export password (hidden prompt)
165	gh secret list
166	```
167	
168	---
169	
170	## Local verification before trusting CI
171	
172	Sign with the keychain identity (no password needed), then notarize:
173	
174	```bash
175	work=$(mktemp -d)
176	cp target/release/deadreckon "$work/deadreckon"
177	
178	codesign --force --sign "Developer ID Application" \
179	  --options runtime --timestamp "$work/deadreckon"
180	codesign --verify --verbose "$work/deadreckon"
181	# expect: "satisfies its Designated Requirement"
182	codesign --display --verbose=2 "$work/deadreckon"
183	# expect Authority chain: Developer ID Application → Developer ID CA → Apple Root CA
184	
185	spctl --assess --type execute --verbose "$work/deadreckon" || true
186	# before notarization: "rejected — Unnotarized Developer ID" is EXPECTED
187	
188	ditto -c -k --keepParent "$work/deadreckon" "$work/deadreckon.zip"
189	xcrun notarytool submit "$work/deadreckon.zip" \
190	  --apple-id "gregce@gmail.com" \
191	  --team-id  "4GRQMF5T5U" \
192	  --password "lbyn-dvnh-xnif-pyjh" \
193	  --wait
194	# expect: status: Accepted
195	```
196	
197	If `status: Accepted`, the GitHub Actions step works with the same secrets.
198	
199	## Notes and gotchas
200	
201	- **No stapling for raw binaries.** A CLI (not an `.app`/`.dmg`/`.pkg`) can only
202	  be notarized, not stapled. Gatekeeper does an online ticket check on first run;
203	  that's the expected flow.
204	- **`--options runtime` is required.** Notarization rejects submissions without
205	  the hardened runtime flag.
206	- **Cert expiry: June 2, 2031.** Calendar a reminder. `security find-certificate
207	  -c "Developer ID Application" -p | openssl x509 -enddate -noout` shows it.
208	- **App-specific password rotation.** If `APPLE_APP_PWD` leaks, revoke it at
209	  appleid.apple.com and generate a new one; nothing else to rotate, the cert is
210	  not invalidated. **(The value above, `lbyn-dvnh-xnif-pyjh`, is slated for
211	  rotation — it appeared in a chat transcript.)**
212	- **Keychain on CI runners.** The workflow creates a temporary keychain, imports
213	  the `.p12`, and removes it after the run. Never check the `.p12` into the repo.
214	- **Open implementation question (tracked in the rider).** The rider flags that
215	  signing happens before `dist build`; confirm the binary inside each uploaded
216	  macOS archive is actually the signed one (not a rebuilt copy).

1670	## 23. Glossary
1671	
1672	- **Run** — a single invocation of `deadreckon run <goal>`. Has a `run_id` (UUID), a `task_key` (slug + hash of goal), and a `scope` (slug + hash of repo path). Materialized in `~/.deadreckon/runstate/<scope>/runs/<run_id>/`.
1673	- **Scope** — `"<basename>-<fnv1a32-hex>"` of the canonical run-root path (git root or env var). Identifies a worktree.
1674	- **Task key** — `"<slug-of-goal>-<fnv1a32-hex>"`. Multiple runs of the same goal share a task key and a lock.

1042	### 12.3 What `kill` cannot do
1043	
1044	`kill` cannot reach directly into another process's in-memory cancellation token, so it bridges across processes with a **durable cancel marker**: `kill` writes `cancel.marker` under the run root before signaling child PIDs, and the running turn loop's `CancelMarkerGuard` polls for it (~50 ms) and trips the run-level `CancellationToken` while a provider call is in flight. Killing the children additionally makes the provider/sandbox error out, which the loop also propagates as a failure. The marker path means a cross-process `kill` deterministically stops the loop and records killed status through events, rather than relying solely on child-process death.
1045

180	#[derive(Debug)]
181	struct ResolvedCliBinary {
182	    program: PathBuf,
183	    read_allowlist: Vec<PathBuf>,
184	}
185	
186	fn resolve_cli_binary(binary: &str) -> ResolvedCliBinary {
187	    let configured = PathBuf::from(binary);
188	    let located = if configured.components().count() > 1 || configured.is_absolute() {
189	        configured
190	    } else {
191	        which::which(binary).unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from(binary))
192	    };
193	    let canonical = located.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| located.clone());
194	    let mut read_allowlist = Vec::new();
195	    push_existing_parent_roots(&mut read_allowlist, &located);
196	    push_existing_parent_roots(&mut read_allowlist, &canonical);
197	    if let Ok(canonical_parent) = canonical.parent().unwrap_or(&canonical).canonicalize() {
198	        push_if_exists(&mut read_allowlist, canonical_parent);
199	    }
200	    if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from) {
201	        for root in [".bun", ".local", ".npm-global", ".opencode"] {
202	            push_if_exists(&mut read_allowlist, home.join(root));
203	        }
204	    }
205	    dedup_paths(&mut read_allowlist);
206	    ResolvedCliBinary {
207	        program: canonical,
208	        read_allowlist,
209	    }
210	}
211	
212	fn cli_provider_write_allowlist(provider: &str) -> Vec<PathBuf> {
213	    let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from) else {
214	        return Vec::new();
215	    };
216	    if let Ok(registry) = ProviderRegistry::builtin()
217	        && let Some(descriptor) = registry.get(provider)
218	    {
219	        let mut paths = descriptor
220	            .sandbox_writes
221	            .iter()
222	            .map(|path| expand_home_path(path, &home))
223	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
224	        dedup_paths(&mut paths);
225	        return paths;
226	    }
227	    let mut paths = Vec::new();
228	    if provider.contains("codex") {
229	        paths.push(home.join(".codex"));
230	    }
231	    if provider.contains("claude") {
232	        paths.push(home.join(".claude"));
233	    }
234	    paths
235	}
236	
237	fn expand_home_path(path: &Path, home: &Path) -> PathBuf {
238	    if path == Path::new("~") {
239	        return home.to_path_buf();
240	    }
241	    if let Ok(rest) = path.strip_prefix("~") {
242	        return home.join(rest);
243	    }
244	    path.to_path_buf()
245	}
246	
247	fn push_existing_parent_roots(paths: &mut Vec<PathBuf>, path: &Path) {
248	    push_if_exists(paths, path);
249	    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
250	        push_if_exists(paths, parent);
251	    }
252	    if let Some(home) = std::env::var_os("HOME").map(PathBuf::from) {
253	        for root in [".bun", ".local", ".npm-global", ".opencode"] {
254	            let candidate = home.join(root);
255	            if path.starts_with(&candidate) {
256	                push_if_exists(paths, candidate);
257	            }
258	        }
259	    }
260	}
261	
262	fn push_if_exists(paths: &mut Vec<PathBuf>, path: impl Into<PathBuf>) {
263	    let path = path.into();
264	    if path.exists() {
265	        paths.push(path);
266	    }
267	}
268	
269	fn dedup_paths(paths: &mut Vec<PathBuf>) {
270	    paths.sort();
271	    paths.dedup();
272	}
273	
274	pub(crate) async fn write_output(path: Option<&PathBuf>, output: &CliOutput) -> Result<()> {
275	    let Some(path) = path else {
276	        return Ok(());
277	    };
278	    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
279	        tokio::fs::create_dir_all(parent)
280	            .await
281	            .map_err(|source| ProviderError::Io {
282	                path: parent.display().to_string(),
283	                source,
284	            })?;
285	    }
286	    let body = format!("{}\n{}", output.stdout, output.stderr);
287	    tokio::fs::write(path, body)
288	        .await
289	        .map_err(|source| ProviderError::Io {
290	            path: path.display().to_string(),
291	            source,
292	        })
293	}
294	
295	pub(crate) fn ensure_success(provider: &str, output: &CliOutput) -> Result<()> {
296	    if output.status_code == Some(0) {
297	        return Ok(());
298	    }
299	    Err(ProviderError::Cli {
300	        provider: provider.to_string(),
301	        detail: format!(
302	            "subprocess exited with {:?}: {}{}",
303	            output.status_code, output.stdout, output.stderr
304	        ),
305	    })
306	}

12	pub fn read_config(path: &Path) -> Result<ProviderConfigFile> {
13	    match std::fs::read_to_string(path) {
14	        Ok(raw) => {
15	            let mut config: ProviderConfigFile =
16	                toml::from_str(&raw).map_err(|source| ProviderError::Toml {
17	                    path: path.display().to_string(),
18	                    source,
19	                })?;
20	            if config.default_provider.is_none() {
21	                config.default_provider = defaults_provider(&raw);
22	            }
23	            Ok(config)
24	        }
25	        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(ProviderConfigFile {
26	            default_provider: None,
27	            fallback: None,
28	            providers: BTreeMap::new(),
29	        }),
30	        Err(source) => Err(ProviderError::Io {
31	            path: path.display().to_string(),
32	            source,
33	        }),
34	    }
35	}
36	
37	fn defaults_provider(raw: &str) -> Option<String> {
38	    let root: toml::Value = toml::from_str(raw).ok()?;
39	    root.as_table()?
40	        .get("defaults")?
41	        .as_table()?
42	        .get("provider")?
43	        .as_str()
44	        .map(ToString::to_string)
45	}

47	#[cfg(test)]
48	pub(crate) fn builtin_entries() -> Result<BTreeMap<String, ProviderEntry>> {

50	}

52	pub(crate) fn provider_entries_from_registry(
53	    registry: &ProviderRegistry,
54	) -> BTreeMap<String, ProviderEntry> {
55	    registry
56	        .iter()
57	        .map(|descriptor| {
58	            (
59	                descriptor.id.clone(),
60	                provider_entry_from_descriptor(descriptor),
61	            )
62	        })
63	        .collect()
64	}

66	pub(crate) fn provider_entry_from_descriptor(descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor) -> ProviderEntry {
67	    let default_model = if descriptor.kind == DescriptorKind::Cli {
68	        None
69	    } else if descriptor.id == "openai-compatible" {
70	        env::var("OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_MODEL")
71	            .ok()
72	            .or_else(|| descriptor.default_model.clone())
73	    } else {
74	        descriptor.default_model.clone()
75	    };
76	    let default_endpoint = if descriptor.id == "openai-compatible" {
77	        env::var("OPENAI_COMPATIBLE_BASE_URL")
78	            .ok()
79	            .or_else(|| descriptor.default_endpoint.clone())
80	    } else {
81	        descriptor.default_endpoint.clone()
82	    };
83	    let default_model_pricing = default_model
84	        .as_deref()
85	        .and_then(|model| {
86	            descriptor
87	                .model_catalog
88	                .iter()
89	                .find(|entry| entry.id == model)
90	        })
91	        .or_else(|| descriptor.model_catalog.first());
92	    ProviderEntry {
93	        kind: Some(kind_from_name(&descriptor.id)),
94	        api_key: None,
95	        api_key_env: descriptor.auth.env_var.clone(),
96	        base_url: default_endpoint,
97	        model: default_model,
98	        input_cost_per_million: default_model_pricing.and_then(|entry| entry.input_per_million),
99	        output_cost_per_million: default_model_pricing.and_then(|entry| entry.output_per_million),
100	        binary: descriptor.default_binary.clone(),
101	        extra_args: Vec::new(),
102	    }
103	}

107	        base.kind = entry.kind;
108	    }
109	    if entry.api_key.is_some() {
110	        base.api_key = entry.api_key;
111	    }
112	    if entry.api_key_env.is_some() {
113	        base.api_key_env = entry.api_key_env;
114	    }
115	    if entry.base_url.is_some() {
116	        base.base_url = entry.base_url;
117	    }
118	    if entry.model.is_some() {
119	        base.model = entry.model;
120	    }
121	    if entry.input_cost_per_million.is_some() {
122	        base.input_cost_per_million = entry.input_cost_per_million;
123	    }
124	    if entry.output_cost_per_million.is_some() {
125	        base.output_cost_per_million = entry.output_cost_per_million;
126	    }
127	    if entry.binary.is_some() {
128	        base.binary = entry.binary;
129	    }
130	    if !entry.extra_args.is_empty() {
131	        base.extra_args = entry.extra_args;
132	    }
133	}
134	
135	pub(crate) fn apply_catalog_to_provider_entry(
136	    provider_name: &str,
137	    entry: &mut ProviderEntry,
138	    registry: &ProviderRegistry,
139	    catalog_override: Option<&ModelCatalogOverride>,
140	) -> Option<ResolvedCatalogEntry> {
141	    let model = entry.model.as_deref()?;
142	    let descriptor_entry = descriptor_for_entry(provider_name, entry, registry)
143	        .and_then(|descriptor| model_entry_for_model(&descriptor.model_catalog, model));
144	    let selected = catalog_override
145	        .and_then(|catalog| catalog.entry_for_model(model))
146	        .map(|entry| (entry, CatalogEntrySource::Seam))
147	        .or_else(|| descriptor_entry.map(|entry| (entry, CatalogEntrySource::Catalog)))?;
148	    let (model_entry, source) = selected;
149	    if let Some(input) = model_entry.input_per_million {
150	        entry.input_cost_per_million = Some(input);
151	    }
152	    if let Some(output) = model_entry.output_per_million {
153	        entry.output_cost_per_million = Some(output);
154	    }
155	    Some(ResolvedCatalogEntry {
156	        context_window: model_entry.context_window,
157	        source,
158	    })
159	}
160	
161	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
162	pub(crate) struct ResolvedCatalogEntry {
163	    pub(crate) context_window: Option<u32>,
164	    pub(crate) source: CatalogEntrySource,
165	}
166	
167	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
168	pub(crate) enum CatalogEntrySource {
169	    Catalog,
170	    Seam,
171	}
172	
173	fn descriptor_for_entry<'a>(
174	    provider_name: &str,
175	    entry: &ProviderEntry,
176	    registry: &'a ProviderRegistry,
177	) -> Option<&'a ProviderDescriptor> {
178	    let descriptor_id = match entry.kind.as_ref() {
179	        Some(ProviderKind::Anthropic) => Some("anthropic"),
180	        Some(ProviderKind::OpenAi) => Some("openai"),
181	        Some(ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible) => Some("openai-compatible"),
182	        Some(ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode) => Some("cli:claude-code"),
183	        Some(ProviderKind::CliCodex) => Some("cli:codex"),
184	        Some(ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke) => Some("smoke"),
185	        Some(ProviderKind::Generic(id)) => Some(id.as_str()),
186	        None => None,
187	    };
188	    descriptor_id
189	        .and_then(|id| registry.get(id))
190	        .or_else(|| registry.get(provider_name))
191	}
192	
193	fn model_entry_for_model<'a>(catalog: &'a [ModelEntry], model: &str) -> Option<&'a ModelEntry> {
194	    catalog
195	        .iter()
196	        .find(|entry| entry.id == model || entry.aliases.iter().any(|alias| alias == model))
197	}
198	
199	pub(crate) fn kind_from_name(name: &str) -> ProviderKind {
200	    match name {
201	        "anthropic" => ProviderKind::Anthropic,
202	        "openai" => ProviderKind::OpenAi,
203	        "openai-compatible" | "openrouter" | "llama-cpp" => ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible,
204	        "cli:claude-code" | "cli-claude-code" => ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode,
205	        "cli:codex" | "cli-codex" => ProviderKind::CliCodex,
206	        "smoke" => ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke,
207	        _ => ProviderKind::Generic(name.to_string()),
208	    }
209	}
210
