3	pub(crate) async fn init_command(
4	    provider: Option<String>,
5	    api_key: Option<String>,
6	    base_url: Option<String>,
7	    max_spend: f64,
8	    sandbox: String,
9	    no_confirm: bool,
10	    no_completion: bool,
11	) -> Result<()> {
12	    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
13	    fs::create_dir_all(paths.home())?;
14	    let registry = ProviderRegistry::with_overrides(paths.home())?;
15	    let provider = match provider {
16	        Some(provider) => provider,
17	        None if no_confirm => preferred_init_subscription_cli_provider(&registry)
18	            .unwrap_or_else(|| "anthropic".to_string()),
19	        None => prompt_provider()?,
20	    };
21	    provider_setup_selection(
22	        &paths,
23	        setup::ProviderSetupRequest {
24	            role: setup::SetupProviderRoleRef::ConfigDefault,
25	            explicit_provider: Some(&provider),
26	            explicit_model: None,
27	            config_default_provider: None,
28	            config_doc_provider: None,
29	            run_provider: None,
30	            auto_subscription_provider: None,
31	            built_in_default_provider: Some("anthropic"),
32	            use_router_default: false,
33	            allow_auto_subscription: true,
34	            require_usable_route: false,
35	        },
36	    )?;
37	    let api_key = api_key.or_else(|| {
38	        if provider.starts_with("cli:") {
39	            None
40	        } else {
41	            prompt::open("provider API key (leave blank to use env var): ", None).ok()
42	        }
43	    });
44	    let config = init_config_text(
45	        &provider,
46	        api_key.as_deref(),
47	        base_url.as_deref(),
48	        max_spend,
49	        &sandbox,
50	    );
51	    fs::write(paths.config_path(), config)?;
52	    let provider_setup = provider_setup_selection(
53	        &paths,
54	        setup::ProviderSetupRequest {
55	            role: setup::SetupProviderRoleRef::ConfigDefault,
56	            explicit_provider: Some(&provider),
57	            explicit_model: None,
58	            config_default_provider: None,
59	            config_doc_provider: None,
60	            run_provider: None,
61	            auto_subscription_provider: None,
62	            built_in_default_provider: Some("anthropic"),
63	            use_router_default: false,
64	            allow_auto_subscription: true,
65	            require_usable_route: false,
66	        },
67	    )?;
68	    println!("{} {}", ui_ok("wrote"), paths.config_path().display());
69	    print_provider_setup_rows(&[provider_setup]);
70	    let doctor_summary = super::doctor::doctor_setup_summary().await?;
71	    let completion_status = if no_completion {
72	        "skipped by --no-completion".to_string()
73	    } else {
74	        super::completion::try_install_completion_after_init()
75	    };
76	    print!(
77	        "{}",
78	        init_completion_surface(
79	            &paths,
80	            &provider,
81	            &sandbox,
82	            &completion_status,
83	            &doctor_summary,
84	        )
85	        .render_plain(!completion_hints_enabled(false))
86	    );
87	    Ok(())
88	}
89	
90	fn init_completion_surface(
91	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
92	    provider: &str,
93	    sandbox: &str,
94	    completion_status: &str,
95	    doctor_summary: &super::doctor::DoctorSetupSummary,
96	) -> VerdictSurface {
97	    let (kind, why, primary, secondary) = if doctor_summary.has_blocking_issues() {
98	        (
99	            VerdictKind::Blocked,
100	            "Initialization wrote the config, but setup verification found blocking issues; run doctor before starting managed work.",
101	            "deadreckon doctor",
102	            vec![("Secondary", "deadreckon run \"describe the coding goal\"")],
103	        )
104	    } else {
105	        (
106	            VerdictKind::Completed,
107	            "Initialization completed; the next step is to start a managed run from this workspace.",
108	            "deadreckon run \"describe the coding goal\"",
109	            vec![("Secondary", "deadreckon doctor")],
110	        )
111	    };
112	    VerdictSurface::try_new(
113	        kind,
114	        "init",
115	        None,
116	        ExplanationPanel::new(
117	            "DeadReckon wrote the local configuration and checked the provider setup.",
118	            why,
119	            vec![
120	                ("config", paths.config_path().display().to_string()),
121	                ("provider", provider.to_string()),
122	                ("sandbox", sandbox.to_string()),
123	                ("doctor", doctor_summary.evidence_detail()),
124	                ("completion", completion_status.to_string()),
125	            ],
126	        ),
127	        vec![("Recommended", primary)],
128	        secondary,
129	    )
130	    .expect("init verdict surface must be valid")
131	}
132	
133	fn preferred_init_subscription_cli_provider(registry: &ProviderRegistry) -> Option<String> {

136	        .filter(|descriptor| {

139	                && descriptor
140	                    .default_binary
141	                    .as_deref()
142	                    .is_some_and(command_exists)
143	        })
144	        .map(|descriptor| descriptor.id.clone())
145	        .next()
146	}

197	pub fn workspace_scope(start: &Path) -> Result<String> {
198	    let root = env::var_os("DEADRECKON_SCOPE_ROOT")
199	        .map(PathBuf::from)
200	        .or_else(|| find_git_root(start))
201	        .unwrap_or_else(|| start.to_path_buf());
202	    let canonical = root.canonicalize().map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
203	        path: root.clone(),
204	        source,
205	    })?;
206	    let base = canonical
207	        .file_name()
208	        .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
209	        .map(sanitize_slug)
210	        .filter(|name| !name.is_empty())
211	        .unwrap_or_else(|| "workspace".to_string());
212	    Ok(format!(
213	        "{base}-{:08x}",
214	        fnv1a32(canonical.to_string_lossy().as_ref())
215	    ))
216	}
217	
218	pub fn task_key(goal: &str) -> String {
219	    let trimmed = goal.trim();
220	    let mut stem = sanitize_slug(trimmed);
221	    if stem.len() > 48 {
222	        stem.truncate(48);
223	        stem = stem.trim_end_matches('-').to_string();
224	    }
225	    if stem.is_empty() {
226	        stem = "task".to_string();
227	    }
228	    format!("{stem}-{:08x}", fnv1a32(trimmed))
229	}
230	
231	pub fn sanitize_slug(input: &str) -> String {
232	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(input.len());
233	    let mut last_dash = false;
234	    for ch in input.chars() {
235	        let next = if ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
236	            last_dash = false;
237	            Some(ch.to_ascii_lowercase())
238	        } else if matches!(ch, '-' | '_' | ' ' | '.') {
239	            if last_dash {
240	                None
241	            } else {
242	                last_dash = true;
243	                Some('-')
244	            }
245	        } else {
246	            None
247	        };
248	        if let Some(ch) = next {
249	            out.push(ch);
250	        }
251	    }
252	    out.trim_matches('-').to_string()
253	}
254	
255	fn find_git_root(start: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
256	    let mut cursor = if start.is_file() {
257	        start.parent()?.to_path_buf()
258	    } else {
259	        start.to_path_buf()
260	    };
261	    loop {
262	        if cursor.join(".git").exists() {
263	            return Some(cursor);
264	        }
265	        if !cursor.pop() {
266	            return None;
267	        }
268	    }
269	}
270	
271	fn fnv1a32(input: &str) -> u32 {
272	    let mut hash = 0x811c_9dc5u32;
273	    for byte in input.as_bytes() {
274	        hash ^= u32::from(*byte);
275	        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0100_0193);
276	    }
277	    hash
278	}

180	pub fn create_run(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, options: RunOptions) -> Result<PipelineState> {
181	    let scope = workspace_scope(&options.cwd)?;
182	    let task_key = task_key(&options.goal);
183	    let run_id = options
184	        .run_id
185	        .unwrap_or_else(|| Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string());
186	    let run_root = paths.run_root(&scope, &run_id);
187	    let codebase = options.codebase.unwrap_or_else(CodebaseRecord::fresh);
188	    let working_dir = working_dir_for_codebase(&run_root, &codebase);
189	    fs::create_dir_all(&working_dir).with_path(&working_dir)?;
190	    fs::create_dir_all(run_root.join("snapshots")).with_path(run_root.join("snapshots"))?;
191	    let gate_dir = run_root.join("gate");
192	    fs::create_dir_all(&gate_dir).with_path(&gate_dir)?;
193	    fs::write(gate_dir.join("nonce"), Uuid::new_v4().simple().to_string())
194	        .with_path(gate_dir.join("nonce"))?;
195	
196	    // AS-BUILT §3: the binary owns deterministic paths while the skill stays a
197	    // markdown subprocess boundary under the source tree.
198	    let skill_path = PathBuf::from(SOURCE_ROOT)
199	        .join("skills")
200	        .join(&options.skill_name)
201	        .join("SKILL.md");
202	    let now = Utc::now();
203	    let mut state = PipelineState {
204	        version: STATE_VERSION,
205	        goal: options.goal,
206	        task_key,
207	        run_id,
208	        scope,
209	        status: RunStatus::Pending,
210	        current_phase_id: PhaseId(0),
211	        started_at: now,
212	        updated_at: now,
213	        cwd: options.cwd,
214	        run_root,
215	        working_dir,
216	        skill_name: options.skill_name,
217	        skill_path,
218	        sandbox: options.sandbox,
219	        provider: options.provider,
220	        max_spend_usd: options.max_spend_usd,
221	        max_wall_seconds: options.max_wall_seconds,
222	        total_spend_usd: 0.0,
223	        total_wall_seconds: 0.0,
224	        turn: 0,
225	        pause_reason: None,
226	        failure_reason: None,
227	        child_pids: Vec::new(),
228	        killed_at: None,
229	        promoted_library_dir: None,
230	        phases: default_phases(now),
231	    };
232	    state.set_phase_status(PhaseId(0), PhaseStatus::Planned)?;
233	    save_state(&state)?;
234	    write_codebase_record(&state.working_dir, &codebase)?;
235	    ensure_docs_started(&state)?;
236	    write_current_pointer(paths, &state)?;
237	    Ok(state)
238	}

286	pub fn spend_summary(state: &PipelineState) -> Result<SpendSummary> {
287	    let path = state.run_root.join("spend.jsonl");
288	    let raw = match fs::read_to_string(&path) {
289	        Ok(raw) => raw,
290	        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
291	            return Ok(SpendSummary {
292	                total_usd: state.total_spend_usd,
293	                wall_seconds: state.total_wall_seconds,
294	                ..SpendSummary::default()
295	            });
296	        }
297	        Err(source) => {
298	            return Err(DeadreckonError::Io { path, source });
299	        }
300	    };
301	    let mut summary = SpendSummary::default();
302	    for line in raw.lines().filter(|line| !line.trim().is_empty()) {
303	        let record: SpendRecord =
304	            serde_json::from_str(line).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Json {
305	                path: path.clone(),
306	                source,
307	            })?;
308	        summary.total_usd = record.total_cost_usd;
309	        summary.input_tokens = summary.input_tokens.saturating_add(record.input_tokens);
310	        summary.output_tokens = summary.output_tokens.saturating_add(record.output_tokens);
311	        summary.wall_seconds += record.wall_time_seconds.unwrap_or(0.0);
312	        summary.turns = summary.turns.saturating_add(1);
313	        if record.subscription {
314	            summary.subscription_turns = summary.subscription_turns.saturating_add(1);
315	        }
316	        summary.any_subscription_turn |= record.subscription;
317	        summary.any_estimated_turn |= record.estimated;
318	    }
319	    if summary.wall_seconds == 0.0 {
320	        summary.wall_seconds = state.total_wall_seconds;
321	    }
322	    if summary.total_usd == 0.0 {
323	        summary.total_usd = state.total_spend_usd;
324	    }
325	    Ok(summary)
326	}

354	
355	pub fn find_run_state_path(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, run_id: &str) -> Result<PathBuf> {
356	    let run_id = run_id.trim();
357	    if run_id.is_empty() {
358	        return Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
359	            "run id prefix cannot be empty".to_string(),
360	        ));
361	    }
362	    let root = paths.runstate_dir();
363	    if !root.exists() {
364	        return Err(DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!("run {run_id}")));
365	    }
366	    let mut prefix_matches = Vec::new();
367	    // Bound the walk to the runstate layout depth (run dir -> state.json), matching
368	    // list_runs. Without this, resolving one run descends into sibling runs' worktree
369	    // and artifact subtrees (thousands of files) on every attach tick.
370	    for entry in WalkDir::new(&root)
371	        .max_depth(4)
372	        .into_iter()
373	        .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
374	    {
375	        if !entry.file_type().is_file() || entry.file_name() != "state.json" {
376	            continue;
377	        }
378	        let candidate = entry.path();
379	        let Some(candidate_run_id) = candidate
380	            .parent()
381	            .and_then(Path::file_name)
382	            .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
383	        else {
384	            continue;
385	        };
386	        if candidate_run_id == run_id {
387	            return Ok(candidate.to_path_buf());
388	        }
389	        if candidate_run_id.starts_with(run_id) {
390	            prefix_matches.push((candidate_run_id.to_string(), candidate.to_path_buf()));
391	        }
392	    }
393	    match prefix_matches.len() {
394	        1 => Ok(prefix_matches.remove(0).1),
395	        0 => Err(DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!("run {run_id}"))),
396	        _ => {
397	            let matches = prefix_matches
398	                .into_iter()
399	                .map(|(id, _)| id)
400	                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
401	                .join(", ");
402	            Err(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
403	                "ambiguous run id prefix {run_id}; matches {matches}"
404	            )))
405	        }
406	    }
407	}
408	
409	pub fn load_run(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, run_id: &str) -> Result<PipelineState> {
410	    let path = find_run_state_path(paths, run_id)?;
411	    load_state(&path)
412	}
413	
414	pub fn list_runs(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, scope_filter: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<RunListEntry>> {
415	    let root = paths.runstate_dir();
416	    if !root.exists() {
417	        return Ok(Vec::new());
418	    }
419	    let mut runs = Vec::new();
420	    for entry in WalkDir::new(&root)
421	        .max_depth(4)
422	        .into_iter()
423	        .filter_map(std::result::Result::ok)
424	    {
425	        if !entry.file_type().is_file() || entry.file_name() != "state.json" {
426	            continue;
427	        }
428	        let state = load_state(entry.path())?;
429	        if scope_filter.is_some_and(|scope| scope != state.scope) {
430	            continue;
431	        }
432	        runs.push(RunListEntry {
433	            run_id: state.run_id,
434	            scope: state.scope,
435	            goal: state.goal,
436	            status: state.status,
437	            updated_at: state.updated_at,
438	            state_path: entry.path().to_path_buf(),
439	        });
440	    }
441	    runs.sort_by(|left, right| right.updated_at.cmp(&left.updated_at));
442	    Ok(runs)
443	}
444	
445	pub(crate) fn atomic_write_json<T: Serialize>(path: &Path, value: &T) -> Result<()> {
446	    let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
447	        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("path has no parent: {}", path.display()))
448	    })?;
449	    fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
450	    let mut temp = NamedTempFile::new_in(parent).with_path(parent)?;
451	    serde_json::to_writer_pretty(&mut temp, value).with_json_path(path)?;
452	    temp.write_all(b"\n").with_path(path)?;
453	    temp.as_file_mut().sync_all().with_path(path)?;
454	    persist_temp(temp, path)
455	}
456	
457	fn persist_temp(temp: NamedTempFile, path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
458	    match temp.persist(path) {
459	        Ok(_) => Ok(()),
460	        Err(err) => Err(DeadreckonError::Io {
461	            path: path.to_path_buf(),
462	            source: err.error,
463	        }),
464	    }
465	}
466	
467	pub fn append_json_line<T: Serialize>(path: &Path, value: &T) -> Result<()> {
468	    let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(|| {
469	        DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!("path has no parent: {}", path.display()))
470	    })?;
471	    fs::create_dir_all(parent).with_path(parent)?;
472	    let mut line = Vec::new();
473	    serde_json::to_writer(&mut line, value).with_json_path(path)?;
474	    line.push(b'\n');
475	    let mut file = File::options()
476	        .create(true)
477	        .append(true)
478	        .open(path)
479	        .with_path(path)?;
480	    file.write_all(&line).with_path(path)?;
481	    file.sync_all().with_path(path)
482	}

209	        .map(sanitize_slug)

211	        .unwrap_or_else(|| "workspace".to_string());
212	    Ok(format!(
213	        "{base}-{:08x}",
214	        fnv1a32(canonical.to_string_lossy().as_ref())
215	    ))
216	}
217	
218	pub fn task_key(goal: &str) -> String {
219	    let trimmed = goal.trim();
220	    let mut stem = sanitize_slug(trimmed);
221	    if stem.len() > 48 {
222	        stem.truncate(48);
223	        stem = stem.trim_end_matches('-').to_string();
224	    }
225	    if stem.is_empty() {
226	        stem = "task".to_string();
227	    }
228	    format!("{stem}-{:08x}", fnv1a32(trimmed))
229	}
230	
231	pub fn sanitize_slug(input: &str) -> String {
232	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(input.len());
233	    let mut last_dash = false;
234	    for ch in input.chars() {
235	        let next = if ch.is_ascii_alphanumeric() {
236	            last_dash = false;
237	            Some(ch.to_ascii_lowercase())
238	        } else if matches!(ch, '-' | '_' | ' ' | '.') {
239	            if last_dash {
240	                None
241	            } else {
242	                last_dash = true;
243	                Some('-')
244	            }
245	        } else {
246	            None
247	        };
248	        if let Some(ch) = next {
249	            out.push(ch);
250	        }
251	    }
252	    out.trim_matches('-').to_string()
253	}
254	
255	fn find_git_root(start: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
256	    let mut cursor = if start.is_file() {
257	        start.parent()?.to_path_buf()
258	    } else {
259	        start.to_path_buf()
260	    };
261	    loop {
262	        if cursor.join(".git").exists() {
263	            return Some(cursor);
264	        }
265	        if !cursor.pop() {
266	            return None;
267	        }
268	    }
269	}
270	
271	fn fnv1a32(input: &str) -> u32 {
272	    let mut hash = 0x811c_9dc5u32;
273	    for byte in input.as_bytes() {
274	        hash ^= u32::from(*byte);
275	        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0100_0193);
276	    }
277	    hash
278	}

124	
125	    fn from_config_with_model_and_registry(
126	        config: ProviderConfigFile,
127	        override_provider: Option<&str>,
128	        override_model: Option<&str>,
129	        registry: &ProviderRegistry,
130	        catalog_override: Option<&ModelCatalogOverride>,
131	    ) -> Result<Self> {
132	        let mut providers = provider_entries_from_registry(registry);
133	        for (name, entry) in config.providers {
134	            if let Some(base) = providers.get_mut(&name) {
135	                merge_provider_entry(base, entry);
136	            } else {
137	                providers.insert(name, entry);
138	            }
139	        }
140	
141	        let route_names = if let Some(provider) = override_provider {
142	            vec![provider.to_string()]
143	        } else {
144	            configured_route_names(config.default_provider, config.fallback)
145	        };
146	
147	        let mut routes = Vec::new();
148	        let mut context_windows = BTreeMap::new();
149	        let mut context_window_sources = BTreeMap::new();
150	        for name in route_names {
151	            let Some(mut entry) = providers.remove(&name) else {
152	                return Err(ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!(
153	                    "unknown provider route {name}"
154	                )));
155	            };
156	            if let Some(model) = override_model {
157	                entry.model = Some(model.to_string());
158	            }
159	            let catalog_entry =
160	                apply_catalog_to_provider_entry(&name, &mut entry, registry, catalog_override);
161	            let context_window = catalog_entry.and_then(|entry| entry.context_window);
162	            let context_window_source = catalog_entry.and_then(|entry| {
163	                entry.context_window.map(|_| match entry.source {
164	                    CatalogEntrySource::Catalog => ModelContextWindowSource::Catalog,
165	                    CatalogEntrySource::Seam => ModelContextWindowSource::Seam,
166	                })
167	            });
168	            let kind = entry.kind.unwrap_or_else(|| kind_from_name(&name));
169	            entry.kind = Some(kind.clone());
170	            routes.push(build_provider(name.clone(), kind, entry, registry)?);
171	            context_windows.insert(name.clone(), context_window);
172	            context_window_sources.insert(name, context_window_source);
173	        }
174	
175	        Ok(Self {
176	            routes,
177	            context_windows,
178	            context_window_sources,
179	        })
180	    }

232	    pub async fn complete(&self, request: &ProviderRequest) -> Result<ProviderResponse> {
233	        let mut failures = Vec::new();
234	        for route in &self.routes {
235	            if !route.has_credential() {
236	                failures.push(format!("{}: missing credential", route.name()));
237	                continue;
238	            }
239	            match route.complete(request).await {
240	                Ok(response) => return Ok(response),
241	                Err(err) => failures.push(format!("{}: {err}", route.name())),
242	            }
243	        }
244	        Err(ProviderError::NoRoute(failures.join("; ")))
245	    }
246	
247	    pub fn estimate_for_route(
248	        &self,
249	        provider_name: Option<&str>,
250	        usage: ProviderUsage,
251	    ) -> Result<SpendEstimate> {
252	        let route = provider_name
253	            .and_then(|name| self.routes.iter().find(|route| route.name() == name))
254	            .or_else(|| self.routes.first())
255	            .ok_or_else(|| ProviderError::NoRoute("empty provider route".to_string()))?;
256	        Ok(route.estimate_spend(usage))
257	    }
258	}
259	
260	fn configured_route_names(
261	    default_provider: Option<String>,
262	    fallback: Option<Vec<String>>,
263	) -> Vec<String> {
264	    let mut route_names = Vec::new();
265	    if let Some(default_provider) = default_provider {
266	        route_names.push(default_provider);
267	    }
268	    if let Some(fallback) = fallback {
269	        for provider in fallback {
270	            if !route_names.iter().any(|route| route == &provider) {
271	                route_names.push(provider);
272	            }
273	        }
274	    }
275	    if route_names.is_empty() {
276	        route_names.extend([
277	            "cli:claude-code".to_string(),
278	            "cli:codex".to_string(),
279	            "anthropic".to_string(),
280	            "openai".to_string(),
281	            "openai-compatible".to_string(),
282	        ]);
283	    }
284	    route_names
285	}
286	
287	fn build_provider(
288	    name: String,
289	    kind: ProviderKind,
290	    entry: ProviderEntry,
291	    registry: &ProviderRegistry,
292	) -> Result<Box<dyn Provider>> {
293	    match kind {
294	        ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode => Ok(Box::new(CliClaudeCodeProvider::new(name, entry))),
295	        ProviderKind::CliCodex => Ok(Box::new(CliCodexProvider::new(name, entry))),
296	        ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke => Ok(Box::new(ScriptedSmokeProvider::new())),
297	        ProviderKind::Anthropic | ProviderKind::OpenAi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => {
298	            Ok(Box::new(ProviderAdapter::new(name, kind, entry)))
299	        }
300	        ProviderKind::Generic(id) => {
301	            let descriptor = registry
302	                .get(&id)
303	                .or_else(|| registry.get(&name))
304	                .ok_or_else(|| {
305	                    ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!("generic provider {id} has no descriptor"))
306	                })?;
307	            if descriptor.kind != DescriptorKind::Cli {
308	                return Err(ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!(
309	                    "generic provider {id} is not a cli descriptor"
310	                )));
311	            }
312	            Ok(Box::new(GenericCliProvider::new(
313	                name,
314	                entry,
315	                descriptor.clone(),
316	            )?))
317	        }
318	    }
319	}

264	fn doctor_verdict_surface(report: &DoctorReport) -> VerdictSurface {
265	    let failed_count = report
266	        .findings
267	        .iter()
268	        .filter(|finding| finding.is_failed())
269	        .count();
270	    let warning_count = report
271	        .findings
272	        .iter()
273	        .filter(|finding| finding.status == "warning")
274	        .count();
275	    let kind = if failed_count == 0 {
276	        VerdictKind::Verified
277	    } else {
278	        VerdictKind::Blocked
279	    };
280	    let primary = doctor_primary_action(report);
281	    let secondary = doctor_secondary_actions(report, &primary)
282	        .into_iter()
283	        .map(|action| ("Secondary", action))
284	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
285	    VerdictSurface::try_new(
286	        kind,
287	        "doctor",
288	        None,
289	        doctor_explanation(report, failed_count, warning_count),
290	        vec![("Recommended", primary.as_str())],
291	        secondary,
292	    )
293	    .expect("doctor verdict surface must be valid")
294	}

296	fn doctor_explanation(
297	    report: &DoctorReport,
298	    failed_count: usize,
299	    warning_count: usize,
300	) -> ExplanationPanel {
301	    let what = if failed_count == 0 {
302	        format!(
303	            "Doctor checked {} setup areas and found no blocking setup failures.",
304	            report.findings.len()
305	        )
306	    } else {
307	        format!(
308	            "Doctor checked {} setup areas and found {failed_count} blocking setup issue(s).",
309	            report.findings.len()
310	        )

460	async fn collect_doctor_provider_ping(
461	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
462	    name: &str,
463	    kind_label: &str,
464	) -> Result<DoctorFinding> {
465	    let router = ProviderRouter::from_config_path(&paths.config_path(), Some(name))?;
466	    let request = ProviderRequest {
467	        prompt: "Reply with OK only.".to_string(),
468	        max_output_tokens: 8,
469	        cwd: None,

480	    .await

482	        Ok(Ok(response)) => Ok(DoctorFinding::passed(

487	            )),

5. **Verdict Surface (2026-06-02)** — one-verdict/one-Recommended-command contract across all outcome surfaces; burned down the FRIENDLINESS-AUDIT one-primary-action failures with a regression test.
6. **Seam conformance kit (2026-05-31)** — `examples/seams/`, `deadreckon seams validate`.
7. **Composable seams production release (2026-05-31)** — `[seams]` worker swapping (P1–P11), deterministic direct-API history compaction, adversarial gate-boundary tests, `--no-seams`.
8. **Navigable campaign attach (2026-05-31)** — live campaign ratatui TUI with sub-plan drill-in to plan/run attach.
9. **Decompose (2026-05-30)** — split the 40.6k-line `main.rs` into private `commands/`/`tui/` modules, behavior-preserving.
10–15. **Effortless, Campaign Orchestration, Tamper-Evident Gate, Production release posture, Plan Doc Consolidation (all 2026-05-28); Production command model (2026-05-27)** — friendliness contract pass, depth-2 campaign orchestration, hollow-pass tamper detection, consolidated `PLAN-*` docs, flat-but-grouped command model.

## (c) Conceptual model a user must understand (docs/CONCEPTS.md)

- **The loop is the product**: the agent CLI does the coding; deadreckon owns the boundary and decides when "done" actually means done.
- **Done contract in English**: `def-done` compiles a plain-English sentence into executable checks (`cargo_test`, `file_exists`, `content_match`, `build_success`, `shell`) in `acceptance.yaml`. Default when unconfigured: working dir exists and `cargo test` passes (if `Cargo.toml` present).
- **Anti-self-attestation watchdog**: a separate process, `dr-gate`, holds a run-local secret the agent process can't read and signs the acceptance marker; the agent literally cannot forge "done." Check failures mean another turn, not termination.
- **Isolation**: runs default to an isolated `git worktree` on a `dr/...` branch inside a sandbox; the real checkout changes only on `deadreckon apply`.
- **Durable runstate**: every turn writes state, spend, traces, provenance, snapshots — enabling attach from another terminal, kill, resume (from last completed tool boundary), per-turn undo, and audit.
- **Promoted artifact, not transcript**: accepted runs promote atomically to `RUN-NARRATIVE.md`, `RUN-DECISIONS.md`, `RUN-AS-BUILT.md`, `provenance.jsonl`, `manifest.json`.
- **Bring your own agent**: routes `cli:claude-code`, `cli:codex`, `cli:gemini`, `cli:copilot`, `cli:opencode`, `cli:pi`, plus BYOK `anthropic`/`openai`/`openai-compatible`, and keyless `--smoke`; `import` ingests other tools' history read-only.
- **Scaling shapes**: `chain` for ordered multi-step goals (each step has its own signed gate, stops at first failure); plans/orchestrate for parallel children; campaigns for N orchestrators on one task (depth-capped at 2).
- **The name is the contract**: dead reckoning — navigate by evidence, don't trust the final answer.

  printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

download() {
  url="$1"
  out="$2"
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$out"
  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    wget -qO "$out" "$url"
  else
    die "install curl or wget, then rerun this installer"
  fi
}

cleanup() {
  rm -rf "$tmp"
}

trap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM

(umask 077 && mkdir "$tmp") || die "could not create temp dir: $tmp"

printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: ${repo} ${tag}"
download "${base_url}/${asset}" "${tmp}/${asset}" || die "could not download ${base_url}/${asset}"

if download "${base_url}/SHA256SUMS" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS"; then
  if grep "  ${asset}\$" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS" > "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS.${asset}"; then
    if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      (cd "$tmp" && shasum -a 256 -c "SHA256SUMS.${asset}") \
        || die "checksum verification failed for ${asset}"
    elif command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      (cd "$tmp" && sha256sum -c "SHA256SUMS.${asset}") \
        || die "checksum verification failed for ${asset}"
    else
      printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: shasum/sha256sum not found; skipping checksum verification" >&2
    fi
  else
    printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: ${asset} was not listed in SHA256SUMS" >&2
  fi
else
  printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: could not download SHA256SUMS; skipping checksum verification" >&2
fi

sh "${tmp}/${asset}" "$@"

installed="${DEADRECKON_BIN:-${HOME}/.local/share/deadreckon/bin/deadreckon}"
if [ -x "$installed" ]; then
  bin="$installed"
elif command -v deadreckon >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  bin="deadreckon"
else
  bin="$installed"
fi

printf '\n%s\n' "deadreckon install: next"
printf '  %s\n' "${bin} doctor"
printf '  %s\n' "${bin} try"
printf '  %s\n' "${bin} start \"make a small safe change\""

```text
1	# deadreckon — Build Rider (V0)
2	
3	This rider holds the prescriptive constraints for the goal at
4	`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-05-10-1400-deadreckon-build-goal.md`.
5	Read it before writing code. Sections marked "do not violate" are hard constraints.
6	
7	**All paths in this document are absolute. Generated code, config, docs, and
8	verification scripts must use absolute paths or paths anchored to a single
9	known root (`/Users/gdc/deadreckon/` for source, `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`
10	for runtime state). No bare relative paths in user-visible artifacts.**
11	
12	## Product framing (decided — do not redesign)
13	
14	- **What it is.** A Rust CLI agent harness whose default flow is **unattended long-running coding tasks**. The user types one goal, hits enter, and the harness drives the task across hours of model time — sandboxed, crash-resumable, spend-capped, with full provenance.
15	- **What it isn't.** Not an editor, not a chat app, not an MCP framework, not a CI runner, not a kitchen-sink agent IDE.
16	- **Target user.** Solo developers and ≤ 10-person teams currently paying $200+/month per seat across Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, opencode, and still doing manual bookkeeping for spend, undo, and multi-agent coordination.
17	- **BYOK posture.** Multi-provider from day one, opencode-style. The user supplies keys; the harness never bills usage. V0 providers: Anthropic, OpenAI, plus an OpenAI-compatible shim (OpenRouter, llama.cpp, etc.).
18	- **Name.** **deadreckon.** Dead reckoning is navigation by integrating known motion from a fixed starting point — no GPS, no external check. The harness drives long-running agent work the same way: durable state at every turn, no live human in the loop, no live model attestation, reconstructable position after any crash.
19	
20	## Architecture (decided — do not redesign)
21	
22	Adopt these patterns from `/Users/gdc/Downloads/AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md`. Each
23	adoption cites the AS-BUILT section in a code comment near the implementation.
24	
25	- **Two-layer split.** Rust binary owns state, locks, sandboxes, gates, atomic file ops, sub-agent management. Agent-facing skill layer (markdown skills loaded at runtime) owns judgment, prose, orchestration. The skill is invoked as a sub-process; the binary never reaches into skill internals. (AS-BUILT §3)
26	- **Phase machine with on-disk state.** `state.json` per run, status enum (`pending|planned|executing|completed|failed`), gap-numbered phase IDs. (AS-BUILT §4)
27	- **Run pointer + run scoping.** `current/<task>.json` points at the active run per task; `runs/<run-id>/` carries durable state. Scope hash from git root or env var lets parallel worktrees coexist. (AS-BUILT §4)
28	- **Locks with heartbeats + PID liveness.** Process-held locks survive crash detection via PID-zero kill probe; stale locks reclaimable after timeout. (AS-BUILT §6)
29	- **Atomic promotion.** Work happens in `working/`; promoted atomically to `library/` only after a gate marker is written. (AS-BUILT §7)
30	- **Anti-self-attestation gates.** Acceptance markers (test pass, sandbox green, spend within cap) can only be written by an external runner and are validated by the binary against the run identity. The agent cannot self-mark a gate. (AS-BUILT §8, §17)
31	- **Sub-agent forking with context isolation.** Research-heavy or diagnostic-heavy sub-tasks run in forked subprocess agents; they return structured summaries to the parent. (AS-BUILT §10)
32	- **Bounded fix loops with rollback.** Every code mutation is backed up, build-checked, regression-checked, and rolled back on failure within a retry budget. (AS-BUILT §9)
33	
34	## Patterns to mine from Claude Code source (`/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/`)
35	
36	The Claude Code source is a working reference for the user-facing primitives
37	this harness needs. Read these subtrees before implementing the relevant
38	crate; cite the file in a code comment when adopting a pattern.
39	
40	- **Tool-use loop and turn structure** — `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/assistant/`. How the assistant runs a turn, schedules tool calls, handles streaming, and unwinds on errors. Inform `deadreckon-core`'s run loop.
41	- **Tool implementations and permission model** — `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/tools/`. Per-tool permission gates, parameter schemas, side-effect boundaries, the analogue of `--dangerously-skip-permissions`. Inform `deadreckon-core` tool dispatch, the platform-sandbox profile (filesystem/network/env scope), and the `--sandbox none` warning.
42	- **Task / coordinator orchestration** — `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/tasks/`, `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/coordinator/`. Multi-task supervision, sub-agent forking patterns. Inform `deadreckon`'s `run/attach/kill/resume`.
43	- **Upstream proxy / provider abstraction** — `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/upstreamproxy/`. How Claude Code shapes requests, handles streaming, retries, and tool-result feedback. Inform `deadreckon-providers`.
44	- **TUI patterns** — `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/src/ink/`. React-Ink reference for a streaming, attachable terminal UI; port idioms to `ratatui` rather than copying React.
45	- **Prompts and skill structure** — `/Users/gdc/claude-code-source-code/docs/prompts/`. Existing system prompt shapes, skill loading conventions. Inform `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/default-coding/SKILL.md`.
46	
47	**Rust adaptations (use these crates, no alternatives in V0):**
48	
49	- `tokio` — async runtime.
50	- `serde` + `serde_json` — state serialization.
51	- `nix` (Unix) + `fs2` — advisory file locking + PID liveness via `kill(pid, 0)`.
52	- `tracing` + `tracing-subscriber` — structured logs / observability.
53	- `clap` derive — CLI parsing.
54	- `ratatui` + `crossterm` — TUI.
55	- `reqwest` — HTTP client for provider calls.
56	- `which` — locate `sandbox-exec` / `bwrap` / `docker` binaries at preflight time. Sandbox backends shell out via `tokio::process::Command`; no Docker SDK dep.
57	- Cargo workspace: separate crates for `deadreckon-core`, `deadreckon-providers`, `deadreckon-sandbox`, `deadreckon` (bin).
58	
59	## Must-have unmet needs (V0 scope)
60	
61	Each implementation slice maps to ≥ 1 of these. Comment in the source where
62	each is implemented (e.g., `// REPORT.md: Live Context & Spend Meter`).
63	
64	1. **Live Context & Spend Meter** — `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/runstate/<scope>/runs/<id>/spend.jsonl` (durable per-turn telemetry); surfaces in TUI.
65	2. **Multi-Agent Worktree Coordination** — scopes + lock primitives let N agents run in parallel without conflict.
66	3. **Infinite Undo for Agent Edits** — `snapshots/turn-<N>/` per run; `deadreckon undo` restores to any prior turn.
67	4. **Prompt-to-Code Provenance Audit Trail** — `provenance.jsonl` per run; every file change carries `{ prompt_id, model, tool_call_id, timestamp, session_id, files: [...] }`.
68	5. **Cross-Tool State Sharing (read-only import)** — `deadreckon import claude-code|codex|cursor` reads `/Users/gdc/.claude/projects/`, `/Users/gdc/.codex/sessions/`, `/Users/gdc/.cursor/chats/`. No live bridging in V0.
69	6. **Agent Observability** — `traces.jsonl` per run (LLM calls, tool calls, retries, latency); exportable.
70	7. **Disposable Sandboxes** — platform-native per run by default (`sandbox-exec` on macOS, `bubblewrap` on Linux); `--sandbox auto|sandbox-exec|bwrap|docker|none` flag, default `auto`.
71	8. **Billing Guardrails** — `--max-spend <USD>` flag; mid-run pause when cap is hit; resume requires explicit user OK.
72	9. **Provider Routing / BYOK** — multi-provider with fallback chain configured in `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/config.toml`.
73	10. **Workspace Inventory & Run Queue** — `deadreckon list/attach/kill/resume` over `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/runstate/`.
74	
75	## V0 prescribed decisions (do not deliberate)
76	
77	These resolve the open options that would otherwise belong in a design doc.
78	
79	- **Sandbox primary.** Platform-native: `sandbox-exec` (Seatbelt) on macOS, `bubblewrap` (`bwrap`) on Linux. Flag `--sandbox auto|sandbox-exec|bwrap|docker|none`; default `auto` (auto-selects the platform-native backend). Docker is `--sandbox docker` opt-in for users who want it. Lima / Firecracker / E2B / Landlock are V1 candidates. No `bollard` dep — backends shell out via `tokio::process::Command`.
80	- **Plugin / skill language.** Markdown skills, Claude-Code-style. Loaded at runtime from `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/skills/`. WASM plugins are V1.
81	- **State store.** Plain JSON files, atomically written via temp+rename. SQLite cache is V1.
82	- **TUI framework.** `ratatui` + `crossterm`.
83	- **Provider abstraction.** Custom `Provider` trait per provider; one OpenAI-compatible shim that handles any compliant endpoint (lets users plug in OpenRouter, llama.cpp).
84

86

103	## Runtime state layout (`/Users/gdc/.deadreckon/`)
104

108	├── runstate/

121	
122	## CLI surface (must implement in V0)
123	
124	- `deadreckon run <goal> [--max-spend <USD>] [--sandbox auto|sandbox-exec|bwrap|docker|none] [--provider anthropic|openai|...] [--skill <name>]`
125	- `deadreckon list [--scope <scope>]` — list runs (active + recent).
126	- `deadreckon attach <run-id>` — open the live TUI on an in-flight or completed run.
127	- `deadreckon kill <run-id>` — terminate cleanly, release lock.
128	- `deadreckon resume <run-id>` — re-attach after a crash or pause; respects the phase machine.
129	- `deadreckon undo [--run <run-id>] [--turn <N>]` — restore files to N turns ago.
130	- `deadreckon show <run-id> [--turn <N>]` — print state, files changed, provenance.
131	- `deadreckon import {claude-code|codex|cursor}` — read-only import of histories.
132	- `deadreckon doctor` — preflight: platform sandbox binary reachable (`sandbox-exec` on mac, `bwrap` on Linux), Docker present only if `--sandbox docker` was used, config present, providers credentialed. Output is **actionable**: each missing item names the exact fix command.

22	impl CliClaudeCodeProvider {
23	    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>, entry: ProviderEntry) -> Self {
24	        let (model, model_arg) = cli_model(entry.model, "cli:claude-code");
25	        Self {
26	            name: name.into(),
27	            binary: entry.binary.unwrap_or_else(|| "claude".to_string()),
28	            extra_args: entry.extra_args,
29	            model,
30	            model_arg,
31	        }
32	    }
33	
34	    async fn run(&self, request: &ProviderRequest) -> Result<ProviderResponse> {
35	        let started = Instant::now();
36	        let mut args = self.extra_args.clone();
37	        if let Some(model) = self.model_arg.as_deref() {
38	            args.extend(["--model".to_string(), model.to_string()]);
39	        }
40	        // `claude --help` on this machine documents `-p, --print` for
41	        // non-interactive output and `--dangerously-skip-permissions` for
42	        // bypassing Claude Code prompts inside an outer sandbox.
43	        args.extend([
44	            "--dangerously-skip-permissions".to_string(),
45	            "-p".to_string(),
46	            request.prompt.clone(),
47	        ]);
48	        let output = run_cli(
49	            &self.name,
50	            &self.binary,
51	            &args,
52	            request.cwd.clone(),
53	            request.sandbox_backend,
54	            request.pid_file.clone(),
55	            request.cancellation_token.clone(),
56	        )
57	        .await?;
58	        write_output(request.output_path.as_ref(), &output).await?;
59	        ensure_success(&self.name, &output)?;
60	        let wall_time_seconds = started.elapsed().as_secs_f64();
61	        let usage = ProviderUsage {
62	            input_tokens: 0,
63	            output_tokens: 0,
64	        };
65	        let spend = self
66	            .estimate_spend(usage.clone())
67	            .with_wall_time(wall_time_seconds);
68	        Ok(ProviderResponse {
69	            provider: self.name.clone(),
70	            model: self.model.clone(),
71	            content: output.stdout.clone(),
72	            usage,
73	            spend,
74	            trace: json!({
75	                "kind": "cli_subagent",
76	                "binary": self.binary,
77	                "args": args,
78	                "stdout_path": request.output_path,
79	                "duration_ms": (wall_time_seconds * 1000.0).round() as u64,
80	                "exit_code": output.status_code,
81	                "pid": output.pid,
82	                "sandbox_backend": output.sandbox_backend,
83	                "sandbox_warning": output.sandbox_warning,
84	            }),
85	        })
86	    }
87	}

89	fn cli_model(model: Option<String>, legacy_label: &str) -> (String, Option<String>) {

92	            ("provider default".to_string(), None)
93	        }
94	        Some(model) => (model.clone(), Some(model)),
95	        None => ("provider default".to_string(), None),
96	    }
97	}

23	impl ProviderAdapter {
24	    pub fn new(name: impl Into<String>, kind: ProviderKind, entry: ProviderEntry) -> Self {
25	        let name = name.into();
26	        let api_key = entry
27	            .api_key
28	            .or_else(|| entry.api_key_env.as_deref().and_then(env_value));
29	        let base_url = entry.base_url.unwrap_or_else(|| default_base_url(&kind));
30	        let model = entry.model.unwrap_or_else(|| default_model(&kind));
31	        Self {
32	            name,
33	            kind,
34	            base_url,
35	            model,
36	            api_key,
37	            input_cost_per_million: entry.input_cost_per_million.unwrap_or(0.0),
38	            output_cost_per_million: entry.output_cost_per_million.unwrap_or(0.0),
39	            client: reqwest::Client::new(),
40	        }
41	    }
42	
43	    fn headers(&self) -> Result<HeaderMap> {
44	        let Some(api_key) = self.api_key.as_deref() else {
45	            return Err(ProviderError::MissingCredential(self.name.clone()));
46	        };
47	        let mut headers = HeaderMap::new();
48	        headers.insert(CONTENT_TYPE, HeaderValue::from_static("application/json"));
49	        match &self.kind {
50	            ProviderKind::Anthropic => {
51	                let key = HeaderValue::from_str(api_key).map_err(|err| {
52	                    ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!("invalid Anthropic API key header: {err}"))
53	                })?;
54	                headers.insert("x-api-key", key);
55	                headers.insert("anthropic-version", HeaderValue::from_static("2023-06-01"));
56	            }
57	            ProviderKind::OpenAi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => {
58	                let bearer =
59	                    HeaderValue::from_str(&format!("Bearer {api_key}")).map_err(|err| {
60	                        ProviderError::InvalidConfig(format!("invalid bearer token header: {err}"))
61	                    })?;
62	                headers.insert(AUTHORIZATION, bearer);
63	            }
64	            ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode
65	            | ProviderKind::CliCodex
66	            | ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke
67	            | ProviderKind::Generic(_) => {}
68	        }
69	        Ok(headers)
70	    }
71	
72	    fn endpoint(&self) -> String {
73	        match &self.kind {
74	            ProviderKind::Anthropic => {
75	                format!("{}/v1/messages", self.base_url.trim_end_matches('/'))
76	            }
77	            ProviderKind::OpenAi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => {
78	                format!("{}/chat/completions", self.base_url.trim_end_matches('/'))
79	            }
80	            ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode
81	            | ProviderKind::CliCodex
82	            | ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke
83	            | ProviderKind::Generic(_) => {
84	                unreachable!("CLI providers do not use HTTP endpoints")
85	            }
86	        }
87	    }
88	
89	    fn payload(&self, request: &ProviderRequest) -> Value {
90	        match &self.kind {
91	            ProviderKind::Anthropic => json!({
92	                "model": self.model,
93	                "max_tokens": request.max_output_tokens,
94	                "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": request.prompt}],
95	            }),
96	            ProviderKind::OpenAi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => json!({
97	                "model": self.model,
98	                "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": request.prompt}],
99	                "max_tokens": request.max_output_tokens,
100	                "stream": false,
101	            }),
102	            ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode
103	            | ProviderKind::CliCodex
104	            | ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke
105	            | ProviderKind::Generic(_) => {
106	                unreachable!("CLI providers do not use HTTP payloads")
107	            }
108	        }
109	    }

111	    async fn send(&self, request: &ProviderRequest) -> Result<ProviderResponse> {
112	        let headers = self.headers()?;
113	        let request_future = self
114	            .client
115	            .post(self.endpoint())
116	            .headers(headers)
117	            .json(&self.payload(request))
118	            .send();
119	        let response = if let Some(token) = request.cancellation_token.as_ref() {
120	            tokio::select! {
121	                _ = token.cancelled() => {
122	                    return Err(ProviderError::Http {
123	                        provider: self.name.clone(),
124	                        detail: "request cancelled".to_string(),
125	                    });
126	                }
127	                response = request_future => response
128	            }
129	        } else {
130	            request_future.await
131	        }
132	        .map_err(|err| ProviderError::Http {
133	            provider: self.name.clone(),
134	            detail: err.to_string(),
135	        })?;
136	        let status = response.status();
137	        let body = response.text().await.map_err(|err| ProviderError::Http {
138	            provider: self.name.clone(),
139	            detail: err.to_string(),
140	        })?;
141	        if !status.is_success() {
142	            return Err(ProviderError::Http {
143	                provider: self.name.clone(),
144	                detail: format!("HTTP {status}: {}", trim_for_error(&body)),
145	            });
146	        }
147	        self.parse_response(&body)
148	    }
149	
150	    fn parse_response(&self, body: &str) -> Result<ProviderResponse> {
151	        let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(body).map_err(|err| ProviderError::Http {
152	            provider: self.name.clone(),
153	            detail: err.to_string(),
154	        })?;
155	        let (content, usage) = match &self.kind {
156	            ProviderKind::Anthropic => parse_anthropic_response(&value),
157	            ProviderKind::OpenAi | ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => parse_openai_response(&value),
158	            ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode

160	            | ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke
161	            | ProviderKind::Generic(_) => {
162	                unreachable!("CLI providers do not parse HTTP responses")
163	            }
164	        };
165	        let spend = self.estimate_spend(usage.clone());
166	        Ok(ProviderResponse {
167	            provider: self.name.clone(),
168	            model: self.model.clone(),
169	            content,
170	            usage,
171	            spend,
172	            trace: json!({"kind": "http_llm"}),
173	        })
174	    }
175	}

179	        &self.name
180	    }

195	        let input = usage.input_tokens as f64 / 1_000_000.0 * self.input_cost_per_million;
196	        let output = usage.output_tokens as f64 / 1_000_000.0 * self.output_cost_per_million;

198	            provider: self.name.clone(),
199	            model: self.model.clone(),
200	            input_tokens: usage.input_tokens,
201	            output_tokens: usage.output_tokens,
202	            cost_usd: round_usd(input + output),
203	            subscription: false,
204	            wall_time_seconds: None,
205	        }
206	    }
207	
208	    fn complete<'a>(&'a self, request: &'a ProviderRequest) -> ProviderFuture<'a> {
209	        Box::pin(async move { self.send(request).await })
210	    }
211	}

91	pub fn acquire_lock(

99	    // REPORT.md: Multi-Agent Worktree Coordination Layer starts with scoped
100	    // locks so parallel agents do not claim the same task at once.
101	    fs::create_dir_all(paths.locks_dir()).with_path(paths.locks_dir())?;
102	    let path = lock_path(paths, scope, task_key);
103	    let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
104	        .create(true)
105	        .read(true)
106	        .write(true)
107	        .truncate(false)
108	        .open(&path)
109	        .with_path(&path)?;
110	
111	    match file.try_lock_exclusive() {
112	        Ok(()) => {}
113	        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => {
114	            if let Some(existing) = read_lock_state(&path)? {
115	                return Err(DeadreckonError::LockHeld {
116	                    task_key: task_key.to_string(),
117	                    run_id: existing.run_id,
118	                    phase: existing.phase,
119	                });
120	            }
121	            return Err(DeadreckonError::Io { path, source });
122	        }
123	        Err(source) => return Err(DeadreckonError::Io { path, source }),
124	    }
125	
126	    let existing = read_lock_state_from_file(&mut file, &path)?;
127	    if let Some(existing) = existing {
128	        let stale = lock_is_stale(&existing, stale_after);
129	        let alive = pid_is_alive(existing.pid);
130	        let same_owner = existing.run_id == run_id;
131	        if !same_owner && !stale && alive {
132	            file.unlock().with_path(&path)?;
133	            return Err(DeadreckonError::LockHeld {
134	                task_key: task_key.to_string(),
135	                run_id: existing.run_id,
136	                phase: existing.phase,
137	            });
138	        }
139	    }
140	
141	    // AS-BUILT §6: process-held locks are paired with a durable heartbeat so
142	    // a successor can distinguish live work from crash residue.
143	    let now = Utc::now();
144	    let state = LockState {
145	        task_key: task_key.to_string(),
146	        run_id: run_id.to_string(),
147	        scope: scope.to_string(),
148	        phase: phase.to_string(),
149	        pid: std::process::id(),
150	        acquired_at: now,
151	        updated_at: now,
152	    };
153	    write_lock_state_to_file(&mut file, &path, &state)?;
154	    Ok(LockGuard {
155	        path,
156	        file,
157	        state,
158	        released: false,
159	    })
160	}

255	fn read_lock_state(path: &Path) -> Result<Option<LockState>> {
256	    match fs::read(path) {
257	        Ok(data) if data.is_empty() => Ok(None),
258	        Ok(data) => serde_json::from_slice(&data).map(Some).with_json_path(path),
259	        Err(source) if source.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),
260	        Err(source) => Err(DeadreckonError::Io {
261	            path: path.to_path_buf(),
262	            source,
263	        }),
264	    }
265	}

267	fn read_lock_state_from_file(file: &mut File, path: &Path) -> Result<Option<LockState>> {
268	    file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0)).with_path(path)?;
269	    let mut data = Vec::new();
270	    file.read_to_end(&mut data).with_path(path)?;
271	    if data.is_empty() {
272	        return Ok(None);
273	    }
274	    serde_json::from_slice(&data).map(Some).with_json_path(path)
275	}

277	fn write_lock_state_to_file(file: &mut File, path: &Path, state: &LockState) -> Result<()> {
278	    file.set_len(0).with_path(path)?;
279	    file.seek(SeekFrom::Start(0)).with_path(path)?;
280	    serde_json::to_writer_pretty(&mut *file, state).with_json_path(path)?;
281	    file.write_all(b"\n").with_path(path)?;
282	    file.sync_all().with_path(path)
283	}

30	        requested_at: Utc::now(),

# Friendliness Audit

This is the P1 Effortless evaluation. It is intentionally bounded: the table
scores the canonical top-level command surface against the six-clause
friendliness contract, then later Effortless phases burn down the failing cells.

Legend: `pass` means the current surface satisfies the clause, `fail` means it is
part of the Effortless backlog, and `n-a` means the clause does not apply to that
verb.

| Verb | Clause | Status | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `init` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | Detects subscription CLIs during setup and offers the obvious provider path. |
| `init` | Preview before mutate | pass | Interactive setup confirms before writing config and completions. |
| `init` | Refuse with try: | pass | Setup refusals point at `doctor`, `detect`, or provider configuration. |
| `init` | One-command rollback | n-a | Setup writes user config rather than a workspace change. |
| `init` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | `init_completion_surface` renders one verdict and one `Recommended` command; `init_installs_shell_completion_by_default` guards it. |
| `init` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Help and completion install end by pointing to `doctor` or `start`. |
| `config` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | Direct get/set/provider commands do not prompt when the target is explicit. |
| `config` | Preview before mutate | pass | Provider/model interactive changes show the chosen route before writing. |
| `config` | Refuse with try: | fail | Some invalid key/value paths still need canonical `try:` coverage. |
| `config` | One-command rollback | pass | Config changes can be corrected with a single `config set` command. |
| `config` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | Config set/provider/model surfaces now render one primary command, with missing-key/provider refusals covered by lifecycle tests. |
| `config` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Help points back to `start` after configuration. |
| `help-all` | Auto-detect, don't ask | n-a | Static catalog; there is no environment-dependent choice. |
| `help-all` | Preview before mutate | n-a | Read-only command. |
| `help-all` | Refuse with try: | n-a | The command has no meaningful refusal path. |
| `help-all` | One-command rollback | n-a | Read-only command. |
| `help-all` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | The catalog has a single purpose: find the right command. |
| `help-all` | Lifecycle hint | pass | It ends with `deadreckon <command> --help`. |
| `completion` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | `completion install` detects the active shell when possible. |
| `completion` | Preview before mutate | pass | Install shows managed file/rc behavior and supports explicit shell output. |
| `completion` | Refuse with try: | pass | Unsupported shell and install errors include recovery commands. |
| `completion` | One-command rollback | pass | Generated files/managed rc blocks can be removed or regenerated in one command. |
| `completion` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | `completion_install_surface` has one `Recommended` command; `completion_install_detects_zsh_writes_script_and_managed_rc_block` guards it. |
| `completion` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Help points users back to setup/start. |
| `acceptance` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | Compatibility path maps to explicit done-criteria actions. |
| `acceptance` | Preview before mutate | pass | Draft/check/init paths expose criteria before launch use. |
| `acceptance` | Refuse with try: | pass | Criteria errors point to `def-done` recovery. |
| `acceptance` | One-command rollback | pass | Criteria can be overwritten or replaced with `def-done`. |
| `acceptance` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | Acceptance/def-done check and write paths route through VerdictSurface with one primary action. |
| `acceptance` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Help points to `def-done` and run/start use. |
| `def-done` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | Existing criteria are reused or displayed directly. |
| `def-done` | Preview before mutate | pass | Check/show/draft flows expose the done contract before runs depend on it. |
| `def-done` | Refuse with try: | pass | Invalid criteria and suppression refusals include concrete recovery. |
| `def-done` | One-command rollback | pass | Re-running `def-done` or `def-done add` changes the contract directly. |
| `def-done` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | `def-done` write/check success/failure surfaces render one verdict, explanation, and recommended command. |
| `def-done` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Help points to `start` after criteria are defined. |
| `try` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | It always uses the local smoke provider and throwaway workspace. |
| `try` | Preview before mutate | n-a | It mutates only isolated demo runstate under `DEADRECKON_HOME`. |
| `try` | Refuse with try: | pass | Any failed smoke proof points at inspection and normal `start`. |
| `try` | One-command rollback | n-a | It does not change the caller checkout. |
| `try` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | The proof block leads with a signed gate and one start command. |
| `try` | Lifecycle hint | pass | It ends with `deadreckon start "build the real thing"`. |
| `start` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | A single detected subscription provider is adopted inline; multiple detections keep the picker. |
| `start` | Preview before mutate | pass | Guided launch previews and confirms before creating run/plan state. |
| `start` | Refuse with try: | pass | Non-TTY missing provider/done/source refusals include recovery lines. |
| `start` | One-command rollback | pass | Launched worktree runs point at cleanup/abandon paths. |
| `start` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | Start preview and lifecycle launch surfaces use VerdictSurface; JSON goldens assert `primary_action` parity. |
| `start` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Successful launches print attach/status/kill/finish commands. |
| `run` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | Defaults resolve provider, source mode, and done criteria without prompts when explicit. |
| `run` | Preview before mutate | pass | Worktree/in-place/high-spend paths preview or require confirmation. |
| `run` | Refuse with try: | pass | Common provider/source/safety refusals end with `try:` guidance. |
| `run` | One-command rollback | pass | Worktree runs can be abandoned and in-place runs have undo snapshots. |
| `run` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | Exit cards now distinguish one primary next action and demote the rest. |
| `run` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Completion hints point to attach/show/apply/finish/cleanup. |
| `seams` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | Validation targets an explicit seam worker kind and config path without prompting. |
| `seams` | Preview before mutate | n-a | Seam validation is read-only and does not mutate workspace or run state. |
| `seams` | Refuse with try: | pass | Missing or invalid seam worker configuration reports a concrete validation/config recovery command. |
| `seams` | One-command rollback | n-a | Seam validation has no durable mutation to roll back. |
| `seams` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | Seam validation summaries and JSON now carry one `primary_action`; `seam_validation_*` tests guard it. |
| `seams` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Help and diagnostics point back to `run --no-seams` or focused seam validation. |
| `orchestrate` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | Explicit mode/provider flags avoid extra prompts; auto chooses a conservative path. |
| `orchestrate` | Preview before mutate | pass | Preview and final confirmation precede plan creation/forking. |
| `orchestrate` | Refuse with try: | pass | Planner/provider/source refusals include concrete launch commands. |
| `orchestrate` | One-command rollback | pass | Plan state can be killed/cleaned and merged results are applied explicitly. |
| `orchestrate` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | Orchestrate/plan lifecycle output uses `plan_verdict_surface`, with preview/setup rows demoted to non-primary guidance. |
| `orchestrate` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Output names attach/merge/finish. |
| `campaign` | Auto-detect, don't ask | fail | `--n` is still required instead of recommendation-seeded. |
| `campaign` | Preview before mutate | pass | Campaign preview shows sub-goals before launch. |
| `campaign` | Refuse with try: | pass | Depth/count/cross-sub refusals include recovery lines. |
| `campaign` | One-command rollback | pass | Campaigns can be killed and result application is explicit. |
| `campaign` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | Campaign preview, rollup, repair, and JSON paths use `campaign_verdict_surface` with one primary command. |
| `campaign` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Campaign output points at attach/show/finish. |
| `plan` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | Explicit planning inputs run without extra prompts. |
| `plan` | Preview before mutate | pass | Preview mode writes no plan state. |
| `plan` | Refuse with try: | pass | Planner and graph validation errors include recovery. |
| `plan` | One-command rollback | pass | Draft plan state can be killed/removed before merge. |
| `plan` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | Plan refusal/completion/failure output uses `plan_verdict_surface`; attach footers use subordinate `next` hints. |
| `plan` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Help/output point at fork/attach/merge. |
| `fork` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | Ready tasks and provider routes are read from the plan. |
| `fork` | Preview before mutate | pass | Fork refuses already-forked or invalid plans before spawning. |
| `fork` | Refuse with try: | pass | Blocked dependency and provider errors include next commands. |
| `fork` | One-command rollback | pass | Live plans can be killed. |
| `fork` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | Fork completion and refusal paths render VerdictSurface; `fork_completion_uses_one_verdict_surface` guards it. |
| `fork` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Output points at attach and merge. |
| `merge` | Auto-detect, don't ask | pass | Completed children and repair providers resolve from plan/config. |
| `merge` | Preview before mutate | pass | Conflict repair/refusal happens before promotion. |
| `merge` | Refuse with try: | pass | Conflict refusals point to merge repair/prefer-child options. |
| `merge` | One-command rollback | pass | Promotion results are library entries until explicitly applied/exported. |
| `merge` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | Merge completion, conflict, repair, and invalid-option paths render one primary action. |
| `merge` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Output points at finish/apply/export. |
| `chain` | Auto-detect, don't ask | fail | Chain breadth/step planning still asks more than the effortless path should. |
| `chain` | Preview before mutate | pass | Plan/run/apply modes preview or confirm state changes. |
| `chain` | Refuse with try: | pass | Chain refusals include scoped recovery commands. |
| `chain` | One-command rollback | pass | Undo/redo/reapply are one-command recovery paths. |
| `chain` | One verdict + ONE primary action | pass | Chain run/pause/completion/status surfaces use VerdictSurface; attach/help footers were demoted from `recommended:` to one `next` command. |
| `chain` | Lifecycle hint | pass | Chain output points at attach/resume/finish-style actions. |

| `doctor` | Preview before mutate | n-a | Read-only diagnostic. |
| `doctor` | Refuse with try: | pass | Findings include concrete setup/provider commands. |

842	impl CancelMarkerGuard {
843	    fn spawn(run_root: &Path, run_token: CancellationToken) -> Self {
844	        let shutdown = CancellationToken::new();
845	        let shutdown_for_task = shutdown.clone();
846	        let marker = cancel_marker_path_for_run_root(run_root);
847	        let handle = tokio::spawn(async move {
848	            loop {
849	                tokio::select! {
850	                    _ = shutdown_for_task.cancelled() => break,
851	                    _ = tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50)) => {
852	                        if marker.exists() {
853	                            run_token.cancel();
854	                            break;
855	                        }
856	                    }
857	                }
858	            }
859	        });
860	        Self { shutdown, handle }
861	    }
862	}
863	
864	impl Drop for CancelMarkerGuard {
865	    fn drop(&mut self) {
866	        self.shutdown.cancel();
867	        self.handle.abort();

fn footer_for_state(state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState, tui_state: &AttachTuiState) -> String {
    if let Some(action) = tui_state.pending_confirm {
        return footer(&[
            (format!("confirm {}?", action.label()), String::new()),
            ("y".to_string(), "run".to_string()),
            ("any other key".to_string(), "cancel".to_string()),
        ]);
    }
    let mut items: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
    let push = |items: &mut Vec<(String, String)>, pairs: &[(&str, &str)]| {
        items.extend(pairs.iter().map(|(k, l)| (k.to_string(), l.to_string())));
    };

    // Detach (or, for a child run attached from a plan, back-to-plan + the parent
    // breadcrumb) comes first so the exit affordance and parent context stay
    // visible even when a narrow terminal truncates the footer tail.
    if let Some(parent_plan) = tui_state.parent_plan.as_ref() {
        items.push((
            "b/Backspace/q/Esc/Ctrl-D".to_string(),
            "back to plan".to_string(),
        ));
        let campaign = parent_plan
            .campaign_parent
            .as_ref()
            .map(|campaign| {
                format!(
                    "campaign {} / {} / ",
                    run_prefix(&campaign.campaign_id),
                    campaign.sub_id
                )
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
        items.push((
            "parent".to_string(),
            format!(
                "{campaign}plan {} {}",
                run_prefix(&parent_plan.plan_id),
                parent_plan.task_id
            ),
        ));
    } else {
        items.push(("q/Esc/Ctrl-D".to_string(), "detach".to_string()));
    }

/// Resolve a completion-overlay keystroke given any pending confirmation.
/// Destructive actions (Apply/Abandon) require a two-step confirm: the action
/// key arms `pending`, then `y` runs it and any other key cancels. Abandon is
/// `x` so that `b` is unambiguously "back" (no longer overloaded with Abandon).
fn resolve_completion_key(
    key: KeyEvent,
    pending: Option<CompletionAction>,
) -> CompletionKeyOutcome {
    if let Some(action) = pending {
        return if key.code == KeyCode::Char('y') {
            CompletionKeyOutcome::Execute(action)
        } else {
            CompletionKeyOutcome::Cancel
        };
    }
    let action = match key.code {
        KeyCode::Char('m') => CompletionAction::Materialize,
        KeyCode::Char('e') => CompletionAction::Extend,
        KeyCode::Char('a') => CompletionAction::Apply,
        KeyCode::Char('x') => CompletionAction::Abandon,
        KeyCode::Char('s') => CompletionAction::Show,
        _ => return CompletionKeyOutcome::Ignored,
    };
    if action.is_destructive() {
        CompletionKeyOutcome::Confirm(action)
    } else {
        CompletionKeyOutcome::Execute(action)
    }
}

async fn run_completion_action(
    terminal: &mut Terminal<CrosstermBackend<io::Stdout>>,
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState,
    action: CompletionAction,
) -> Result<Option<AttachActionNotice>> {

    #[test]
    fn back_and_abandon_are_distinct_keys() {
        // Abandon is 'x'; 'b' is no longer Abandon (it is reserved for "back").
        assert_eq!(
            resolve_completion_key(key(KeyCode::Char('x')), None),
            CompletionKeyOutcome::Confirm(CompletionAction::Abandon)
        );
        assert_eq!(
            resolve_completion_key(key(KeyCode::Char('b')), None),
            CompletionKeyOutcome::Ignored
        );
        // Non-destructive actions run immediately, no confirm.
        assert_eq!(
            resolve_completion_key(key(KeyCode::Char('s')), None),
            CompletionKeyOutcome::Execute(CompletionAction::Show)
        );
    }

//! Shared setup contracts for provider selection and done criteria.
//!
//! This module is deliberately runtime-only: it standardizes how command
//! surfaces describe provider roles and done-criteria sources without adding
//! durable run, plan, or config fields.

    PrimaryRun,
    ConfigDefault,
    DocPolish,
    Planner,
    DefaultChild,
    ChildOverride { index: usize },
    Coder,
    Reviewer,
    Repair,
}

impl SetupProviderRole {
    pub(crate) fn label(&self) -> String {
        match self {
            Self::PrimaryRun => "primary".to_string(),
            Self::ConfigDefault => "default".to_string(),
            Self::DocPolish => "docs".to_string(),
            Self::Planner => "planner".to_string(),
            Self::DefaultChild => "default-child".to_string(),
            Self::ChildOverride { index } => format!("child-{index}"),
            Self::Coder => "coder".to_string(),
            Self::Reviewer => "reviewer".to_string(),
            Self::Repair => "repair".to_string(),
        }
    }
}

pub(crate) async fn write_output(path: Option<&PathBuf>, output: &CliOutput) -> Result<()> {
    let Some(path) = path else {
        return Ok(());
    };
    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
        tokio::fs::create_dir_all(parent)
            .await
            .map_err(|source| ProviderError::Io {
                path: parent.display().to_string(),
                source,
            })?;
    }
    let body = format!("{}\n{}", output.stdout, output.stderr);
    tokio::fs::write(path, body)
        .await
        .map_err(|source| ProviderError::Io {
            path: path.display().to_string(),
            source,
        })
}

pub(crate) fn ensure_success(provider: &str, output: &CliOutput) -> Result<()> {
    if output.status_code == Some(0) {
        return Ok(());
    }
    Err(ProviderError::Cli {
        provider: provider.to_string(),
        detail: format!(
            "subprocess exited with {:?}: {}{}",
            output.status_code, output.stdout, output.stderr
        ),
    })
}

  if (!arch) {

  if (process.platform === "darwin") {
    return `deadreckon-darwin-${arch}`;

  if (process.platform === "linux") {
    return `deadreckon-linux-${arch}`;
  }

fn non_empty(value: Option<&str>) -> Option<&str> {
    value.map(str::trim).filter(|value| !value.is_empty())
}

fn provider_route_exists(config_path: &Path, registry: &ProviderRegistry, provider: &str) -> bool {
    registry.get(provider).is_some()
        || read_config(config_path)
            .ok()
            .is_some_and(|config| config.providers.contains_key(provider))
}

fn route_info_for_provider(
    config_path: &Path,
    provider: Option<&str>,
    model: Option<&str>,
) -> Result<Option<ProviderRouteInfo>, ProviderError> {
    let router = ProviderRouter::from_config_path_with_model(config_path, provider, model)?;
    Ok(router.selected_route_info())
}

fn setup_refusal_for_provider_error(provider: Option<&str>, error: ProviderError) -> SetupRefusal {
    match error {
        ProviderError::InvalidConfig(message) if message.contains("unknown provider route") => {
            match provider {
                Some(provider) => SetupRefusal::unknown_provider(provider),
                None => SetupRefusal {
                    message,
                    try_line: "deadreckon providers list --all".to_string(),
                },
            }
        }
        other => SetupRefusal {
            message: other.to_string(),
            try_line: "deadreckon providers list --all".to_string(),
        },
    }
}

fn provider_credential_label(
    descriptor: Option<&ProviderDescriptor>,
    route: Option<&ProviderRouteInfo>,
) -> String {
    let has_credential = route.is_some_and(|route| route.has_credential);
    match descriptor {
        Some(descriptor) if descriptor.subscription && has_credential => "subscription",
        Some(descriptor) if descriptor.subscription => "missing",
        Some(descriptor) if descriptor.auth.kind == AuthKind::None && has_credential => "none",
        Some(_) if has_credential => "ready",
        Some(_) => "missing",
        None if has_credential => "ready",
        None => "missing",
    }
    .to_string()
}

fn first_install_hint(descriptor: &ProviderDescriptor) -> Option<String> {
    descriptor.install_hint.try_lines.first().cloned()
}

fn descriptor_kind_label(kind: &DescriptorKind) -> &'static str {
    match kind {
        DescriptorKind::Http => "http",
        DescriptorKind::Cli => "cli",
        DescriptorKind::LocalHttp => "local-http",
        DescriptorKind::Scripted => "scripted",
    }
}

fn provider_kind_label(kind: &ProviderKind) -> String {
    match kind {
        ProviderKind::Anthropic => "anthropic".to_string(),
        ProviderKind::OpenAi => "openai".to_string(),
        ProviderKind::OpenAiCompatible => "openai-compatible".to_string(),
        ProviderKind::CliClaudeCode => "cli".to_string(),
        ProviderKind::CliCodex => "cli".to_string(),
        ProviderKind::ScriptedSmoke => "scripted".to_string(),
        ProviderKind::Generic(id) => id.clone(),
    }
}

    pub explanation: ExplanationPanel,

}

impl VerdictSurface {
    pub fn try_new<L, C, SL, SC>(
        kind: VerdictKind,
        subject_kind: impl Into<String>,
        subject: Option<&str>,
        explanation: ExplanationPanel,
        primary_actions: impl IntoIterator<Item = (L, C)>,
        secondary_actions: impl IntoIterator<Item = (SL, SC)>,
    ) -> Result<Self, VerdictSurfaceError>
    where
        L: Into<String>,
        C: Into<String>,
        SL: Into<String>,
        SC: Into<String>,
    {
        let subject_kind = subject_kind.into();
        if subject_kind.trim().is_empty() {
            return Err(VerdictSurfaceError::MissingSubjectKind);
        }
        explanation.validate()?;

        let primary = primary_actions
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(label, command)| HintLine {
                label: label.into(),
                command: command.into(),
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        if primary.len() != 1 {
            return Err(VerdictSurfaceError::ExpectedOnePrimaryAction {
                actual: primary.len(),
            });
        }
        let mut primary = primary;
        let primary_action = primary.remove(0);
        if primary_action.command.trim().is_empty() {
            return Err(VerdictSurfaceError::MissingPrimaryCommand);
        }

        let primary_command = primary_action.command.clone();
        let secondary_actions = secondary_actions
            .into_iter()
            .map(|(label, command)| HintLine {
                label: label.into(),
                command: command.into(),
            })
            .filter(|action| action.command != primary_command)
            .collect();

        Ok(Self {
            kind,
            subject_kind,
            subject: subject.map(str::to_string),
            explanation,
            primary_action,
            secondary_actions,
```
