## 2. Help screen structure & rendering

### The hook — `/Users/gdc/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/cmd/help.go`

```go
func DisplayLogoAndHelp(cmd *cobra.Command) {
	fmt.Println() // Add visual separation before the logo
	fmt.Println(utils.GetRandomLogo())
	_ = cmd.Help()
}
```

A custom `help` command (`Use: "help [command]"`, alias `h`) calls this; unknown subcommands print `Unknown command: X` then logo + root help. The root command's bare `Run` also calls `cmdpkg.DisplayLogoAndHelp(c)` (main.go:245-253), so `specstory` with no args = banner + help.

### Execution wiring — `main.go:1628`

```go
if err := fang.Execute(context.Background(), rootCmd, fang.WithVersion(version)); err != nil {
```

`fang.Execute` calls `root.SetHelpFunc(helpFunc)` — so `cmd.Help()` above routes into **fang's styled help renderer** (`helpFn` in fang's `help.go`). Fang also sets `SilenceUsage/SilenceErrors`, adds a hidden `man` command, and shell completions.

### Layout produced by fang's `helpFn` (fang@v0.4.4/help.go), top to bottom:

1. **Description** — `cmp.Or(c.Long, c.Short)`, wrapped to terminal width (capped at 120 cols), 2-space left pad.
2. **`USAGE` title** — bold, uppercase-transformed, purple, `Padding(1,0)` + `Margin(0,2)`.
3. **Usage codeblock** — background-tinted block, `MarginLeft(2)`, `Padding(1,2)`; usage line is tokenized: program name, subcommand, and dimmed `[command] [args] [--flags]` placeholders each styled separately.
4. **`EXAMPLES` title + codeblock** — `cmd.Example` is parsed line by line; `# comment` lines styled as comments; shell lines get full **syntax highlighting** (program name, subcommands, `--flags`, `"quoted strings"`, arguments, pipes/redirects all distinct colors). Long lines truncated with `…`.
5. **`COMMANDS` section(s)** — two-column: styled command name (4-space left pad) + description, aligned via computed `space` shared with the flags column (min 10).
6. **`FLAGS` section** — `-s --session` style keys (flag color), descriptions with **first word auto-Title-cased** (`titleFirstWord` transform), and defaults appended dimmed as ` (value)` when non-empty/non-false/non-zero.
7. Trailing blank line.

Errors render a `ERROR` badge (bold, butter-on-cherry background, padded) + message, and for usage errors append: `Try` ` --help ` `for usage.` with the flag styled. If stderr is not a TTY, plain `err.Error()` only.

### SpecStory's actual help content (main.go `createRootCommand`)

```go
Use:   "specstory [command]",
Short: "SpecStory auto-saves terminal coding agent chat interactions",
Long:  `SpecStory is a wrapper for terminal coding agents that auto-saves markdown files of all your chat interactions.`
       // + "\n\nSupported agents: " + providerList + "."
```

Examples are **dynamically built from the provider registry**, with comment lines:

```
# Check terminal coding agents installation
specstory check

# Run the default agent with auto-saving
specstory run

# Run a specific agent with auto-saving
specstory run <each provider id>

# Run with custom command
specstory run claude -c "/custom/path/to/agent"

# Generate markdown files for all agent sessions associated with the current directory
specstory sync

# Generate markdown files for specific agent sessions
specstory sync -s <session-id>
...
# Watch for any agent activity in the current directory and generate markdown files
specstory watch
```

Subcommands: `run` (alias `r`), `watch`, `sync` (alias `s`), `list`, `version` (aliases `v`, `ver`), `check`, `login`, `logout`, custom `help` (alias `h`). Hidden flags (`--cloud-token`, `--cloud-url`, `--debug-raw`, `--provenance`) are filtered out of help by fang (`if f.Hidden { return }`).

---

### Fang default colorscheme (fang@v0.4.4/theme.go, `DefaultColorScheme`, light/dark adaptive via background detection), with charmtone hex values:

| Element | Dark-bg color | Light-bg color |
|---|---|---|
| Section titles (USAGE/EXAMPLES/COMMANDS/FLAGS) | **Charple `#6B50FF`** (bold, uppercased) | same |
| Body/argument text (Base) | Ash `#DFDBDD` | Charcoal `#3A3943` |
| Codeblock background | `#2F2E36` | Salt `#F1EFEF` |
| Program name (`specstory`) | Guppy `#7272FF` | Malibu `#00A4FF` |
| Subcommand names | Cheeky `#FF79D0` | Pony `#FF4FBF` |

| `# comments` in examples | `#747282` | Squid `#858392` |

| Quoted strings | Salmon `#FF7F90` | Coral `#FF577D` |
| ERROR badge | Butter `#FFFAF1` on Cherry `#FF388B` | same |

So: **purple headings, blue program name, pink commands, green flags, salmon strings, grey dim args** — plus the random 256-color gradient banner on top. There's also an `AnsiColorScheme` fallback for limited terminals.

### SpecStory's own colors for non-help output — `/Users/gdc/getspecstory/specstory-cli/pkg/log/logger.go`:

ColorYellow = "33m"; ColorBlue = "34m"; ColorMagenta = "35m"; ColorCyan = "36m";

## 4. Banner shown vs suppressed

- **Shown** (random palette each time): bare `specstory` (root Run), `specstory help`, `specstory help <cmd>`, `specstory help <unknown>` (after "Unknown command: X").
- **NOT shown**: `specstory --help` / `specstory <cmd> --help` (these go straight to fang's helpFunc — styled help, no logo); error-triggered usage (main.go:1659 calls `rootCmd.Usage()` only, and only for cobra command/flag errors detected by string-matching `"unknown command"`, `"unknown flag"`, etc.); `--silent` is not checked for the banner, but the banner paths only run in interactive-help situations.
- **TTY detection**: the logo itself is printed raw with `fmt.Println` — **no TTY/NO_COLOR detection for the banner** (the embedded ANSI always goes out). The fang help text, however, goes through `colorprofile.NewWriter(c.OutOrStdout(), os.Environ())`, which downgrades/strips colors based on TTY, `NO_COLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE`, and `TERM`. Fang also drops the codeblock's vertical padding when the profile is ASCII/no-TTY or there's no background color (`help.go:57-59`). Terminal width: `min(actual, 120)`, fallback 120.

### Reproducing in Rust — closest equivalents
- Banner: pre-render figlet "standard" font + per-character 256-color gradient (or use a small gradient function at runtime); store 10-12 palettes, pick randomly.

# OpenClaw study — how "everything is SMART" maps to code

OpenClaw (`/Users/gdc/openclaw`) is a TypeScript/Node CLI (`openclaw`, entry `openclaw.mjs` → `dist/entry.js`, built with commander). Below is everything relevant for a Rust CLI emulation, with verbatim copy and file paths.

---

## 1. First run / no config — the onboarding wizard

**Trigger paths:**
- The installer script (`curl … install.sh | bash`) "Attempts onboarding when appropriate (TTY available, onboarding not disabled, and bootstrap/config checks pass)" — `/Users/gdc/openclaw/docs/install/installer.md` (Post-install tasks step). Skippable with `--no-onboard`.
- Manually: `openclaw onboard` (alias-ish: `openclaw setup --wizard`). Docs recommend `openclaw onboard --install-daemon` as step 2 of getting started (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/docs/start/getting-started.md`).
- There is no auto-wizard on bare invocation; instead a **config guard** runs before every command and points broken configs at `doctor` (see §5).

**The wizard flow** — `/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/wizard/onboarding.ts` (`runOnboardingWizard`), dispatched from `/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/commands/onboard.ts`:

1. **ASCII-art header** (`printWizardHeader`, `/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/commands/onboard-helpers.ts:99`) — a block-art "OPENCLAW" banner with `🦞 OPENCLAW 🦞`.
2. **`intro("OpenClaw onboarding")`** then a **mandatory risk acknowledgement** note (verbatim):
   ```
   Security warning — please read.

   OpenClaw is a hobby project and still in beta. Expect sharp edges.
   This bot can read files and run actions if tools are enabled.
   A bad prompt can trick it into doing unsafe things.

   If you're not comfortable with basic security and access control, don't run OpenClaw.
   Ask someone experienced to help before enabling tools or exposing it to the internet.

   Recommended baseline:
   - Pairing/allowlists + mention gating.
   - Sandbox + least-privilege tools.
   ...
   ```
   followed by `confirm: "I understand this is powerful and inherently risky. Continue?"` with `initialValue: false`. Decline = wizard cancelled, exit 1.
3. **Config snapshot check** — `readConfigFileSnapshot()`. If config exists but is invalid, it prints each issue (`- path: message`) and bails: `` Config invalid. Run `openclaw doctor` to repair it, then re-run onboarding. ``
4. **Flow select** (defaults-first):
   ```
   message: "Onboarding mode"
   { value: "quickstart", label: "QuickStart", hint: "Configure details later via `openclaw configure`." }
   { value: "advanced",   label: "Manual",     hint: "Configure port, network, Tailscale, and auth options." }
   initialValue: "quickstart"
   ```
5. **Existing config detected** → note titled `"Existing config detected"` with `summarizeExistingConfig()` (key/value rows like `workspace: …`, `model: …`, `gateway.port: …`; else `"No key settings detected."`), then:
   ```
   message: "Config handling"
   keep   → "Use existing values"
   modify → "Update values"
   reset  → "Reset"          → reset scope: "Config only" | "Config + creds + sessions" | "Full reset (config + creds + sessions + workspace)"
   ```
6. **QuickStart summary note** — prints the exact defaults it's about to apply (`Gateway port: 18789`, `Gateway bind: Loopback (127.0.0.1)`, `Gateway auth: Token (default)`, `Tailscale exposure: Off`, `Direct to chat channels.`) — or, if config exists, "Keeping your current gateway settings:" with current values.
7. **Live gateway probing** — it probes `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>` and any configured remote URL *before* asking local/remote, and bakes results into menu hints:
   ```
   message: "What do you want to set up?"
   { value: "local",  label: "Local gateway (this machine)",  hint: localProbe.ok ? `Gateway reachable (${localUrl})` : `No gateway detected (${localUrl})` }
   { value: "remote", label: "Remote gateway (info-only)",    hint: !remoteUrl ? "No remote URL configured yet" : remoteProbe?.ok ? `Gateway reachable (${remoteUrl})` : `Configured but unreachable (${remoteUrl})` }
   ```
   QuickStart skips this question entirely (assumes local).
8. **Workspace** — text prompt `"Workspace directory"` with `initialValue` from existing config or `~/.openclaw/workspace` (QuickStart never asks).
9. **Model/auth** — grouped two-level menu (see §3), then default-model picker, then `warnIfModelConfigLooksOff`.
10. **Gateway config** (`onboarding.gateway-config.ts`), **channels**, **skills**, **hooks** — each step a confirm-gated section. Writes config, stamps `wizard.lastRunAt/lastRunVersion/lastRunCommand/lastRunMode` metadata (`applyWizardMetadata`).
11. **Finalize** (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/wizard/onboarding.finalize.ts`): daemon install (`confirm: "Install Gateway service (recommended)", initialValue: true`; auto-yes on QuickStart), waits for gateway with `waitForGatewayReachable` (15s poll loop) so the health check doesn't false-fail, runs `health`, prints Control UI links + token explainer, then the signature prompt:
    ```
    message: "How do you want to hatch your bot?"
    { value: "tui",   label: "Hatch in TUI (recommended)" }
    { value: "web",   label: "Open the Web UI" }
    { value: "later", label: "Do this later" }
    initialValue: "tui"
    ```
    If a bootstrap file exists in the workspace it first shows (verbatim, title `"Start TUI (best option!)"`):
    ```
    This is the defining action that makes your agent you.
    Please take your time.
    The more you tell it, the better the experience will be.
    We will send: "Wake up, my friend!"
    ```
    TUI choice launches the chat TUI directly with the message `"Wake up, my friend!"`. Web choice opens the tokenized dashboard URL via OS-detected opener and prints `"Opened in your browser. Keep that tab to control OpenClaw."` (or a precomputed SSH tunnel hint if headless).

**Platform smarts in the entry command** (`onboard.ts`): on Windows it prints
```
Windows detected — OpenClaw runs great on WSL2!
Native Windows might be trickier.
Quick setup: wsl --install (one command, one reboot)
Guide: https://docs.openclaw.ai/windows
```
Non-interactive mode requires `--accept-risk` explicitly: `"Non-interactive onboarding requires explicit risk acknowledgement."` Deprecated auth choices are normalized with a notice instead of erroring (`'Auth choice "claude-cli" is deprecated; using setup-token flow instead.'`).

---

## 2. Context detection & adaptive behavior

This is the densest "smart" layer:

- **Config snapshot everywhere** — `readConfigFileSnapshot()` returns `{exists, valid, issues, legacyIssues, config}`; every flow branches on it (wizard offers keep/modify/reset; guard blocks commands; doctor migrates).
- **Gateway probing before asking** — `probeGatewayReachable` / `waitForGatewayReachable` (`onboard-helpers.ts:380-436`) do a real WS health call with 1.5s timeout and feed *menu hints* and post-install verification. Errors are summarized to one trimmed 120-char line (`summarizeError`).
- **Binary detection** — `detectBinary(name)` (`onboard-helpers.ts:342`) — `which`/`where` with 2s timeout, used for: `signal-cli`, `brew`, `open`/`xdg-open`/`wslview`, imessage CLI.
- **Channel quickstart scoring** — each channel onboarding adapter returns `{configured, statusLines, selectionHint, quickstartScore}`; the wizard preselects the highest score (`resolveQuickstartDefault`, `onboard-channels.ts:208`). Scores encode opinion + detection: WhatsApp `linked ? 5 : 4`, Telegram `configured ? 1 : 10` (i.e. *push Telegram for new users*), Signal `signalCliDetected ? 1 : 0`, iMessage `imessageCliDetected ? 1 : 0`, Slack/Discord `configured ? 2 : 1`. Files: `/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/channels/plugins/onboarding/{whatsapp,telegram,signal,discord,slack,imessage}.ts`.
- **Per-channel live status lines** baked into hints, e.g. Signal: `` `Signal: ${configured ? "configured" : "needs setup"}` `` + `` `signal-cli: ${found ? "found" : "missing"} (${path})` ``, selection hint `"signal-cli found"`/`"signal-cli missing"`. Already-configured channels get an adaptive menu: `"${label} already configured. What do you want to do?"` → Modify settings / Disable (keeps config) / Delete config / Skip (leave as-is).
- **Environment-aware browser opening** — `resolveBrowserOpenCommand` detects SSH-without-DISPLAY, WSL (`wslview`), macOS `open`, Linux `xdg-open`; on failure prints a *fully formed* SSH port-forward recipe with the user/host pulled from `$SSH_CONNECTION`:
  ```
  No GUI detected. Open from your computer:
  ssh -N -L 18789:127.0.0.1:18789 user@host
  Then open:
  http://localhost:18789/  (+ #token=… variant)
  ```
- **Platform branches** — Linux: checks `isSystemdUserServiceAvailable()`; if absent, skips daemon install with `"Systemd user services are unavailable; skipping service install. Use your container supervisor or \`docker compose up -d\`."`; if present, walks through systemd *lingering* with an explanation of why. macOS doctor checks `launchctl getenv` overrides that shadow config tokens (`doctor-platform-notes.ts`).
- **Skills eligibility scan** — `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` classifies skills into eligible / missing requirements / unsupported-on-OS / blocked-by-allowlist and shows counts before offering installs; detects missing Homebrew and offers the install one-liner (`onboard-skills.ts`).
- **Web-search key detection** — finalize checks both config and `BRAVE_API_KEY` env and prints a different note for each state.
- **State migrations** — doctor detects legacy config keys/state layouts and offers migrations (`doctor-state-migrations.ts`, `doctor-legacy-config.ts`).

---

## 3. Interactive UX building blocks

- **Language/stack:** TypeScript on Node, **commander** for the CLI, **`@clack/prompts` ^1.0.1** for all interactive prompts/spinners, **chalk ^5.6.2** behind a custom theme (`src/terminal/theme.ts`), plus a custom TUI (`src/tui/`) for chat.
- **Abstraction layer:** `WizardPrompter` interface (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/wizard/prompts.ts`) — `intro/outro/note/select/multiselect/text/confirm/progress` — with two implementations: `createClackPrompter()` (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/wizard/clack-prompter.ts`) for humans, and non-interactive/RPC prompters for scripts (`onboard-non-interactive.ts`, `doctor-prompter.ts`). Every menu item is `{value, label, hint?}`; cancellation is uniform (`isCancel` → `cancel("Setup cancelled.")` → `WizardCancelledError` → exit 1).
- **Menu mechanics:** clack-style **arrow-key navigation with an `initialValue` default** (defaults-first everywhere — quickstart preselected, recommended option preselected, detected channel preselected). Hints render dim after the label. Multiselect used for skill deps with a literal `"Skip for now"` first option. No single-key selection. Two-level select with a `"Back"` sentinel for grouped menus (`auth-choice-prompt.ts`, `BACK_VALUE = "__back"`).
- **Spinners:** clack `spinner()` wrapped in `progress(label)` with `update()`/`stop(message)`, plus OSC 9;4 terminal progress (`createCliProgress` in `src/cli/progress.ts`). Usage pattern: `Installing X…` → `Installed X` / `Install failed: X (exit N) — detail`.
- **Notes as primary teaching tool:** titled boxes (`src/terminal/note.ts`) used constantly — `"Channel status"`, `"How channels work"`, `"Token"`, `"Security"`, `"What now"`.
- **Auth menu structure** (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/commands/auth-choice-options.ts`): first a provider group select (`message: "Model/auth provider"`) — `OpenAI (hint: "Codex OAuth + API key")`, `Anthropic (hint: "setup-token + API key")`, `MiniMax (hint: "M2.5 (recommended)")`, … `Custom Provider (hint: "Any OpenAI or Anthropic compatible endpoint")`, plus `Skip for now` — then a per-group method select if >1 option (auto-selects when 1). Option labels carry actionable hints, e.g. `"Anthropic token (paste setup-token)"` / hint `` "run `claude setup-token` elsewhere, then paste the token here" ``.

---

## 4. Bare invocation (`openclaw` with no args)

There is **no default action**: commander prints the styled help. But the help itself is curated (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/cli/program/help.ts`):
- A **banner** prepended via `addHelpText("beforeAll")` — `🦞 OpenClaw <version> (<commit>) — <tagline>` where the tagline is randomly picked from ~60 jokes plus date-aware holiday lines (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/cli/tagline.ts`), e.g. `"If you're lost, run doctor; if you're brave, run prod; if you're wise, run tests."` and `"curl for conversations."` Banner suppressed for `--json`, `--version`, non-TTY, `OPENCLAW_HIDE_BANNER`, and `update`/`completion` commands (`src/cli/banner.ts`, `program/preaction.ts`).
- Headings (`Usage:`/`Options:`/`Commands:`) recolored, subcommands/options sorted alphabetically and themed.
- An `Examples:` section appended `afterAll` (8 real command+description pairs) ending with `Docs: docs.openclaw.ai/cli`.
- Subcommands are *lazily registered* (`command-registry.ts`) — placeholders carry descriptions for help, real modules load only when invoked. Hot read-only paths (`status`, `health`, `sessions`, `config get`…) bypass commander entirely via a fast router (`src/cli/program/routes.ts`).
- Several subcommands have smart no-arg defaults: `openclaw config` (no subcommand) opens the configure wizard; `openclaw models` → `models status`; `openclaw skills` → `skills list` (docs/cli/*.md).

---

## 5. Doctor / status / dashboard patterns

- **Config guard before every command** (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/cli/program/config-guard.ts`): if config exists but is invalid, prints
  ```
  Config invalid
  File: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
  Problem:
    - <path>: <message>
  Run: openclaw doctor --fix
  ```
  and exits 1 — *except* for an allowlist of diagnostic commands (`doctor`, `logs`, `health`, `help`, `status`, and gateway status/probe/start/stop/…) which may proceed on a broken config. This is a great pattern: never lock the user out of the tools that fix the problem.
- **`openclaw doctor`** (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/commands/doctor.ts` + ~20 `doctor-*.ts` modules): banner + `intro("OpenClaw doctor")`, then sequential check/repair phases, each a `note(...)` plus an optional `confirmRepair` prompt: update offer, UI protocol freshness, source-install issues, deprecated env vars, config migration, auth profile health (incl. keychain prompts only when TTY), gateway mode/auth (`"Gateway auth is off or missing a token. Token auth is now the recommended default (including loopback)."` → `confirm: "Generate and configure a gateway token now?"` default true), gateway daemon repair, extra-service scan, sandbox images, state integrity, security warnings, memory search health, workspace status + backup tip, shell completion. Flags: `--repair`/`--fix` (writes `.bak`, drops unknown keys listing each removal), `--deep`, `--non-interactive`, `--generate-gateway-token`. Missing-config case: `` Missing config: run `openclaw setup` first. ``
- **`openclaw status`** (`status.command.ts`): renders a real table (`renderTable`) of Item/Status/Detail rows where free-text channel health is classified into colored badges (`OK`/`WARN`/`OFF`/`LINKED`/`UNLINKED`), then FAQ/troubleshooting links, update-available hint, and **adaptive next steps**:
  ```
  Next steps:
    Need to share?      openclaw status --all
    Need to debug live? openclaw logs --follow
    Need to test channels? openclaw status --deep     (only if gateway reachable)
    Fix reachability first: openclaw gateway probe    (only if not)
  ```
  `status --all` produces a shareable full report; `getStatusSummary` (`status.summary.ts`) aggregates per-agent sessions with token usage %, model, heartbeats, queued events, and has a `redactSensitiveStatusSummary` variant.
- **`openclaw dashboard`** (`dashboard.ts`): resolves the Control UI URL from config (coercing `lan`→`loopback` because "LAN URLs fail secure-context checks"), puts the token in the **URL fragment** (not query) to avoid leaks, prints it, **copies to clipboard**, auto-opens the browser if the environment supports it, else prints the SSH tunnel recipe.

---

## 6. Best copy to steal (voice & structure)

The voice: short declarative lines, honest about risk, always pairs a statement with the exact command to run next, playful only at the edges (banner/taglines), never in safety or error text.

- Risk gate: `"OpenClaw is a hobby project and still in beta. Expect sharp edges."` / `"I understand this is powerful and inherently risky. Continue?"` (default **No**).
- Windows: `"Windows detected — OpenClaw runs great on WSL2! … Quick setup: wsl --install (one command, one reboot)"`.
- QuickStart hint pattern: option label is the *choice*, hint is the *consequence*: `QuickStart — "Configure details later via \`openclaw configure\`."` vs `Manual — "Configure port, network, Tailscale, and auth options."`
- Detection-in-hint: `"Gateway reachable (ws://127.0.0.1:18789)"` / `"No gateway detected (…)"` / `"Configured but unreachable (…)"`.
- Hatching ceremony: `"How do you want to hatch your bot?"`, `"Hatch in TUI (recommended)"`, and the bootstrap note `"This is the defining action that makes your agent you. Please take your time."` … `'We will send: "Wake up, my friend!"'`
- Token explainer note (title `Token`): states what it is, where it's stored, how to view it, how to regenerate it, where the browser caches it — five facts, five lines, each with a command.
- Channel security primer: `"DM security: default is pairing; unknown DMs get a pairing code."` + `"Approve with: openclaw pairing approve <channel> <code>"`; DM policy menu: `Pairing (recommended) / Allowlist (specific users only) / Open (public inbound DMs) / Disabled (ignore DMs)`.
- Skills status note: four counters (`Eligible / Missing requirements / Unsupported on this OS / Blocked by allowlist`), then `confirm: "Configure skills now? (recommended)"`.
- Skip affordances everywhere: `"Skip for now"` with hint `` "You can add channels later via `openclaw channels add`" ``; `"Do this later"` → `"When you're ready: openclaw dashboard --no-open"`.
- Outro: `"Onboarding complete. Dashboard opened; keep that tab to control OpenClaw."`; closing notes `"Back up your agent workspace."`, `"Running agents on your computer is risky — harden your setup: https://docs.openclaw.ai/security"`, and `'What now: https://openclaw.ai/showcase ("What People Are Building").'`

**Rust equivalents** for deadreckon: `cliclack` or `inquire`/`dialoguer` (for clack-style intro/note/select-with-hints/spinner), `indicatif` for progress, `owo-colors`/`anstyle` theming, `clap` with lazy/sorted help + after-help examples. The load-bearing architecture to copy: (a) a `Prompter` trait with interactive + non-interactive implementations, (b) snapshot-validate config with an allowlist of commands that run on broken config, (c) probe/detect *before* asking and surface findings as menu hints + preselected defaults, (d) every terminal message ends in the next command to run.

Rendered as a VerdictSurface; `deadreckon init` runs `doctor_setup_summary()` (init.rs:70) and its closing verdict flips to Blocked→"deadreckon doctor" if blocking issues exist (init.rs:97-111).
- **`init` flow** (init.rs:3-88): creates home dir, prompts for provider (`prompt_provider`, main.rs:7766 — plain text-input with detected-subscription-CLI default; `--no-confirm` auto-picks installed subscription CLI else "anthropic"), prompts for API key for non-`cli:` providers, writes config.toml, prints provider rows, attempts shell-completion install, prints verdict surface.

- `coherence.rs::top_help_names_audience_and_start_path` (433) — wants audience copy near the top.
- `coherence.rs::top_help_uses_canonical_discovery_words` (693) — pins exact strings AND **absence** patterns like `"{advanced}    "` (an ASCII banner containing words like "run" followed by spaces could trip the negative assertions at 716-719).
- `coherence.rs::help_all_keeps_aliases_inline` (750), `start_command_is_visible_in_top_help_and_help_all` (451), `audience_copy_does_not_call_deadreckon_a_provider_replacement` (663).
- `friendliness_contract.rs` row for `help-all` (src/friendliness_contract.rs:69-72) if behavior class changes.
- Help is colored only on TTY (`ui_heading`/`ui_command` gate through `ui::enabled`), and these tests capture piped stdout, so color is safe but literal text/widths are not.

**(c) Prompts re-rendered by a new library**
- Unit tests inside `prompt.rs` itself (prompt.rs:526-724): menu_step keyboard semantics, Esc→cancel-choice behavior, digit accumulation, `menu_fits` fallback, `truncate_menu_line` widths, `\r\n` raw-mode line endings, **`style_menu_row` no-color-off-TTY guarantee**, `paint_menu_row` width invariance.
- `crates/deadreckon/tests/codebase.rs:765-800` (`config_remove_provider_without_arg_prompts_configured_provider_choices`) — drives the real binary with `DEADRECKON_PROMPT_LINE_MODE=1`, pipes `1\n`, asserts literal `"Remove provider"` and `"[1] anthropic"`. Any new library must preserve the env-var line-mode escape hatch and the `[n] label` rendering, or this breaks.
- `src/tui_tests.rs:1977-2018+` — `ScriptedStartPrompter` implements `StartPrompter` against `SelectPrompt`/`SelectChoice` types and pins prompt titles and choice ids (tests at 2439, 2467, 2596, 2618, 2640, 2677, 2723…). Changing the prompt-type signatures breaks these; changing only rendering does not.
- `tests/smoke_invariant.rs` + `tests/.smoke-baseline` if prompt output leaks into smoke narrative (prompts are TTY-gated so likely safe).
- Goldens in `tests/goldens/characterization/` are off-TTY captures; safe so long as the new library stays silent off-TTY (the current `ui::enabled`/`should_use_selectable_menu` discipline is the contract to keep).
- Also note `main.rs:7785` `prompt_non_git_mode` is a stderr-printed hand-rolled menu — divergent from prompt.rs and a prime unification target.
```

13	// DisplayLogoAndHelp prints the SpecStory logo followed by the command's help text.
14	// Exported because it's used by both the help command and the root command's Run handler.
15	func DisplayLogoAndHelp(cmd *cobra.Command) {
16		fmt.Println() // Add visual separation before the logo
17		fmt.Println(utils.GetRandomLogo())
18		_ = cmd.Help()
19	}
20	
21	// CreateHelpCommand creates a custom help command that displays the SpecStory logo.
22	// rootCmd is needed to look up subcommands when the user types "specstory help <command>".
23	func CreateHelpCommand(rootCmd *cobra.Command) *cobra.Command {
24		return &cobra.Command{
25			Use:     "help [command]",
26			Aliases: []string{"h"},
27			Short:   "Help about any command",
28			Run: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {
29				// Track help command usage with context about why help was shown
30				helpTopic := "general"
31				helpReason := "requested"
32	
33				// If a subcommand is specified, determine if it's valid
34				if len(args) > 0 {
35					targetCmd, _, err := rootCmd.Find(args)
36					if err != nil {
37						// Unknown command - track as error-triggered help
38						helpReason = "unknown_command"
39						fmt.Printf("Unknown command: %s\n", args[0])
40						DisplayLogoAndHelp(rootCmd)
41					} else {
42						// Valid command - track the specific topic
43						helpTopic = args[0]
44						DisplayLogoAndHelp(targetCmd)
45					}
46				} else {
47					// No command specified - general help requested
48					DisplayLogoAndHelp(rootCmd)
49				}
50	
51				// Track analytics after determining the context
52				analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventHelpCommand, analytics.Properties{
53					"help_topic":  helpTopic,
54					"help_reason": helpReason,
55				})
56			},
57		}
58	}

84	// validateFlags checks for mutually exclusive flag combinations
85	func validateFlags() error {
86		if console && silent {
87			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use `console` and `silent` together. These are mutually exclusive"}
88		}
89		if debug && !console && !logFile {
90			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "`debug` requires either `console` or `log` to be specified"}
91		}
92		if onlyCloudSync && noCloudSync {
93			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use `only-cloud-sync` and `no-cloud-sync` together. These are mutually exclusive"}
94		}
95		if onlyStats && onlyCloudSync {
96			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use --only-stats and --only-cloud-sync together. These flags are mutually exclusive"}
97		}
98		if onlyStats && noCloudSync {
99			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "--only-stats already skips cloud sync, no need for --no-cloud-sync"}
100		}
101		if onlyStats && printToStdout {
102			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use --only-stats and --print together. These flags are mutually exclusive"}
103		}
104		if printToStdout && onlyCloudSync {
105			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use --print and `only-cloud-sync` together. These are mutually exclusive"}
106		}
107		if printToStdout && console {
108			return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use --print and `console` together. Console debug output would interleave with markdown on stdout"}
109		}
110		return nil
111	}

316					registry := factory.GetRegistry()
317					ids := registry.ListIDs()
318					example := "specstory run <provider> -c \"/custom/path/to/agent\""
319					if len(ids) > 0 {
320						example = fmt.Sprintf("specstory run %s -c \"/custom/path/to/agent\"", ids[0])
321					}
322					return utils.ValidationError{
323						Message: "The -c/--command flag requires a provider to be specified.\n" +
324							"Example: " + example,
325					}
326				}
327				return nil
328			},
329			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
330				config.EnsureDefaultProjectConfig()
331				slog.Info("Running in interactive mode")
332	
333				// Get custom command if provided via flag
334				customCmd, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("command")
335	
336				// Get the provider
337				registry := factory.GetRegistry()
338				var providerID string
339				if len(args) == 0 {
340					// Default to first registered provider
341					ids := registry.ListIDs()
342					if len(ids) > 0 {
343						providerID = ids[0]
344					} else {
345						return fmt.Errorf("no providers registered")
346					}
347				} else {
348					providerID = args[0]
349				}
350	
351				provider, err := registry.Get(providerID)
352				if err != nil {
353					// Provider not found - show helpful error
354					fmt.Printf("❌ Provider '%s' is not a valid provider implementation\n\n", providerID)
355	
356					ids := registry.ListIDs()
357					if len(ids) > 0 {
358						fmt.Println("The registered providers are:")
359						for _, id := range ids {
360							if p, _ := registry.Get(id); p != nil {
361								fmt.Printf("  • %s - %s\n", id, p.Name())
362							}
363						}
364						fmt.Println("\nExample: specstory run " + ids[0])
365					}
366					return err
367				}
368	
369				// Fall back to config file provider command if -c flag wasn't provided
370				if customCmd == "" && loadedConfig != nil {
371					customCmd = loadedConfig.GetProviderCmd(providerID)
372				}
373	
374				slog.Info("Launching agent", "provider", provider.Name())
375	
376				// Set the agent provider for analytics
377				analytics.SetAgentProviders([]string{provider.Name()})
378	
379				// Setup output configuration
380				config, err := utils.SetupOutputConfig(outputDir, debugDir)
381				if err != nil {
382					return err
383				}
384				// Ensure history directory exists for interactive mode
385				if err := utils.EnsureHistoryDirectoryExists(config); err != nil {
386					return err
387				}
388	
389				// Initialize project identity
390				cwd, err := os.Getwd()
391				if err != nil {
392					slog.Error("Failed to get current working directory", "error", err)
393					return err
394				}
395				identityManager := utils.NewProjectIdentityManager(cwd)
396				if _, err := identityManager.EnsureProjectIdentity(); err != nil {
397					// Log error but don't fail the command
398					slog.Error("Failed to ensure project identity", "error", err)
399				}
400	
401				// Create context for graceful cancellation (Ctrl+C handling)
402				ctx, cancel := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
403				defer cancel()
404	
405				// Start provenance infrastructure before the agent so all file changes are captured
406				provenanceEngine, provenanceCleanup, err := provenance.StartEngine(provenanceEnabled)
407				if err != nil {
408					return err
409				}
410				defer provenanceCleanup()
411	
412				fsCleanup, err := provenance.StartFSWatcher(ctx, provenanceEngine, cwd)
413				if err != nil {
414					return err
415				}
416				defer fsCleanup()
417	
418				// Check authentication for cloud sync
419				cmdpkg.CheckAndWarnAuthentication(noCloudSync)
420				// Track extension activation
421				analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventExtensionActivated, nil)
422	
423				// Get resume session ID if provided
424				resumeSessionID, _ := cmd.Flags().GetString("resume")
425				if resumeSessionID != "" {
426					resumeSessionID = strings.TrimSpace(resumeSessionID)
427					// Note: Different providers may have different session ID formats
428					// Let the provider validate its own format
429					slog.Info("Resuming session", "sessionId", resumeSessionID)
430				}
431	
432				// Get debug-raw flag value (must be before callback to capture in closure)
433				debugRaw, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("debug-raw")
434				useUTC := !localTimeZone
435	
436				// This callback pattern enables real-time processing of agent sessions
437				// without blocking the agent's execution. As the agent writes updates to its
438				// data files, the provider's watcher detects changes and invokes this callback,
439				// allowing immediate markdown generation and cloud sync. Errors are logged but
440				// don't stop execution because transient failures (e.g., network issues) shouldn't
441				// interrupt the user's coding session.
442				sessionCallback := func(session *spi.AgentChatSession) {
443					if session == nil {
444						return
445					}
446	
447					// Track the session ID for deep linking on exit
448					lastRunSessionID = session.SessionID
449	
450					// Process the session (write markdown and sync to cloud)
451					// Don't show output during interactive run mode
452					// This is autosave mode (true)
453					_, err := sessionpkg.ProcessSingleSession(context.Background(), session, config, sessionpkg.ProcessingOptions{
454						OnlyCloudSync:      onlyCloudSync,
455						IsAutosave:         true,
456						DebugRaw:           debugRaw,
457						UseUTC:             useUTC,
458						NoTelemetryPrompts: noTelemetryPrompts,
459					})
460					if err != nil {
461						// Log error but continue - don't fail the whole run
462						// In interactive mode, we prioritize keeping the agent running.
463						// Failed markdown writes or cloud syncs can be retried later via
464						// the sync command, so we just log and continue.
465						slog.Error("Failed to process session update",
466							"sessionId", session.SessionID,
467							"error", err)
468					}
469	
470					// Push agent events to provenance engine for correlation
471					provenance.ProcessEvents(ctx, provenanceEngine, session)
472				}
473	
474				// Execute the agent and watch for updates
475				slog.Info("Starting agent execution and monitoring", "provider", provider.Name())
476				err = provider.ExecAgentAndWatch(cwd, customCmd, resumeSessionID, debugRaw, sessionCallback)
477	
478				if err != nil {
479					slog.Error("Agent execution failed", "provider", provider.Name(), "error", err)
480				}
481	
482				return err
483			},
484		}
485	}
486	
487	var runCmd *cobra.Command
488	
489	// createSyncCommand dynamically creates the sync command with provider information
490	func createSyncCommand() *cobra.Command {
491		registry := factory.GetRegistry()
492		ids := registry.ListIDs()
493		providerList := registry.GetProviderList()
494	
495		// Build dynamic examples
496		examples := `
497	# Sync all agents with activity
498	specstory sync`
499	
500		if len(ids) > 0 {
501			examples += "\n\n# Sync specific agent"
502			for _, id := range ids {
503				examples += fmt.Sprintf("\nspecstory sync %s", id)
504			}
505		}
506	
507		examples += `
508	
509	# Sync a specific session by UUID
510	specstory sync -s <session-id>
511	
512	# Sync multiple sessions
513	specstory sync -s <session-id-1> -s <session-id-2> -s <session-id-3>
514	
515	# Output session markdown to stdout without saving
516	specstory sync -s <session-id> --print
517	
518	# Output multiple sessions to stdout
519	specstory sync -s <session-id-1> -s <session-id-2> --print
520	
521	# Sync all sessions for the current directory, with console output
522	specstory sync --console
523	
524	# Sync all sessions for the current directory, with a log file
525	specstory sync --log`
526	
527		longDesc := `Create or update markdown files for the agent sessions in the current working directory.
528	
529	By default, syncs all registered providers that have activity.
530	Provide a specific agent ID to sync a specific provider.`
531		if providerList != "No providers registered" {
532			longDesc += "\n\nAvailable provider IDs: " + providerList + "."
533		}
534	
535		return &cobra.Command{
536			Use:     "sync [provider-id]",
537			Aliases: []string{"s"},
538			Short:   "Sync markdown files for terminal coding agent sessions",
539			Long:    longDesc,
540			Example: examples,
541			Args:    cobra.MaximumNArgs(1), // Accept 0 or 1 argument (provider ID)
542			PreRunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
543				// Validate that --print requires -s flag
544				sessionIDs, _ := cmd.Flags().GetStringSlice("session")
545				if printToStdout && len(sessionIDs) == 0 {
546					return utils.ValidationError{Message: "--print requires the -s/--session flag to specify which sessions to output"}
547				}
548				if onlyStats && len(sessionIDs) > 0 {
549					return utils.ValidationError{Message: "cannot use --only-stats with -s/--session. Use --only-stats without -s to collect statistics for all sessions"}
550				}
551				return nil
552			},
553			RunE: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) error {
554				config.EnsureDefaultProjectConfig()
555	
556				// Get session IDs if provided via flag
557				sessionIDs, _ := cmd.Flags().GetStringSlice("session")
558	
559				// Handle specific session sync if -s flag is provided
560				if len(sessionIDs) > 0 {
561					return syncSpecificSessions(cmd, args, sessionIDs)
562				}
563	
564				slog.Info("Running sync command")
565				registry := factory.GetRegistry()
566	
567				// Check if user specified a provider
568				if len(args) > 0 {
569					// Sync specific provider
570					return syncSingleProvider(registry, args[0], cmd)
571				} else {
572					// Sync all providers with activity
573					return syncAllProviders(registry, cmd)
574				}
575			},
576		}
577	}
578	
579	// syncSpecificSessions syncs one or more sessions by their IDs
580	// When printToStdout is set, outputs markdown to stdout instead of saving to files.
581	// args[0] is the optional provider ID
582	func syncSpecificSessions(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string, sessionIDs []string) error {
583		if len(sessionIDs) == 1 {
584			slog.Info("Running single session sync", "sessionId", sessionIDs[0])
585		} else {
586			slog.Info("Running multiple session sync", "sessionCount", len(sessionIDs))
587		}
588	
589		// Get debug-raw flag value
590		debugRaw, _ := cmd.Flags().GetBool("debug-raw")
591		useUTC := !localTimeZone
592	
593		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
594		if err != nil {
595			slog.Error("Failed to get current working directory", "error", err)
596			return err
597		}
598	
599		// Setup file output and cloud sync (not needed for --print mode)
600		var config utils.OutputConfig
601		if !printToStdout {
602			config, err = utils.SetupOutputConfig(outputDir, debugDir)
603			if err != nil {
604				return err
605			}
606	
607			identityManager := utils.NewProjectIdentityManager(cwd)
608			if _, err := identityManager.EnsureProjectIdentity(); err != nil {
609				slog.Error("Failed to ensure project identity", "error", err)
610			}
611	
612			cmdpkg.CheckAndWarnAuthentication(noCloudSync || onlyStats)
613	
614			if err := utils.EnsureHistoryDirectoryExists(config); err != nil {
615				return err
616			}
617		}
618	
619		registry := factory.GetRegistry()
620	
621		// Track statistics for summary output
622		var successCount, notFoundCount, errorCount int
623		var lastError error
624	
625		// Resolve provider once if specified (fail fast if provider not found)
626		var specifiedProvider spi.Provider
627		if len(args) > 0 {
628			providerID := args[0]
629			provider, err := registry.Get(providerID)
630			if err != nil {
631				if !printToStdout {
632					fmt.Printf("❌ Provider '%s' not found\n", providerID)
633				}
634				return fmt.Errorf("provider '%s' not found: %w", providerID, err)
635			}
636			specifiedProvider = provider
637		}
638	
639		// Process each session ID
640		var printedSessions int // tracks sessions printed to stdout for separator logic
641		for _, sessionID := range sessionIDs {
642			sessionID = strings.TrimSpace(sessionID)
643			if sessionID == "" {
644				continue // Skip empty session IDs
645			}
646	
647			// Find session across providers
648			var session *spi.AgentChatSession
649	
650			// Case A: Provider was specified - use it directly
651			if specifiedProvider != nil {
652				session, err = specifiedProvider.GetAgentChatSession(cwd, sessionID, debugRaw)
653				if err != nil {
654					if !printToStdout {
655						fmt.Printf("❌ Error getting session '%s' from %s: %v\n", sessionID, specifiedProvider.Name(), err)
656					}
657					slog.Error("Error getting session from provider", "sessionId", sessionID, "provider", specifiedProvider.Name(), "error", err)
658					errorCount++
659					lastError = err
660					continue
661				}
662				if session == nil {
663					if !printToStdout {
664						fmt.Printf("❌ Session '%s' not found in %s\n", sessionID, specifiedProvider.Name())
665					}
666					slog.Warn("Session not found in provider", "sessionId", sessionID, "provider", specifiedProvider.Name())
667					notFoundCount++
668					continue
669				}
670			} else {
671				// Case B: No provider specified - try all providers
672				providerIDs := registry.ListIDs()
673				for _, id := range providerIDs {
674					provider, err := registry.Get(id)
675					if err != nil {
676						continue
677					}
678	
679					session, err = provider.GetAgentChatSession(cwd, sessionID, debugRaw)
680					if err != nil {
681						slog.Debug("Error checking provider for session", "provider", id, "sessionId", sessionID, "error", err)
682						continue
683					}
684					if session != nil {
685						if !silent && !printToStdout {
686							fmt.Printf("✅ Found session '%s' for %s\n", sessionID, provider.Name())
687						}
688						break // Found it, don't check other providers
689					}
690				}
691	
692				if session == nil {
693					if !printToStdout {
694						fmt.Printf("❌ Session '%s' not found in any provider\n", sessionID)
695					}
696					slog.Warn("Session not found in any provider", "sessionId", sessionID)
697					notFoundCount++
698					continue
699				}
700			}
701	
702			// Process the found session
703			if printToStdout {
704				sessionpkg.ValidateSessionData(session, debugRaw)
705				sessionpkg.WriteDebugSessionData(session, debugRaw)
706	
707				markdownContent, err := sessionpkg.GenerateMarkdownFromAgentSession(session.SessionData, false, useUTC)
708				if err != nil {
709					slog.Error("Failed to generate markdown", "sessionId", session.SessionID, "error", err)
710					analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownError, analytics.Properties{
711						"session_id": session.SessionID,
712						"error":      err.Error(),
713						"mode":       "print",
714					})
715					errorCount++
716					lastError = err
717					continue
718				}
719	
720				// Separate multiple sessions with a horizontal rule
721				if printedSessions > 0 {
722					fmt.Print("\n---\n\n")
723				}
724				fmt.Print(markdownContent)
725				printedSessions++
726				successCount++
727				analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownSuccess, analytics.Properties{
728					"session_id": session.SessionID,
729					"mode":       "print",
730				})
731			} else {
732				// Normal sync: write to file and optionally cloud sync
733				if _, err := sessionpkg.ProcessSingleSession(context.Background(), session, config, sessionpkg.ProcessingOptions{
734					OnlyCloudSync:      onlyCloudSync,
735					ShowOutput:         true,
736					DebugRaw:           debugRaw,
737					UseUTC:             useUTC,
738					NoTelemetryPrompts: noTelemetryPrompts,
739				}); err != nil {
740					errorCount++
741					lastError = err
742				} else {
743					successCount++
744				}
745			}
746		}
747	
748		// Print summary if multiple sessions were processed (not for --print mode)
749		if !printToStdout && len(sessionIDs) > 1 && !silent {
750			fmt.Println()
751			fmt.Println("📊 Session sync summary:")
752			fmt.Printf("  ✅ %d %s successfully synced\n", successCount, pluralSession(successCount))
753			if notFoundCount > 0 {
754				fmt.Printf("  ❌ %d %s not found\n", notFoundCount, pluralSession(notFoundCount))
755			}
756			if errorCount > 0 {
757				fmt.Printf("  ❌ %d %s failed with errors\n", errorCount, pluralSession(errorCount))
758			}
759			fmt.Println()
760		}
761	
762		// Return error if any sessions failed
763		if errorCount > 0 || (notFoundCount > 0 && successCount == 0) {
764			if lastError != nil {
765				return lastError
766			}
767			return fmt.Errorf("%d %s not found", notFoundCount, pluralSession(notFoundCount))
768		}
769	
770		return nil
771	}
772	
773	// preloadBulkSessionSizesIfNeeded optimizes bulk syncs by fetching all session sizes upfront.
774	// This avoids making individual HEAD requests for each session during sync operations.
775	//
776	// The function only performs the preload if:
777	//   - Cloud sync is enabled (noCloudSync flag is false)
778	//   - User is authenticated with SpecStory Cloud
779	//   - A valid projectID can be determined from the identity manager
780	//
781	// Parameters:
782	//   - identityManager: Provides project identity (git_id or workspace_id) for the current project
783	//
784	// The preloaded sizes are cached in the SyncManager and shared across all providers since they
785	// use the same projectID. If the bulk fetch fails or if projectID cannot be determined, individual
786	// sessions will gracefully fall back to HEAD requests during sync.
787	//
788	// This function is safe to call multiple times but should typically be called once before processing
789	// multiple sessions in batch sync operations.
790	func preloadBulkSessionSizesIfNeeded(identityManager *utils.ProjectIdentityManager) {
791		// Skip if cloud sync is disabled or user is not authenticated
792		if noCloudSync || !cloud.IsAuthenticated() {
793			return
794		}
795	
796		// Get projectID from identity manager - required for cloud sync
797		projectID, err := identityManager.GetProjectID()
798		if err != nil {
799			slog.Warn("Cannot preload session sizes: failed to get project ID", "error", err)
800			return
801		}
802	
803		// Preload bulk sizes once - shared across all providers since they use same projectID
804		if syncMgr := cloud.GetSyncManager(); syncMgr != nil {
805			syncMgr.PreloadSessionSizes(projectID)
806		} else {
807			slog.Warn("Cannot preload session sizes: sync manager is nil despite authentication")
808		}
809	}
810	
811	// syncProvider performs the actual sync for a single provider.
812	// The caller-provided statsCollector accumulates statistics across providers so
813	// they can be flushed to disk in a single I/O operation after all providers are done.
814	// Returns (sessionCount, error) for analytics tracking.
815	func syncProvider(provider spi.Provider, providerID string, config utils.OutputConfig, debugRaw bool, useUTC bool, statsCollector *sessionpkg.StatisticsCollector) (int, error) {
816		cwd, err := os.Getwd()
817		if err != nil {
818			slog.Error("Failed to get current working directory", "error", err)
819			return 0, err
820		}
821	
822		// Create progress callback for parsing phase
823		// The callback updates the "Parsing..." line in place with [n/m] progress
824		var parseProgress spi.ProgressCallback
825		if !silent {
826			providerName := provider.Name()
827			parseProgress = func(current, total int) {
828				fmt.Printf("\rParsing %s sessions [%d/%d]", providerName, current, total)
829				_ = os.Stdout.Sync()
830			}
831		}
832	
833		// Get all sessions from the provider
834		sessions, err := provider.GetAgentChatSessions(cwd, debugRaw, parseProgress)
835		if err != nil {
836			return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to get sessions: %w", err)
837		}
838	
839		sessionCount := len(sessions)
840	
841		if sessionCount == 0 && !silent {
842			// This comes after "Parsing..." message, on the same line
843			fmt.Printf(", no non-empty sessions found for %s\n", provider.Name())
844			fmt.Println()
845			return 0, nil
846		}
847	
848		if !silent && !onlyStats {
849			fmt.Printf("\nSyncing markdown files for %s", provider.Name())
850		}
851	
852		// Initialize statistics
853		stats := &SyncStats{
854			TotalSessions: sessionCount,
855		}
856	
857		historyPath := config.GetHistoryDir()
858		agentName := provider.Name()
859		ctx := context.Background()
860	
861		// Process each session
862		for i := range sessions {
863			session := &sessions[i]
864	
865			// Process session in a closure so defers scope to each iteration,
866			// ensuring spans are ended and metrics recorded even on early returns.
867			func() {
868				processingStart := time.Now()
869	
870				// Create a context with a deterministic trace ID from the session ID
871				sessionCtx := telemetry.ContextWithSessionTrace(ctx, session.SessionID)
872	
873				// Start an OTel span for this session processing
874				sessionCtx, span := telemetry.Tracer("specstory").Start(sessionCtx, "process_session")
875				defer span.End()
876	
877				// Compute session statistics
878				sessionStats := telemetry.ComputeSessionStats(agentName, session)
879				defer func() {
880					telemetry.RecordSessionMetrics(sessionCtx, sessionStats, time.Since(processingStart))
881				}()
882	
883				// Set session span attributes
884				telemetry.SetSessionSpanAttributes(span, sessionStats)
885	
886				// Create child spans for each exchange
887				if session.SessionData != nil && len(session.SessionData.Exchanges) > 0 {
888					telemetry.ProcessExchangeSpans(sessionCtx, sessionStats, session.SessionData.Exchanges, noTelemetryPrompts)
889				}
890	
891				sessionpkg.ValidateSessionData(session, debugRaw)
892				sessionpkg.WriteDebugSessionData(session, debugRaw)
893	
894				// Generate markdown from SessionData
895				markdownContent, err := sessionpkg.GenerateMarkdownFromAgentSession(session.SessionData, false, useUTC)
896				if err != nil {
897					slog.Error("Failed to generate markdown from SessionData",
898						"sessionId", session.SessionID,
899						"error", err)
900					// Track sync error
901					analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownError, analytics.Properties{
902						"session_id": session.SessionID,
903						"error":      err.Error(),
904					})
905					return
906				}
907	
908				// Compute statistics from the SessionData
909				sessionStatistics := sessionpkg.ComputeSessionStatistics(session.SessionData, markdownContent, providerID)
910				statsCollector.AddSessionStats(session.SessionID, sessionStatistics)
911	
912				// In only-stats mode, skip file writes and cloud sync
913				if onlyStats {
914					stats.SessionsSkipped++
915					slog.Info("Skipping local file write (only-stats mode)", "sessionId", session.SessionID)
916					return
917				}
918	
919				// Generate filename from timestamp and slug
920				fileFullPath := sessionpkg.BuildSessionFilePath(session, historyPath, useUTC)
921	
922				// Check if file already exists with same content
923				identicalContent := false
924				fileExists := false
925				if existingContent, err := os.ReadFile(fileFullPath); err == nil {
926					fileExists = true
927					if string(existingContent) == markdownContent {
928						identicalContent = true
929						slog.Info("Markdown file already exists with same content, skipping write",
930							"sessionId", session.SessionID,
931							"path", fileFullPath)
932					}
933				}
934	
935				// Write file if needed (skip if only-cloud-sync is enabled)
936				if !onlyCloudSync {
937					if !identicalContent {
938						// Ensure history directory exists (handles deletion during long-running sync)
939						if err := utils.EnsureHistoryDirectoryExists(config); err != nil {
940							slog.Error("Failed to ensure history directory", "error", err)
941							return
942						}
943						err := os.WriteFile(fileFullPath, []byte(markdownContent), 0644)
944						if err != nil {
945							slog.Error("Error writing markdown file",
946								"sessionId", session.SessionID,
947								"error", err)
948							// Track sync error

950								"session_id":      session.SessionID,

952								"only_cloud_sync": onlyCloudSync,
953							})
954							return
955						}
956						slog.Info("Successfully wrote file",
957							"sessionId", session.SessionID,

960						// Track successful sync
961						if !fileExists {
962							analytics.TrackEvent(analytics.EventSyncMarkdownNew, analytics.Properties{
963								"session_id":      session.SessionID,
964								"only_cloud_sync": onlyCloudSync,
965							})

969								"only_cloud_sync": onlyCloudSync,
970							})
971						}
972					}
973	
974					// Update statistics for normal mode
975					if identicalContent {
976						stats.SessionsSkipped++
977					} else if fileExists {
978						stats.SessionsUpdated++
979					} else {
980						stats.SessionsCreated++
981					}
982				} else {
983					// In cloud-only mode, count as skipped since no local file operation occurred
984					stats.SessionsSkipped++
985					slog.Info("Skipping local file write (only-cloud-sync mode)",
986						"sessionId", session.SessionID)
987				}
988	
989				// Trigger cloud sync with provider-specific data
990				// Manual sync command: perform immediate sync with HEAD check (not autosave mode)
991				// In only-cloud-sync mode: always sync
992				cloud.SyncSessionToCloud(session.SessionID, fileFullPath, markdownContent, []byte(session.RawData), provider.Name(), false)
993			}()

1003		if !silent && sessionCount > 0 && !onlyCloudSync && !onlyStats {
1004			fmt.Println()

1007			actualTotal := stats.SessionsSkipped + stats.SessionsUpdated + stats.SessionsCreated
1008	
1009			// Print summary message with proper pluralization
1010			fmt.Printf("\n%s✅ %s sync complete!%s 📊 %s%d%s %s processed\n",
1011				log.ColorBoldGreen, provider.Name(), log.ColorReset,
1012				log.ColorBoldCyan, actualTotal, log.ColorReset, pluralSession(actualTotal))
1013			fmt.Println()

1016				log.ColorCyan, stats.SessionsSkipped, pluralSession(stats.SessionsSkipped), log.ColorReset)

1020				log.ColorGreen, stats.SessionsCreated, pluralSession(stats.SessionsCreated), log.ColorReset)

1304			case "--console":
1305				console = true
1306			case "--log":

1313				noVersionCheck = true
1314			case "--no-telemetry-prompts":
1315				noTelemetryPrompts = true
1316			case "--output-dir":
1317				// Handle --output-dir <value> format (space-separated)
1318				if i+1 < len(args) && !strings.HasPrefix(args[i+1], "-") {
1319					outputDir = utils.ExpandTilde(args[i+1])
1320					i++ // Skip the value in next iteration
1321				}
1322			case "--telemetry-endpoint":
1323				if i+1 < len(args) && !strings.HasPrefix(args[i+1], "-") {
1324					telemetryEndpoint = args[i+1]
1325					i++ // Skip the value in next iteration
1326				}
1327			case "--telemetry-service-name":

1341			}

103	fn select_one_menu(prompt: &SelectPrompt) -> Result<SelectChoice> {
104	    // A list taller than the terminal can't be redrawn in place; use line mode.
105	    if !menu_fits(prompt.choices.len(), terminal_rows()) {
106	        return select_one_line(prompt);
107	    }
108	    print_select_header(prompt);
109	    let mut selected = prompt
110	        .default_index
111	        .min(prompt.choices.len().saturating_sub(1));
112	    let cancel_index = cancel_choice_index(prompt);
113	    let mut buffer = String::new();
114	    let _raw_mode = RawModeGuard::enable()?;
115	    render_select_menu(prompt, selected, false, false)?;
116	    loop {
117	        let Event::Key(key) = event::read()? else {
118	            continue;
119	        };
120	        match menu_step(
121	            prompt.choices.len(),
122	            selected,
123	            cancel_index,
124	            &mut buffer,
125	            key,
126	        ) {
127	            MenuStep::Move(new_selected) => {
128	                selected = new_selected;
129	                buffer.clear();
130	                render_select_menu(prompt, selected, true, false)?;
131	            }
132	            MenuStep::Commit(index) => {
133	                finish_select_menu_line()?;
134	                return Ok(prompt.choices[index].clone());
135	            }
136	            MenuStep::Accumulate => {
137	                render_select_menu(prompt, selected, true, false)?;
138	            }
139	            MenuStep::Reject => {
140	                render_select_menu(prompt, selected, true, true)?;
141	            }
142	            MenuStep::Cancel | MenuStep::Interrupt => {
143	                finish_select_menu_line()?;
144	                return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted, "prompt cancelled").into());
145	            }
146	            MenuStep::Ignore => {}
147	        }
148	    }
149	}

151	fn render_select_menu(
152	    prompt: &SelectPrompt,
153	    selected: usize,
154	    redraw: bool,
155	    out_of_range: bool,
156	) -> Result<()> {
157	    let mut stdout = io::stdout();
158	    if redraw {
159	        execute!(stdout, MoveUp(prompt.choices.len() as u16), MoveToColumn(0))?;

161	    let width = selectable_menu_width();
162	    for (index, choice) in prompt.choices.iter().enumerate() {
163	        let ordinal = index + 1;
164	        let selected_row = index == selected;
165	        let marker = if selected_row { ">" } else { " " };
166	        execute!(stdout, Clear(ClearType::CurrentLine))?;

168	            Some(detail) if !detail.trim().is_empty() => {
169	                format!("  {marker} [{ordinal}] {} - {detail}", choice.label)
170	            }
171	            _ => format!("  {marker} [{ordinal}] {}", choice.label),
172	        };
173	        let line = style_menu_row(&truncate_menu_line(&line, width), ordinal, selected_row);
174	        write_select_menu_line(&mut stdout, &line)?;
175	    }
176	    execute!(stdout, Clear(ClearType::CurrentLine))?;
177	    let default = prompt
178	        .default_index
179	        .min(prompt.choices.len().saturating_sub(1))
180	        + 1;
181	    let notice = if out_of_range {
182	        format!(" — choose 1-{}", prompt.choices.len())
183	    } else {
184	        String::new()
185	    };
186	    write!(
187	        stdout,
188	        "{} {} ",
189	        ui::render(Stream::Stdout, Tone::Prompt, "?"),
190	        ui::render(
191	            Stream::Stdout,
192	            Tone::Muted,
193	            format!("choose [{default}]: arrows/Enter, number, Esc to cancel{notice}"),
194	        )
195	    )?;
196	    stdout.flush()?;
197	    Ok(())
198	}

218	/// Colorize a normalized, already-truncated select-menu row. Color is applied
219	/// only on a TTY (ui::render is gated) and only after width truncation, so the
220	/// visible width is unchanged and the redraw (MoveUp by line count) math holds.
221	fn style_menu_row(line: &str, ordinal: usize, selected: bool) -> String {
222	    if !ui::enabled(Stream::Stdout) {
223	        return line.to_string();
224	    }
225	    paint_menu_row(line, ordinal, selected, |tone, text| {
226	        ui::render(Stream::Stdout, tone, text)

230	/// Pure painter for a select-menu row: splits the line into `lead | [n] | body`
231	/// and applies `paint` to the marker, ordinal, and (for the selected row) the
232	/// label, dimming the trailing detail. `paint` only ever wraps tokens, so the
233	/// visible width equals the input — stripping the result yields `line` again.
234	fn paint_menu_row(
235	    line: &str,
236	    ordinal: usize,
237	    selected: bool,
238	    paint: impl Fn(Tone, &str) -> String,
239	) -> String {
240	    let token = format!("[{ordinal}]");
241	    let Some(at) = line.find(&token) else {
242	        return line.to_string();
243	    };
244	    let lead = &line[..at];
245	    let rest = &line[at + token.len()..];
246	    let lead = if selected {
247	        lead.replacen('>', &paint(Tone::Prompt, ">"), 1)
248	    } else {
249	        lead.to_string()
250	    };
251	    let number = paint(Tone::Command, &token);
252	    let body = match rest.split_once(" - ") {
253	        Some((label, detail)) => {
254	            let label = if selected {
255	                paint(Tone::Heading, label)
256	            } else {
257	                label.to_string()
258	            };
259	            format!("{label} - {}", paint(Tone::Muted, detail))
260	        }
261	        None if selected => paint(Tone::Heading, rest),
262	        None => rest.to_string(),
263	    };
264	    format!("{lead}{number}{body}")
265	}

267	fn selectable_menu_width() -> usize {
268	    crossterm::terminal::size()
269	        .ok()
270	        .map(|(columns, _)| usize::from(columns))
271	        .or_else(|| {
272	            std::env::var("COLUMNS")
273	                .ok()
274	                .and_then(|columns| columns.parse::<usize>().ok())
275	        })
276	        .filter(|columns| *columns > 1)
277	        .map(|columns| columns.saturating_sub(1))
278	        .unwrap_or(119)
279	}

281	fn truncate_menu_line(line: &str, max_visible: usize) -> String {
282	    let normalized = normalize_menu_line(line);
283	    if normalized.chars().count() <= max_visible {
284	        return normalized;
285	    }
286	    if max_visible == 0 {
287	        return String::new();
288	    }
289	    if max_visible <= 3 {
290	        return normalized.chars().take(max_visible).collect();
291	    }
292	    let keep = max_visible.saturating_sub(3);
293	    let mut out = normalized.chars().take(keep).collect::<String>();
294	    out.push_str("...");
295	    out
296	}
297	
298	fn normalize_menu_line(line: &str) -> String {
299	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(line.len());
300	    let mut previous_was_space = false;
301	    for ch in line.chars() {
302	        if ch.is_whitespace() {
303	            if !previous_was_space {
304	                out.push(' ');
305	                previous_was_space = true;
306	            }
307	        } else {
308	            out.push(ch);
309	            previous_was_space = false;
310	        }
311	    }
312	    out.trim_end().to_string()
313	}

321	#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
322	enum DigitResolution {
323	    Commit(usize),
324	    Accumulate,
325	    OutOfRange,
326	}
327	
328	/// Resolve an accumulated digit `buffer` against a menu of `len` choices. Commits
329	/// as soon as no longer prefix could be valid, so single-digit menus feel instant
330	/// while menus with 10+ choices accept multi-digit entry.
331	fn resolve_digit_selection(buffer: &str, len: usize) -> DigitResolution {
332	    let Ok(value) = buffer.parse::<usize>() else {
333	        return DigitResolution::OutOfRange;
334	    };
335	    if value == 0 || value > len {
336	        return DigitResolution::OutOfRange;
337	    }
338	    if value.saturating_mul(10) > len {
339	        DigitResolution::Commit(value - 1)
340	    } else {
341	        DigitResolution::Accumulate
342	    }
343	}
344	
345	#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
346	enum MenuStep {
347	    Move(usize),
348	    Commit(usize),
349	    Accumulate,
350	    Reject,
351	    Cancel,
352	    Interrupt,
353	    Ignore,
354	}
355	
356	/// Pure key-dispatch for the selectable menu, factored out so the keyboard and
357	/// number-input behavior is unit-testable without a real TTY. `buffer` holds the
358	/// in-progress multi-digit selection and is mutated as digits arrive.
359	fn menu_step(
360	    choice_count: usize,
361	    selected: usize,
362	    cancel_index: Option<usize>,
363	    buffer: &mut String,
364	    key: KeyEvent,
365	) -> MenuStep {
366	    if matches!(key.kind, KeyEventKind::Release) {
367	        return MenuStep::Ignore;
368	    }
369	    match key.code {
370	        KeyCode::Char('c') if key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL) => MenuStep::Interrupt,
371	        KeyCode::Char('j' | 'm') if key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL) => {
372	            MenuStep::Commit(selected)
373	        }
374	        KeyCode::Enter => {
375	            if !buffer.is_empty()
376	                && let Ok(value) = buffer.parse::<usize>()
377	                && (1..=choice_count).contains(&value)
378	            {
379	                return MenuStep::Commit(value - 1);
380	            }
381	            MenuStep::Commit(selected)
382	        }
383	        KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Char('k') if key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
384	            MenuStep::Move(selected.saturating_sub(1))
385	        }
386	        KeyCode::Down | KeyCode::Char('j') if key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
387	            MenuStep::Move((selected + 1).min(choice_count.saturating_sub(1)))
388	        }
389	        KeyCode::Home => MenuStep::Move(0),
390	        KeyCode::End => MenuStep::Move(choice_count.saturating_sub(1)),
391	        KeyCode::Char(value) if key.modifiers.is_empty() && value.is_ascii_digit() => {
392	            buffer.push(value);
393	            match resolve_digit_selection(buffer, choice_count) {
394	                DigitResolution::Commit(index) => MenuStep::Commit(index),
395	                DigitResolution::Accumulate => MenuStep::Accumulate,
396	                DigitResolution::OutOfRange => {
397	                    buffer.clear();
398	                    MenuStep::Reject
399	                }
400	            }
401	        }
402	        KeyCode::Esc => match cancel_index {
403	            Some(index) => MenuStep::Commit(index),
404	            None => MenuStep::Cancel,
405	        },
406	        _ => MenuStep::Ignore,
407	    }
408	}
409	
410	fn cancel_choice_index(prompt: &SelectPrompt) -> Option<usize> {
411	    prompt
412	        .choices
413	        .iter()
414	        .position(|choice| choice.id == "cancel")
415	}

417	/// Whether a menu of `choice_count` choices fits in a terminal `rows` tall. Tall
418	/// menus fall back to line mode because the raw-mode redraw can only MoveUp
419	/// within the visible region (a taller list corrupts the screen).
420	fn menu_fits(choice_count: usize, rows: usize) -> bool {
421	    // title + optional help + the prompt line + a little slack.
422	    choice_count + 4 <= rows
423	}

425	fn terminal_rows() -> usize {

427	        .ok()
428	        .map(|(_, rows)| usize::from(rows))
429	        .filter(|rows| *rows > 0)
430	        .unwrap_or(24)
431	}

448	pub(crate) fn confirm(question: &str, default_yes: bool) -> Result<bool> {
449	    let marker = if default_yes { "[Y/n]" } else { "[y/N]" };
450	    loop {
451	        let answer = open(&format!("{question} {marker}: "), None)?;
452	        if let Some(value) = parse_confirm_answer(&answer, default_yes) {
453	            return Ok(value);
454	        }
455	        println!("Please answer y or n.");
456	    }
457	}
458	
459	fn parse_select_answer(answer: &str, default: usize, len: usize) -> Option<usize> {
460	    if len == 0 {
461	        return None;
462	    }
463	    let trimmed = answer.trim();
464	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
465	        return Some(default.saturating_sub(1).min(len - 1));
466	    }
467	    let value = trimmed.parse::<usize>().ok()?;
468	    if (1..=len).contains(&value) {
469	        Some(value - 1)
470	    } else {
471	        None
472	    }
473	}
474	
475	fn parse_confirm_answer(answer: &str, default_yes: bool) -> Option<bool> {
476	    let trimmed = answer.trim();
477	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
478	        return Some(default_yes);
479	    }
480	    match trimmed.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
481	        "y" | "yes" => Some(true),
482	        "n" | "no" => Some(false),
483	        _ => None,
484	    }
485	}

487	/// Prompt for a number in `range`, re-prompting (never erroring) on empty input
488	/// (which takes `default`), non-numeric input, or an out-of-range value. Use this
489	/// for count-style prompts instead of `open(...).parse()?`, which aborts the whole
490	/// command on a typo.
491	pub(crate) fn ask_number(
492	    label: &str,
493	    range: std::ops::RangeInclusive<usize>,
494	    default: usize,
495	) -> Result<usize> {
496	    loop {
497	        let answer = open(&format!("{label} [{default}]: "), None)?;
498	        if let Some(value) = parse_number_in_range(&answer, &range, default) {
499	            return Ok(value);
500	        }
501	        println!(
502	            "Please enter a number from {} to {}.",
503	            range.start(),
504	            range.end()
505	        );
506	    }
507	}
508	
509	fn parse_number_in_range(
510	    answer: &str,
511	    range: &std::ops::RangeInclusive<usize>,
512	    default: usize,
513	) -> Option<usize> {
514	    let trimmed = answer.trim();
515	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
516	        return Some(default);
517	    }
518	    let value = trimmed.parse::<usize>().ok()?;
519	    if range.contains(&value) {
520	        Some(value)
521	    } else {
522	        None
523	    }
524	}

57	    pub(crate) const fn to_tui_color(self) -> Color {
58	        match self {
59	            Tone::Plain => Color::Reset,
60	            Tone::Heading | Tone::Prompt => Color::Cyan,
61	            Tone::Muted | Tone::Note => Color::DarkGray,
62	            Tone::Id => Color::Magenta,
63	            Tone::Command | Tone::Hint => Color::Blue,
64	            Tone::Ok => Color::Green,
65	            Tone::Warn | Tone::Paused => Color::Yellow,
66	            Tone::Negative => Color::Red,
67	        }
68	    }
69	}

71	/// The closed set of lifecycle status classes. `status_tone` resolves a free-form
72	/// status string into exactly one of these — including an explicit `Unknown` —
73	/// so an unrecognized status renders in a visible default tone rather than being
74	/// silently folded into a dim catch-all, and so adding a class is a compile error.
75	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
76	pub(crate) enum Status {
77	    Ok,
78	    Running,
79	    Paused,
80	    Warn,
81	    Negative,
82	    Note,
83	    Unknown,
84	}
85	
86	impl Status {
87	    pub(crate) fn classify(status: &str) -> Status {
88	        let status = status.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
89	        if status.contains("failed")
90	            || status.contains("killed")
91	            || status.contains("error")
92	            || status.contains("missing")
93	            || status.contains("refused")
94	        {
95	            return Status::Negative;
96	        }
97	        if status.contains("paused") {
98	            return Status::Paused;
99	        }
100	        if status.contains("warning") || status.contains("warn") {
101	            return Status::Warn;
102	        }
103	        match status.as_str() {
104	            "ok" | "ready" | "set" | "wrote" | "updated" | "installed" | "completed" | "passed"
105	            | "polished" | "applied" | "cleaned" | "exported" => Status::Ok,
106	            "running" => Status::Running,
107	            "pending" | "planned" | "skipped" | "undone" | "recorded" | "note" => Status::Note,
108	            _ => Status::Unknown,
109	        }
110	    }
111	
112	    pub(crate) const fn tone(self) -> Tone {
113	        match self {
114	            Status::Ok => Tone::Ok,
115	            Status::Running => Tone::Heading,
116	            Status::Paused => Tone::Paused,
117	            Status::Warn => Tone::Warn,
118	            Status::Negative => Tone::Negative,
119	            Status::Note => Tone::Note,
120	            // Unknown stays a visible default rather than a dim that hides it.
121	            Status::Unknown => Tone::Plain,
122	        }
123	    }
124	}

166	pub(crate) fn enabled(stream: Stream) -> bool {

179	pub(crate) fn render(stream: Stream, tone: Tone, text: impl AsRef<str>) -> String {
180	    let text = text.as_ref();
181	    let Some(code) = tone.to_ansi() else {
182	        return text.to_string();
183	    };
184	    if enabled(stream) {
185	        ansi_wrap(code, text)
186	    } else {
187	        text.to_string()
188	    }
189	}

191	pub(crate) fn ansi_wrap(code: &str, text: &str) -> String {
192	    format!("\x1b[{code}m{text}{ANSI_RESET}")
193	}

197	    ANSI_RESET
198	}

200	#[allow(dead_code)]
201	pub(crate) fn strip_ansi(text: &str) -> String {
202	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
203	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
204	    while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
205	        if read_ansi_sequence(ch, &mut chars).is_some() {
206	            continue;
207	        }
208	        out.push(ch);
209	    }
210	    out
211	}
212	
213	#[allow(dead_code)]
214	pub(crate) fn read_ansi_sequence<I>(first: char, chars: &mut Peekable<I>) -> Option<(String, bool)>
215	where
216	    I: Iterator<Item = char>,
217	{
218	    if first != ANSI_ESC || chars.peek() != Some(&'[') {
219	        return None;
220	    }
221	    let mut sequence = String::from(first);
222	    if let Some(bracket) = chars.next() {
223	        sequence.push(bracket);
224	    }
225	    for code in chars.by_ref() {
226	        sequence.push(code);
227	        if code.is_ascii_alphabetic() {
228	            let active = sequence != ANSI_RESET;
229	            return Some((sequence, active));
230	        }
231	    }
232	    Some((sequence, false))
233	}

235	/// Display width of `text` in terminal columns: ANSI escape sequences are
236	/// stripped first, then each glyph is measured by its Unicode display width so
237	/// wide (CJK / full-width) glyphs count as two columns and zero-width / combining
238	/// marks count as zero. This is the single width function behind every pad,
239	/// truncate, and column-alignment site.
240	#[allow(dead_code)] // used by ui_card today; kv_block/columns/prompt sites adopt it in later phases.
241	pub(crate) fn display_width(text: &str) -> usize {
242	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr;
243	    UnicodeWidthStr::width(strip_ansi(text).as_str())
244	}
245	
246	/// Right-pad `text` with spaces to `width` DISPLAY columns (ANSI-aware). Use this
247	/// for column alignment instead of `{:<N}`: a `{:<N}` format-pad counts the ANSI
248	/// escape bytes of a styled cell, so a colored column ends up short and misaligns
249	/// against its plain header.
250	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P3/P5/P6.
251	pub(crate) fn pad_visible(text: &str, width: usize) -> String {
252	    let used = display_width(text);
253	    if used >= width {
254	        text.to_string()
255	    } else {
256	        format!("{text}{}", " ".repeat(width - used))
257	    }
258	}
259	
260	/// Word-wrap `text` to `width` display columns, breaking words longer than the
261	/// width. This is the single wrap engine behind the kv block, run list, and
262	/// campaign facts. Wrap RAW (unstyled) text — it is ANSI-naive.
263	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P10.
264	pub(crate) fn wrap_words(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
265	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
266	    let width = width.max(1);
267	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
268	    let mut current = String::new();
269	    for word in text.split_whitespace() {
270	        if display_width(word) > width {
271	            if !current.is_empty() {
272	                lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
273	            }
274	            // Break a too-long word into width-sized chunks.
275	            let mut chunk = String::new();
276	            let mut chunk_width = 0usize;
277	            for ch in word.chars() {
278	                let ch_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch).unwrap_or(0);
279	                if chunk_width + ch_width > width {
280	                    lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut chunk));
281	                    chunk_width = 0;
282	                }
283	                chunk.push(ch);
284	                chunk_width += ch_width;
285	            }
286	            current = chunk;
287	            continue;
288	        }
289	        let next = if current.is_empty() {
290	            display_width(word)
291	        } else {
292	            display_width(&current) + 1 + display_width(word)
293	        };
294	        if next <= width {
295	            if !current.is_empty() {
296	                current.push(' ');
297	            }
298	            current.push_str(word);
299	        } else {
300	            lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
301	            current.push_str(word);
302	        }
303	    }
304	    if !current.is_empty() || lines.is_empty() {
305	        lines.push(current);
306	    }
307	    lines
308	}

310	pub(crate) fn status_tone(status: impl AsRef<str>) -> Tone {
311	    Status::classify(status.as_ref()).tone()
312	}
