struct ScriptedStartPrompter {
    choices: VecDeque<String>,
    inputs: VecDeque<String>,
    confirms: VecDeque<bool>,
    prompt_titles: Vec<String>,
}

impl ScriptedStartPrompter {
    fn new(choices: &[&str]) -> Self {
        Self {
            choices: choices.iter().map(|choice| choice.to_string()).collect(),
            inputs: VecDeque::new(),
            confirms: VecDeque::new(),
            prompt_titles: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}

impl StartPrompter for ScriptedStartPrompter {
    fn select_one(
        &mut self,
        prompt: crate::prompt::SelectPrompt,
    ) -> Result<crate::prompt::SelectChoice> {
        self.prompt_titles.push(prompt.title.clone());
        let id = self.choices.pop_front().expect("scripted choice");
        Ok(prompt
            .choices
            .into_iter()
            .find(|choice| choice.id == id)
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("choice {id} not found")))
    }

    fn confirm(&mut self, question: &str, _default_yes: bool) -> Result<bool> {
        self.prompt_titles.push(question.to_string());
        Ok(self.confirms.pop_front().unwrap_or(true))
    }

    fn input(&mut self, message: &str, _default: Option<&str>) -> Result<String> {
        self.prompt_titles.push(message.to_string());
        Ok(self.inputs.pop_front().unwrap_or_default())
    }
}

fn start_args_for_test(goal: &str) -> StartCommandArgs {
    StartCommandArgs {
        goal: goal.to_string(),
        mode: CliStartMode::Auto,
        provider: None,
        children: None,
        planner_provider: None,
        child_provider: Vec::new(),
        coder_provider: None,
        reviewer_provider: None,
        preview: true,
        yes: false,
        no_seams: false,
        fresh: false,
        worktree: false,
        from: None,
        allow_dirty: false,
        plain: false,
        quiet: false,
        json: false,
    }
}

#[test]
fn goal_file_reads_document_goal() {
    let temp = test_tempdir();
    let goal_path = temp.path().join("goal.md");
    std::fs::write(
        &goal_path,
        "\u{feff}\nBuild the dashboard\n\nInclude persistence.\n",
    )
    .expect("write goal");

    let goal = super::resolve_required_goal_input(
        "run",
        None,
        Some(goal_path),
        "deadreckon run --goal-file docs/goal.md",
    )
    .expect("goal");

    assert_eq!(goal, "Build the dashboard\n\nInclude persistence.");
}

#[test]
fn at_goal_reads_document_goal() {
    let temp = test_tempdir();
    let goal_path = temp.path().join("goal.md");
    std::fs::write(&goal_path, "Build from shorthand\n").expect("write goal");

    let goal = super::resolve_required_goal_input(
        "start",
        Some(format!("@{}", goal_path.display())),
        None,
        "deadreckon start --goal-file docs/goal.md",
    )
    .expect("goal");

    assert_eq!(goal, "Build from shorthand");
}

#[test]
fn goal_input_rejects_positional_and_file() {
    let temp = test_tempdir();
    let goal_path = temp.path().join("goal.md");
    std::fs::write(&goal_path, "Build from file\n").expect("write goal");

    let err = super::resolve_required_goal_input(
        "campaign",
        Some("Build inline".to_string()),
        Some(goal_path),
        "deadreckon campaign --goal-file docs/goal.md",
    )
    .expect_err("conflict should fail");

    assert!(
        err.to_string()
            .contains("either a positional goal or --goal-file")
    );
    let surface = err.to_string();
    assert!(surface.contains("blocked campaign"), "{surface}");
    assert!(surface.contains("Explanation\n"), "{surface}");
    assert!(surface.contains("Evidence\n"), "{surface}");
    assert_eq!(surface.matches("\nRecommended\n").count(), 1, "{surface}");
    assert!(
        surface.contains("Recommended\ndeadreckon campaign --goal-file docs/goal.md"),
        "{surface}"
    );
    assert!(!surface.contains("try:"), "{surface}");
}

      }
      const item = line.slice(0, colon).trim();

# Getting Started

Goal: go from zero to a first working chat with minimal setup.

<Info>
Fastest chat: open the Control UI (no channel setup needed). Run `openclaw dashboard`
and chat in the browser, or open `http://127.0.0.1:18789/` on the
<Tooltip headline="Gateway host" tip="The machine running the OpenClaw gateway service.">gateway host</Tooltip>.
Docs: [Dashboard](/web/dashboard) and [Control UI](/web/control-ui).
</Info>

## Prereqs

- Node 22 or newer

<Tip>
Check your Node version with `node --version` if you are unsure.
</Tip>

## Quick setup (CLI)

<Steps>
  <Step title="Install OpenClaw (recommended)">
    <Tabs>
      <Tab title="macOS/Linux">
        ```bash
        curl -fsSL https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash
        ```
        <img
  src="/assets/install-script.svg"
  alt="Install Script Process"
  className="rounded-lg"
/>
      </Tab>
      <Tab title="Windows (PowerShell)">
        ```powershell
        iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex
        ```
      </Tab>
    </Tabs>

    <Note>
    Other install methods and requirements: [Install](/install).
    </Note>

  </Step>
  <Step title="Run the onboarding wizard">
    ```bash
    openclaw onboard --install-daemon
    ```

    The wizard configures auth, gateway settings, and optional channels.
```

# Installer internals

OpenClaw ships three installer scripts, served from `openclaw.ai`.

| Script                             | Platform             | What it does                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`install.sh`](#installsh)         | macOS / Linux / WSL  | Installs Node if needed, installs OpenClaw via npm (default) or git, and can run onboarding. |
| [`install-cli.sh`](#install-clish) | macOS / Linux / WSL  | Installs Node + OpenClaw into a local prefix (`~/.openclaw`). No root required.              |
| [`install.ps1`](#installps1)       | Windows (PowerShell) | Installs Node if needed, installs OpenClaw via npm (default) or git, and can run onboarding. |

## Quick commands

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="install.sh">
    ```bash
    curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash
    ```

    ```bash
    curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --help
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="install-cli.sh">
    ```bash
    curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install-cli.sh | bash
    ```

    ```bash
    curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install-cli.sh | bash -s -- --help
    ```

  </Tab>
  <Tab title="install.ps1">
    ```powershell
    iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1 | iex
    ```

    ```powershell
    & ([scriptblock]::Create((iwr -useb https://openclaw.ai/install.ps1))) -Tag beta -NoOnboard -DryRun
    ```

  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Note>
If install succeeds but `openclaw` is not found in a new terminal, see [Node.js troubleshooting](/install/node#troubleshooting).
</Note>

# `openclaw doctor`

Health checks + quick fixes for the gateway and channels.

Related:

- Troubleshooting: [Troubleshooting](/gateway/troubleshooting)
- Security audit: [Security](/gateway/security)

## Examples

```bash
openclaw doctor
openclaw doctor --repair
openclaw doctor --deep
```

Notes:

- Interactive prompts (like keychain/OAuth fixes) only run when stdin is a TTY and `--non-interactive` is **not** set. Headless runs (cron, Telegram, no terminal) will skip prompts.
- `--fix` (alias for `--repair`) writes a backup to `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json.bak` and drops unknown config keys, listing each removal.

## macOS: `launchctl` env overrides

If you previously ran `launchctl setenv OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN ...` (or `...PASSWORD`), that value overrides your config file and can cause persistent “unauthorized” errors.

```bash
launchctl getenv OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN
launchctl getenv OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD

launchctl unsetenv OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN
launchctl unsetenv OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD
```

```text
  <Step title="Detect OS">
    Supports macOS and Linux (including WSL). If macOS is detected, installs Homebrew if missing.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Ensure Node.js 22+">
    Checks Node version and installs Node 22 if needed (Homebrew on macOS, NodeSource setup scripts on Linux apt/dnf/yum).
  </Step>
  <Step title="Ensure Git">
    Installs Git if missing.
  </Step>
  <Step title="Install OpenClaw">
    - `npm` method (default): global npm install
    - `git` method: clone/update repo, install deps with pnpm, build, then install wrapper at `~/.local/bin/openclaw`
  </Step>
  <Step title="Post-install tasks">
    - Runs `openclaw doctor --non-interactive` on upgrades and git installs (best effort)
    - Attempts onboarding when appropriate (TTY available, onboarding not disabled, and bootstrap/config checks pass)
    - Defaults `SHARP_IGNORE_GLOBAL_LIBVIPS=1`
  </Step>
</Steps>

### Source checkout detection

If run inside an OpenClaw checkout (`package.json` + `pnpm-workspace.yaml`), the script offers:

- use checkout (`git`), or
- use global install (`npm`)

If no TTY is available and no install method is set, it defaults to `npm` and warns.

The script exits with code `2` for invalid method selection or invalid `--install-method` values.

### Examples (install.sh)

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Default">
    ```bash
    curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash
    ```

    curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --no-onboard
    ```

  <Tab title="Git install">
    ```bash
    curl -fsSL --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 https://openclaw.ai/install.sh | bash -s -- --install-method git
    ```

# Inventory: DeadReckon user-interaction surface

## 1. Bare invocation and `print_top_help`

**Bare invocation = `status`, not help.** `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:569-587` — `main_inner()` first checks `wants_top_level_help()` (main.rs:1365-1374: exactly one arg that is `-h`, `--help`, or `help`), and if so prints `print_top_help()` and exits. Otherwise `Cli::parse()` runs and `cli.command.unwrap_or(Commands::Status { run_id: None, all: false, plain: false, json: false })` at main.rs:582-587 makes `deadreckon` with **zero args run the status command**.

**`print_top_help()`** (main.rs:1872-1911) renders, in order:
1. `deadreckon <version>` (heading + muted)
2. Three product lines: `product::PRODUCT_AUDIENCE`, `PRODUCT_HARNESS`, `PRODUCT_NOT_PROVIDER_REPLACEMENT` (src/product.rs:1-6 — "DeadReckon is for people who already use agent CLIs…", "It is the harness around those harnesses…")
3. `Usage:` → `deadreckon [command]`
4. `Production flow:` → `TYPICAL_FLOW_COMMANDS` (main.rs:1422-1428: `PRODUCT_FIRST_COMMAND` ("deadreckon start \"build the app\""), `attach latest`, `status`, `list`, `finish latest`)
5. Four catalog groups via `print_top_help_group` (main.rs:1863-1870) filtering `COMMAND_HELP_CATALOG` (main.rs:1430+) by `TopHelpGroup` (main.rs:1376-1382): **"Start, watch, keep:"**, **"Setup and health:"**, **"Control:"**, **"Find more:"**
6. A `Note:` about id-prefix/`latest` semantics (main.rs:1898-1902)
7. `Options:` listing `-h, --help` / `-V, --version` (main.rs:1904-1910)

Rows render through `print_catalog_rows` (main.rs:1846-1861) using `ui_command`/`ui_heading` with `{:<width$}` char-count padding (note: pads styled text, see ui.rs `pad_visible` doc-comment about that bug class).

`print_help_all()` (main.rs:1913-1961) is the `help-all` subcommand body (dispatched main.rs:611-614): "deadreckon full command map" heading, discovery note, production flow, `HELP_ALL_GROUPS` sections, then three glossaries — `FLAG_POLICY_ROWS` (incl. `--no-hints`, main.rs:~1770-1785), `PROVIDER_ROLE_ROWS` (main.rs:1787-1816), `CAP_POLICY_ROWS` (main.rs:1818-1835).

## 2. Interactive prompt surface

### Primitives — `crates/deadreckon/src/prompt.rs` (724 lines)
- `SelectChoice` (id/label/optional detail; prompt.rs:10-37) and `SelectPrompt` (title/help/choices/default_index; prompt.rs:39-45).
- `open(message, _default)` (prompt.rs:47-54): prints a cyan `?` (Tone::Prompt) + message, reads one stdin line. **The `_default` param is ignored** — defaults are baked into message strings by callers.
- `select_one` (prompt.rs:56-66): dispatches to arrow-key menu when `should_use_selectable_menu()` (prompt.rs:68-72) — stdin AND stdout are TTYs and `DEADRECKON_PROMPT_LINE_MODE` is unset; else numbered line mode `select_one_line` (prompt.rs:74-101).
- Menu mode `select_one_menu` (prompt.rs:103-149): falls back to line mode if `menu_fits(choices, rows)` fails (`count + 4 <= rows`, prompt.rs:420-423); enters raw mode via `RawModeGuard` (prompt.rs:433-446); redraw uses `MoveUp(n)` + `Clear(CurrentLine)` (`render_select_menu`, prompt.rs:151-198) with footer "choose [N]: arrows/Enter, number, Esc to cancel".
- Key dispatch is pure/testable: `menu_step` (prompt.rs:359-408) — Up/`k`, Down/`j`, Home/End, Enter, Ctrl-C → Interrupt, Ctrl-J/M commit, multi-digit accumulation via `resolve_digit_selection` (prompt.rs:331-343). **Esc** (prompt.rs:402-405): commits the choice whose id is literally `"cancel"` (`cancel_choice_index`, prompt.rs:410-415) if present, else returns `MenuStep::Cancel` → `io::ErrorKind::Interrupted` "prompt cancelled".
- `paint_menu_row` (prompt.rs:234-265): pure painter splitting `lead | [n] | body`, coloring marker (Prompt), ordinal (Command), selected label (Heading), detail (Muted); width-invariant (pinned by tests prompt.rs:690-713). `style_menu_row` (prompt.rs:221-228) gates it on `ui::enabled(Stream::Stdout)`.
- `confirm(question, default_yes)` (prompt.rs:448-457): `[Y/n]`/`[y/N]` loop via `parse_confirm_answer` (prompt.rs:475-485).
- `ask_number(label, range, default)` (prompt.rs:491-507): re-prompting numeric input.
- Width/normalize helpers: `selectable_menu_width` (prompt.rs:267-279, char-count based), `truncate_menu_line` / `normalize_menu_line` (prompt.rs:281-313).

### Caller-side TTY gating
- **start**: `StartPromptEligibility` (start.rs:201-224) — `allows_prompts() = stdin_is_tty && !json && !plain && !quiet && !yes`. Off-TTY auto mode falls back to "conservative single supervised run" (start.rs:350-354); off-TTY non-git source produces a recovery error "non-interactive without a source mode" with try-lines (start.rs:1987-2006). Missing goal off-TTY → notice + `start goal required` error (`start_goal_plan`/`resolve_start_goal`, start.rs:2362-2392).
- **completion loop**: `complete_run_actions` gates on `allow_prompt && stdin TTY && stdout TTY` (main.rs:10935).
- **acceptance**: gates on `io::stdin().is_terminal()` (acceptance.rs:558, 829).
- **spend confirm**: off-TTY `--max-spend > $50` is a hard error demanding `--i-know-its-a-lot`/`--no-confirm` (main.rs:3468-3473).

### Every prompt site
| Site | What it asks | How |
|---|---|---|

## 6. First-run detection today

- **There is no automatic first-run interception.** Missing `~/.deadreckon/config.toml` is only surfaced when something needs it: `doctor` checks `paths.config_path().exists()` (doctor.rs:175-198) and emits a **failed** "config … missing" finding with action `deadreckon init`; provider-defaults finding (doctor.rs:204-223) falls back to "CLI subscription provider available → `deadreckon init --no-confirm`" if claude/codex binaries exist, else failed "no provider configured". Other doctor checks (build_doctor_report, doctor.rs:131-263): source/home paths, sandbox backends, providers table + per-provider CLI binary + **CLI auth probe (logged-in vs installed-but-logged-out)** or API credential (+optional `DEADRECKON_DOCTOR_PING=1` live ping, doctor.rs:469-531), seams resolution, runstate-dir writability + disk space (doctor.rs:533-576), OS, sleep prevention, claude/codex subscription binaries. Rendered as a VerdictSurface; `deadreckon init` runs `doctor_setup_summary()` (init.rs:70) and its closing verdict flips to Blocked→"deadreckon doctor" if blocking issues exist (init.rs:97-111).
- **`init` flow** (init.rs:3-88): creates home dir, prompts for provider (`prompt_provider`, main.rs:7766 — plain text-input with detected-subscription-CLI default; `--no-confirm` auto-picks installed subscription CLI else "anthropic"), prompts for API key for non-`cli:` providers, writes config.toml, prints provider rows, attempts shell-completion install, prints verdict surface.
- **`start` prompt-vs-refuse**: `start_command` (start.rs:2401-2444) computes `eligibility.allows_prompts()` (TTY and none of `--json/--plain/--quiet/--yes`); prompting path runs the picker chain, otherwise `resolve_start_setup(..., None, ...)` which off-TTY produces recovery errors with try-lines instead of prompting (e.g. start.rs:1987-2006 non-git, start.rs:350-354 conservative auto mode, start.rs:2366-2369 missing goal notice). Cancelled/incomplete prompts set `set_start_recovery` → exit via Blocked VerdictSurface (start.rs:2538-2541).

## 7. Tests most likely to break

**(a) Bare invocation changes from status to help**
- No test directly pins `deadreckon` (zero args) → status from the outside (no such test found in tests/ or src tests; `Commands::Status` default appears only at main.rs:582). Lowest-risk change of the three, but watch:
  - `crates/deadreckon/tests/coherence.rs:121-131` (`error_lines_use_shared_stderr_helper` reads main.rs source) and any source-grepping coherence tests touching `main.rs` structure.
  - `tests/smoke_invariant.rs` if `make smoke` scripts ever invoke the bare binary (check `Makefile` smoke target before relying on this).
  - `wants_top_level_help` (main.rs:1365) and the `Cli` struct's `Option<Commands>` (cli.rs:544) are the seams to touch.

**(b) Help output gains a banner (ASCII art)**
- `coherence.rs::top_help_names_audience_and_start_path` (433) — wants audience copy near the top.
- `coherence.rs::top_help_uses_canonical_discovery_words` (693) — pins exact strings AND **absence** patterns like `"{advanced}    "` (an ASCII banner containing words like "run" followed by spaces could trip the negative assertions at 716-719).
- `coherence.rs::help_all_keeps_aliases_inline` (750), `start_command_is_visible_in_top_help_and_help_all` (451), `audience_copy_does_not_call_deadreckon_a_provider_replacement` (663).
- `friendliness_contract.rs` row for `help-all` (src/friendliness_contract.rs:69-72) if behavior class changes.
- Help is colored only on TTY (`ui_heading`/`ui_command` gate through `ui::enabled`), and these tests capture piped stdout, so color is safe but literal text/widths are not.

**(c) Prompts re-rendered by a new library**
- Unit tests inside `prompt.rs` itself (prompt.rs:526-724): menu_step keyboard semantics, Esc→cancel-choice behavior, digit accumulation, `menu_fits` fallback, `truncate_menu_line` widths, `\r\n` raw-mode line endings, **`style_menu_row` no-color-off-TTY guarantee**, `paint_menu_row` width invariance.
- `crates/deadreckon/tests/codebase.rs:765-800` (`config_remove_provider_without_arg_prompts_configured_provider_choices`) — drives the real binary with `DEADRECKON_PROMPT_LINE_MODE=1`, pipes `1\n`, asserts literal `"Remove provider"` and `"[1] anthropic"`. Any new library must preserve the env-var line-mode escape hatch and the `[n] label` rendering, or this breaks.
- `src/tui_tests.rs:1977-2018+` — `ScriptedStartPrompter` implements `StartPrompter` against `SelectPrompt`/`SelectChoice` types and pins prompt titles and choice ids (tests at 2439, 2467, 2596, 2618, 2640, 2677, 2723…). Changing the prompt-type signatures breaks these; changing only rendering does not.
- `tests/smoke_invariant.rs` + `tests/.smoke-baseline` if prompt output leaks into smoke narrative (prompts are TTY-gated so likely safe).
- Goldens in `tests/goldens/characterization/` are off-TTY captures; safe so long as the new library stays silent off-TTY (the current `ui::enabled`/`should_use_selectable_menu` discipline is the contract to keep).
- Also note `main.rs:7785` `prompt_non_git_mode` is a stderr-printed hand-rolled menu — divergent from prompt.rs and a prime unification target.

# OpenClaw study — how "everything is SMART" maps to code

OpenClaw (`/Users/gdc/openclaw`) is a TypeScript/Node CLI (`openclaw`, entry `openclaw.mjs` → `dist/entry.js`, built with commander). Below is everything relevant for a Rust CLI emulation, with verbatim copy and file paths.

---

## 1. First run / no config — the onboarding wizard

**Trigger paths:**
- The installer script (`curl … install.sh | bash`) "Attempts onboarding when appropriate (TTY available, onboarding not disabled, and bootstrap/config checks pass)" — `/Users/gdc/openclaw/docs/install/installer.md` (Post-install tasks step). Skippable with `--no-onboard`.
- Manually: `openclaw onboard` (alias-ish: `openclaw setup --wizard`). Docs recommend `openclaw onboard --install-daemon` as step 2 of getting started (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/docs/start/getting-started.md`).
- There is no auto-wizard on bare invocation; instead a **config guard** runs before every command and points broken configs at `doctor` (see §5).

**The wizard flow** — `/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/wizard/onboarding.ts` (`runOnboardingWizard`), dispatched from `/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/commands/onboard.ts`:

1. **ASCII-art header** (`printWizardHeader`, `/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/commands/onboard-helpers.ts:99`) — a block-art "OPENCLAW" banner with `🦞 OPENCLAW 🦞`.
2. **`intro("OpenClaw onboarding")`** then a **mandatory risk acknowledgement** note (verbatim):
   ```
   Security warning — please read.

   OpenClaw is a hobby project and still in beta. Expect sharp edges.
   This bot can read files and run actions if tools are enabled.
   A bad prompt can trick it into doing unsafe things.

   If you're not comfortable with basic security and access control, don't run OpenClaw.
   Ask someone experienced to help before enabling tools or exposing it to the internet.

   Recommended baseline:
   - Pairing/allowlists + mention gating.
   - Sandbox + least-privilege tools.
   ...
   ```
   followed by `confirm: "I understand this is powerful and inherently risky. Continue?"` with `initialValue: false`. Decline = wizard cancelled, exit 1.
3. **Config snapshot check** — `readConfigFileSnapshot()`. If config exists but is invalid, it prints each issue (`- path: message`) and bails: `` Config invalid. Run `openclaw doctor` to repair it, then re-run onboarding. ``
4. **Flow select** (defaults-first):
   ```
   message: "Onboarding mode"
   { value: "quickstart", label: "QuickStart", hint: "Configure details later via `openclaw configure`." }
   { value: "advanced",   label: "Manual",     hint: "Configure port, network, Tailscale, and auth options." }
   initialValue: "quickstart"
   ```
5. **Existing config detected** → note titled `"Existing config detected"` with `summarizeExistingConfig()` (key/value rows like `workspace: …`, `model: …`, `gateway.port: …`; else `"No key settings detected."`), then:
   ```
   message: "Config handling"
   keep   → "Use existing values"
   modify → "Update values"
   reset  → "Reset"          → reset scope: "Config only" | "Config + creds + sessions" | "Full reset (config + creds + sessions + workspace)"
   ```
6. **QuickStart summary note** — prints the exact defaults it's about to apply (`Gateway port: 18789`, `Gateway bind: Loopback (127.0.0.1)`, `Gateway auth: Token (default)`, `Tailscale exposure: Off`, `Direct to chat channels.`) — or, if config exists, "Keeping your current gateway settings:" with current values.
7. **Live gateway probing** — it probes `ws://127.0.0.1:<port>` and any configured remote URL *before* asking local/remote, and bakes results into menu hints:
   ```
   message: "What do you want to set up?"
   { value: "local",  label: "Local gateway (this machine)",  hint: localProbe.ok ? `Gateway reachable (${localUrl})` : `No gateway detected (${localUrl})` }
   { value: "remote", label: "Remote gateway (info-only)",    hint: !remoteUrl ? "No remote URL configured yet" : remoteProbe?.ok ? `Gateway reachable (${remoteUrl})` : `Configured but unreachable (${remoteUrl})` }
   ```
   QuickStart skips this question entirely (assumes local).
8. **Workspace** — text prompt `"Workspace directory"` with `initialValue` from existing config or `~/.openclaw/workspace` (QuickStart never asks).
9. **Model/auth** — grouped two-level menu (see §3), then default-model picker, then `warnIfModelConfigLooksOff`.
10. **Gateway config** (`onboarding.gateway-config.ts`), **channels**, **skills**, **hooks** — each step a confirm-gated section. Writes config, stamps `wizard.lastRunAt/lastRunVersion/lastRunCommand/lastRunMode` metadata (`applyWizardMetadata`).
11. **Finalize** (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/wizard/onboarding.finalize.ts`): daemon install (`confirm: "Install Gateway service (recommended)", initialValue: true`; auto-yes on QuickStart), waits for gateway with `waitForGatewayReachable` (15s poll loop) so the health check doesn't false-fail, runs `health`, prints Control UI links + token explainer, then the signature prompt:
    ```
    message: "How do you want to hatch your bot?"
    { value: "tui",   label: "Hatch in TUI (recommended)" }
    { value: "web",   label: "Open the Web UI" }
    { value: "later", label: "Do this later" }
    initialValue: "tui"
    ```
    If a bootstrap file exists in the workspace it first shows (verbatim, title `"Start TUI (best option!)"`):
    ```
    This is the defining action that makes your agent you.
    Please take your time.
    The more you tell it, the better the experience will be.
    We will send: "Wake up, my friend!"
    ```
    TUI choice launches the chat TUI directly with the message `"Wake up, my friend!"`. Web choice opens the tokenized dashboard URL via OS-detected opener and prints `"Opened in your browser. Keep that tab to control OpenClaw."` (or a precomputed SSH tunnel hint if headless).

**Platform smarts in the entry command** (`onboard.ts`): on Windows it prints
```
Windows detected — OpenClaw runs great on WSL2!
Native Windows might be trickier.
Quick setup: wsl --install (one command, one reboot)
Guide: https://docs.openclaw.ai/windows
```
Non-interactive mode requires `--accept-risk` explicitly: `"Non-interactive onboarding requires explicit risk acknowledgement."` Deprecated auth choices are normalized with a notice instead of erroring (`'Auth choice "claude-cli" is deprecated; using setup-token flow instead.'`).

---

## 2. Context detection & adaptive behavior

This is the densest "smart" layer:

- **Config snapshot everywhere** — `readConfigFileSnapshot()` returns `{exists, valid, issues, legacyIssues, config}`; every flow branches on it (wizard offers keep/modify/reset; guard blocks commands; doctor migrates).
- **Gateway probing before asking** — `probeGatewayReachable` / `waitForGatewayReachable` (`onboard-helpers.ts:380-436`) do a real WS health call with 1.5s timeout and feed *menu hints* and post-install verification. Errors are summarized to one trimmed 120-char line (`summarizeError`).
- **Binary detection** — `detectBinary(name)` (`onboard-helpers.ts:342`) — `which`/`where` with 2s timeout, used for: `signal-cli`, `brew`, `open`/`xdg-open`/`wslview`, imessage CLI.
- **Channel quickstart scoring** — each channel onboarding adapter returns `{configured, statusLines, selectionHint, quickstartScore}`; the wizard preselects the highest score (`resolveQuickstartDefault`, `onboard-channels.ts:208`). Scores encode opinion + detection: WhatsApp `linked ? 5 : 4`, Telegram `configured ? 1 : 10` (i.e. *push Telegram for new users*), Signal `signalCliDetected ? 1 : 0`, iMessage `imessageCliDetected ? 1 : 0`, Slack/Discord `configured ? 2 : 1`. Files: `/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/channels/plugins/onboarding/{whatsapp,telegram,signal,discord,slack,imessage}.ts`.
- **Per-channel live status lines** baked into hints, e.g. Signal: `` `Signal: ${configured ? "configured" : "needs setup"}` `` + `` `signal-cli: ${found ? "found" : "missing"} (${path})` ``, selection hint `"signal-cli found"`/`"signal-cli missing"`. Already-configured channels get an adaptive menu: `"${label} already configured. What do you want to do?"` → Modify settings / Disable (keeps config) / Delete config / Skip (leave as-is).
- **Environment-aware browser opening** — `resolveBrowserOpenCommand` detects SSH-without-DISPLAY, WSL (`wslview`), macOS `open`, Linux `xdg-open`; on failure prints a *fully formed* SSH port-forward recipe with the user/host pulled from `$SSH_CONNECTION`:
  ```
  No GUI detected. Open from your computer:
  ssh -N -L 18789:127.0.0.1:18789 user@host
  Then open:
  http://localhost:18789/  (+ #token=… variant)
  ```
- **Platform branches** — Linux: checks `isSystemdUserServiceAvailable()`; if absent, skips daemon install with `"Systemd user services are unavailable; skipping service install. Use your container supervisor or \`docker compose up -d\`."`; if present, walks through systemd *lingering* with an explanation of why. macOS doctor checks `launchctl getenv` overrides that shadow config tokens (`doctor-platform-notes.ts`).
- **Skills eligibility scan** — `buildWorkspaceSkillStatus` classifies skills into eligible / missing requirements / unsupported-on-OS / blocked-by-allowlist and shows counts before offering installs; detects missing Homebrew and offers the install one-liner (`onboard-skills.ts`).
- **Web-search key detection** — finalize checks both config and `BRAVE_API_KEY` env and prints a different note for each state.
- **State migrations** — doctor detects legacy config keys/state layouts and offers migrations (`doctor-state-migrations.ts`, `doctor-legacy-config.ts`).

---

## 3. Interactive UX building blocks

- **Language/stack:** TypeScript on Node, **commander** for the CLI, **`@clack/prompts` ^1.0.1** for all interactive prompts/spinners, **chalk ^5.6.2** behind a custom theme (`src/terminal/theme.ts`), plus a custom TUI (`src/tui/`) for chat.
- **Abstraction layer:** `WizardPrompter` interface (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/wizard/prompts.ts`) — `intro/outro/note/select/multiselect/text/confirm/progress` — with two implementations: `createClackPrompter()` (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/wizard/clack-prompter.ts`) for humans, and non-interactive/RPC prompters for scripts (`onboard-non-interactive.ts`, `doctor-prompter.ts`). Every menu item is `{value, label, hint?}`; cancellation is uniform (`isCancel` → `cancel("Setup cancelled.")` → `WizardCancelledError` → exit 1).
- **Menu mechanics:** clack-style **arrow-key navigation with an `initialValue` default** (defaults-first everywhere — quickstart preselected, recommended option preselected, detected channel preselected). Hints render dim after the label. Multiselect used for skill deps with a literal `"Skip for now"` first option. No single-key selection. Two-level select with a `"Back"` sentinel for grouped menus (`auth-choice-prompt.ts`, `BACK_VALUE = "__back"`).
- **Spinners:** clack `spinner()` wrapped in `progress(label)` with `update()`/`stop(message)`, plus OSC 9;4 terminal progress (`createCliProgress` in `src/cli/progress.ts`). Usage pattern: `Installing X…` → `Installed X` / `Install failed: X (exit N) — detail`.
- **Notes as primary teaching tool:** titled boxes (`src/terminal/note.ts`) used constantly — `"Channel status"`, `"How channels work"`, `"Token"`, `"Security"`, `"What now"`.
- **Auth menu structure** (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/commands/auth-choice-options.ts`): first a provider group select (`message: "Model/auth provider"`) — `OpenAI (hint: "Codex OAuth + API key")`, `Anthropic (hint: "setup-token + API key")`, `MiniMax (hint: "M2.5 (recommended)")`, … `Custom Provider (hint: "Any OpenAI or Anthropic compatible endpoint")`, plus `Skip for now` — then a per-group method select if >1 option (auto-selects when 1). Option labels carry actionable hints, e.g. `"Anthropic token (paste setup-token)"` / hint `` "run `claude setup-token` elsewhere, then paste the token here" ``.

---

## 4. Bare invocation (`openclaw` with no args)

There is **no default action**: commander prints the styled help. But the help itself is curated (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/cli/program/help.ts`):
- A **banner** prepended via `addHelpText("beforeAll")` — `🦞 OpenClaw <version> (<commit>) — <tagline>` where the tagline is randomly picked from ~60 jokes plus date-aware holiday lines (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/cli/tagline.ts`), e.g. `"If you're lost, run doctor; if you're brave, run prod; if you're wise, run tests."` and `"curl for conversations."` Banner suppressed for `--json`, `--version`, non-TTY, `OPENCLAW_HIDE_BANNER`, and `update`/`completion` commands (`src/cli/banner.ts`, `program/preaction.ts`).
- Headings (`Usage:`/`Options:`/`Commands:`) recolored, subcommands/options sorted alphabetically and themed.
- An `Examples:` section appended `afterAll` (8 real command+description pairs) ending with `Docs: docs.openclaw.ai/cli`.
- Subcommands are *lazily registered* (`command-registry.ts`) — placeholders carry descriptions for help, real modules load only when invoked. Hot read-only paths (`status`, `health`, `sessions`, `config get`…) bypass commander entirely via a fast router (`src/cli/program/routes.ts`).
- Several subcommands have smart no-arg defaults: `openclaw config` (no subcommand) opens the configure wizard; `openclaw models` → `models status`; `openclaw skills` → `skills list` (docs/cli/*.md).

---

## 5. Doctor / status / dashboard patterns

- **Config guard before every command** (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/cli/program/config-guard.ts`): if config exists but is invalid, prints
  ```
  Config invalid
  File: ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json
  Problem:
    - <path>: <message>
  Run: openclaw doctor --fix
  ```
  and exits 1 — *except* for an allowlist of diagnostic commands (`doctor`, `logs`, `health`, `help`, `status`, and gateway status/probe/start/stop/…) which may proceed on a broken config. This is a great pattern: never lock the user out of the tools that fix the problem.
- **`openclaw doctor`** (`/Users/gdc/openclaw/src/commands/doctor.ts` + ~20 `doctor-*.ts` modules): banner + `intro("OpenClaw doctor")`, then sequential check/repair phases, each a `note(...)` plus an optional `confirmRepair` prompt: update offer, UI protocol freshness, source-install issues, deprecated env vars, config migration, auth profile health (incl. keychain prompts only when TTY), gateway mode/auth (`"Gateway auth is off or missing a token. Token auth is now the recommended default (including loopback)."` → `confirm: "Generate and configure a gateway token now?"` default true), gateway daemon repair, extra-service scan, sandbox images, state integrity, security warnings, memory search health, workspace status + backup tip, shell completion. Flags: `--repair`/`--fix` (writes `.bak`, drops unknown keys listing each removal), `--deep`, `--non-interactive`, `--generate-gateway-token`. Missing-config case: `` Missing config: run `openclaw setup` first. ``
- **`openclaw status`** (`status.command.ts`): renders a real table (`renderTable`) of Item/Status/Detail rows where free-text channel health is classified into colored badges (`OK`/`WARN`/`OFF`/`LINKED`/`UNLINKED`), then FAQ/troubleshooting links, update-available hint, and **adaptive next steps**:
  ```
  Next steps:
    Need to share?      openclaw status --all
    Need to debug live? openclaw logs --follow
    Need to test channels? openclaw status --deep     (only if gateway reachable)
    Fix reachability first: openclaw gateway probe    (only if not)
  ```
  `status --all` produces a shareable full report; `getStatusSummary` (`status.summary.ts`) aggregates per-agent sessions with token usage %, model, heartbeats, queued events, and has a `redactSensitiveStatusSummary` variant.
- **`openclaw dashboard`** (`dashboard.ts`): resolves the Control UI URL from config (coercing `lan`→`loopback` because "LAN URLs fail secure-context checks"), puts the token in the **URL fragment** (not query) to avoid leaks, prints it, **copies to clipboard**, auto-opens the browser if the environment supports it, else prints the SSH tunnel recipe.

---

## 6. Best copy to steal (voice & structure)

The voice: short declarative lines, honest about risk, always pairs a statement with the exact command to run next, playful only at the edges (banner/taglines), never in safety or error text.

- Risk gate: `"OpenClaw is a hobby project and still in beta. Expect sharp edges."` / `"I understand this is powerful and inherently risky. Continue?"` (default **No**).
- Windows: `"Windows detected — OpenClaw runs great on WSL2! … Quick setup: wsl --install (one command, one reboot)"`.
- QuickStart hint pattern: option label is the *choice*, hint is the *consequence*: `QuickStart — "Configure details later via \`openclaw configure\`."` vs `Manual — "Configure port, network, Tailscale, and auth options."`
- Detection-in-hint: `"Gateway reachable (ws://127.0.0.1:18789)"` / `"No gateway detected (…)"` / `"Configured but unreachable (…)"`.
- Hatching ceremony: `"How do you want to hatch your bot?"`, `"Hatch in TUI (recommended)"`, and the bootstrap note `"This is the defining action that makes your agent you. Please take your time."` … `'We will send: "Wake up, my friend!"'`
- Token explainer note (title `Token`): states what it is, where it's stored, how to view it, how to regenerate it, where the browser caches it — five facts, five lines, each with a command.
- Channel security primer: `"DM security: default is pairing; unknown DMs get a pairing code."` + `"Approve with: openclaw pairing approve <channel> <code>"`; DM policy menu: `Pairing (recommended) / Allowlist (specific users only) / Open (public inbound DMs) / Disabled (ignore DMs)`.
- Skills status note: four counters (`Eligible / Missing requirements / Unsupported on this OS / Blocked by allowlist`), then `confirm: "Configure skills now? (recommended)"`.
- Skip affordances everywhere: `"Skip for now"` with hint `` "You can add channels later via `openclaw channels add`" ``; `"Do this later"` → `"When you're ready: openclaw dashboard --no-open"`.
- Outro: `"Onboarding complete. Dashboard opened; keep that tab to control OpenClaw."`; closing notes `"Back up your agent workspace."`, `"Running agents on your computer is risky — harden your setup: https://docs.openclaw.ai/security"`, and `'What now: https://openclaw.ai/showcase ("What People Are Building").'`

**Rust equivalents** for deadreckon: `cliclack` or `inquire`/`dialoguer` (for clack-style intro/note/select-with-hints/spinner), `indicatif` for progress, `owo-colors`/`anstyle` theming, `clap` with lazy/sorted help + after-help examples. The load-bearing architecture to copy: (a) a `Prompter` trait with interactive + non-interactive implementations, (b) snapshot-validate config with an allowlist of commands that run on broken config, (c) probe/detect *before* asking and surface findings as menu hints + preselected defaults, (d) every terminal message ends in the next command to run.

pub(crate) fn set_plain_output(plain: bool) {
    PLAIN_OUTPUT.store(plain, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

pub(crate) fn enabled(stream: Stream) -> bool {
    if PLAIN_OUTPUT.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
        return false;
    }
    if std::env::var_os("NO_COLOR").is_some() {
        return false;
    }
    if std::env::var("TERM").is_ok_and(|term| term == "dumb") {
        return false;
    }
    stream_is_terminal(stream)
}

pub(crate) fn render(stream: Stream, tone: Tone, text: impl AsRef<str>) -> String {
    let text = text.as_ref();
    let Some(code) = tone.to_ansi() else {
        return text.to_string();
    };
    if enabled(stream) {
        ansi_wrap(code, text)
    } else {
        text.to_string()
    }
}

pub(crate) fn ansi_wrap(code: &str, text: &str) -> String {
    format!("\x1b[{code}m{text}{ANSI_RESET}")
}

#[allow(dead_code)]
pub(crate) fn ansi_reset() -> &'static str {
    ANSI_RESET
}

banner = r'''/// The figlet "standard" wordmark, rendered with a per-character 256-color
/// horizontal gradient at print time. Palettes are 256-color (not 24-bit) for
/// Terminal.app compatibility; one is picked pseudo-randomly per invocation
/// so the banner feels alive without any new dependency.
const BANNER_ART: [&str; 5] = [
    r"  ____                 _ ____           _               ",
    r" |  _ \  ___  __ _  __| |  _ \ ___  ___| | _____  _ __  ",
    r" | | | |/ _ \/ _` |/ _` | |_) / _ \/ __| |/ / _ \| '_ \ ",
    r" | |_| |  __/ (_| | (_| |  _ <  __/ (__|   < (_) | | | |",
    r" |____/ \___|\__,_|\__,_|_| \_\___|\___|_|\_\___/|_| |_|",
];

const BANNER_PALETTES: [&[u8]; 12] = [
    &[75, 81, 87, 93, 99, 105],        // grad blue -> purple
    &[203, 209, 210, 215, 216],        // sunset
    &[33, 34, 35, 37, 38, 39],         // dawn blues
    &[61, 97, 103, 139, 181],          // nebula violet
    &[24, 30, 37, 44, 51],             // ocean
    &[197, 203, 204, 210, 216, 217],   // fire
    &[23, 24, 30, 66, 72, 108],        // forest
    &[172, 178, 184, 220, 226],        // gold
    &[31, 32, 33, 67, 103],            // purple-steel
    &[32, 38, 44, 45, 68],             // mint
    &[181, 182, 188, 217, 224],        // coral
    &[28, 34, 40, 41, 47],             // matrix
];

/// Render the wordmark with a horizontal gradient from one palette.
/// Plain (no color) when the stream's color gate is off.
pub(crate) fn banner_text(stream: Stream, palette_index: usize) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    if !enabled(stream) {
        for line in BANNER_ART {
            out.push_str(line.trim_end());
            out.push('\n');
        }
        return out;
    }
    let palette = BANNER_PALETTES[palette_index % BANNER_PALETTES.len()];
    let width = BANNER_ART
        .iter()
        .map(|line| line.chars().count())
        .max()
        .unwrap_or(1)
        .max(1);
    for line in BANNER_ART {
        let trimmed = line.trim_end();
        for (column, ch) in trimmed.chars().enumerate() {
            if ch == ' ' {
                out.push(ch);
                continue;
            }
            let slot = column * palette.len() / width;
            let color = palette[slot.min(palette.len() - 1)];
            out.push_str(&format!("\x1b[38;5;{color}m{ch}\x1b[39m"));
        }
        out.push('\n');
    }
    out
}

/// Print the banner block (wordmark + tagline + version) on interactive
/// stdout. Pipes, --plain, NO_COLOR-with-no-TTY, and dumb terminals stay
/// byte-clean: nothing prints unless stdout is a terminal.
pub(crate) fn print_banner(version: &str) {
    if !stream_is_terminal(Stream::Stdout) {
        return;
    }
    let palette_index = std::time::SystemTime::now()
        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
        .map(|elapsed| elapsed.subsec_nanos() as usize)
        .unwrap_or(0);
    println!();
    print!("{}", banner_text(Stream::Stdout, palette_index));
    println!(
        "{}",
        render(
            Stream::Stdout,
            Tone::Muted,
            format!(" v{version} · run your coding agent unattended, and trust the result"),
        )
    );
    println!();
}

pub(crate) fn set_plain_output(plain: bool) {'''

code='''/// Bare `deadreckon` reads the room instead of assuming: a machine with no
/// setup gets a welcome and the guided path, a configured machine in a
/// directory with no runs gets oriented help, and a directory with runs gets
/// its status — the command a returning operator actually wants.
async fn smart_bare_invocation() -> Result<()> {
    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
    if !paths.config_path().exists() {
        return first_run_welcome().await;
    }
    let scope_has_runs = current_scope()
        .ok()
        .and_then(|scope| deadreckon_core::state::list_runs(&paths, Some(&scope)).ok())
        .is_some_and(|runs| !runs.is_empty());
    if scope_has_runs {
        return status_command(None, false, false, false);
    }
    directory_orientation();
    Ok(())
}

const KNOWN_AGENT_CLIS: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("claude", "Claude Code"),
    ("codex", "Codex"),
    ("gemini", "Gemini CLI"),
    ("copilot", "GitHub Copilot CLI"),
    ("opencode", "OpenCode"),
    ("pi", "Pi"),
];

/// First contact on this machine: greet, show what was detected, and point at
/// (or directly offer) the guided setup. Never errors — a welcome that fails
/// is worse than no welcome.
async fn first_run_welcome() -> Result<()> {
    ui::print_banner(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
    println!(
        "{}",
        ui_heading("Welcome — this machine has no deadreckon setup yet.")
    );
    println!("{}", product::PRODUCT_AUDIENCE);
    println!("{}", product::PRODUCT_HARNESS);
    println!();
    println!("{}", ui_heading("Detected agent CLIs:"));
    let mut found_any = false;
    for (binary, label) in KNOWN_AGENT_CLIS {
        if command_exists(binary) {
            found_any = true;
            println!("  {} {label} ({binary})", ui_ok("✓"));
        }
    }
    if !found_any {
        println!(
            "  {}",
            ui_muted("none found — BYO API key works too (anthropic / openai routes)")
        );
    }
    println!();
    println!("{}", ui_heading("Get going:"));
    println!(
        "  {}   {}",
        ui_command("deadreckon init"),
        ui_muted("guided setup (about a minute)")
    );
    println!(
        "  {}    {}",
        ui_command("deadreckon try"),
        ui_muted("keyless proof run of the whole harness")
    );
    println!(
        "  {}   {}",
        ui_command("deadreckon help"),
        ui_muted("the command map")
    );
    if std::io::stdin().is_terminal() && std::io::stdout().is_terminal() {
        println!();
        if prompt::confirm("run guided setup now?", true)? {
            return commands::init::init_command(
                None,
                None,
                None,
                10.0,
                "auto".to_string(),
                false,
                false,
            )
            .await;
        }
        println!(
            "{}",
            ui_muted("whenever you're ready: deadreckon init")
        );
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Configured machine, but this directory has no runs: orient instead of
/// erroring. Explains what start would do *here* and how to find runs made
/// elsewhere.
fn directory_orientation() {
    ui::print_banner(env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION"));
    println!("{}", ui_heading("No deadreckon runs in this directory yet."));
    let in_git = std::env::current_dir()
        .map(|cwd| cwd.join(".git").exists())
        .unwrap_or(false);
    if in_git {
        println!(
            "{}",
            ui_muted("source: git repo — start works in an isolated worktree; your checkout only changes on apply")
        );
    } else {
        println!(
            "{}",
            ui_muted("source: plain directory — start will offer git init, copy, or fresh")
        );
    }
    println!();
    println!("{}", ui_heading("The flow:"));
    for command in TYPICAL_FLOW_COMMANDS {
        println!("  {}", ui_command(command));
    }
    println!();
    println!(
        "  {} {}",
        ui_muted("runs from other directories:"),
        ui_command("deadreckon list --all")
    );
    println!(
        "  {} {}",
        ui_muted("setup and health:        "),
        ui_command("deadreckon doctor")
    );
}

    let metadata = SleepMetadata {

}

#![allow(clippy::expect_used)]

//! Bare `deadreckon` reads the room: first run on a machine welcomes and
//! points at guided setup, a configured machine in a runless directory gets
//! oriented, and a directory with runs gets its status. All three routes are
//! pipe-clean (no banner art off-TTY) and exit 0.

use std::fs;

use deadreckon_core::{DeadreckonPaths, RunOptions, create_run};
use tempfile::TempDir;

mod common;

use common::{assert_success, deadreckon, repo_tempdir, stdout};

#[test]
fn bare_invocation_without_config_prints_first_run_welcome() {
    let temp = repo_tempdir();
    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::from_home(temp.path().join("home"));

    let output = deadreckon(&paths)
        .current_dir(temp.path())
        .output()
        .expect("bare deadreckon");

    assert_success(&output);
    let out = stdout(&output);
    assert!(out.contains("Welcome"), "{out}");
    assert!(out.contains("deadreckon init"), "{out}");
    assert!(out.contains("deadreckon try"), "{out}");
    assert!(out.contains("deadreckon help"), "{out}");
    // Piped output stays byte-clean: no banner art, no ANSI.
    assert!(!out.contains("____"), "banner art leaked into a pipe: {out}");
    assert!(!out.contains('\u{1b}'), "ANSI leaked into a pipe: {out}");
}

#[test]
fn bare_invocation_with_config_but_no_runs_orients_the_directory() {
    let temp = repo_tempdir();
    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::from_home(temp.path().join("home"));
    fs::create_dir_all(paths.home()).expect("home");
    fs::write(
        paths.config_path(),
        "[providers.smoke]\nkind = \"scripted-smoke\"\n",
    )
    .expect("config");
    let workdir = temp.path().join("fresh-project");
    fs::create_dir_all(&workdir).expect("workdir");

    let output = deadreckon(&paths)
        .current_dir(&workdir)
        .output()
        .expect("bare deadreckon");

    assert_success(&output);
    let out = stdout(&output);
    assert!(
        out.contains("No deadreckon runs in this directory yet."),
        "{out}"
    );
    assert!(out.contains("deadreckon start"), "{out}");
    assert!(out.contains("deadreckon list --all"), "{out}");
    assert!(out.contains("deadreckon doctor"), "{out}");
    assert!(!out.contains('\u{1b}'), "ANSI leaked into a pipe: {out}");
}

#[test]
fn bare_invocation_with_runs_in_scope_shows_status() {
    let temp = repo_tempdir();
    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::from_home(temp.path().join("home"));
    fs::create_dir_all(paths.home()).expect("home");
    fs::write(
        paths.config_path(),
        "[providers.smoke]\nkind = \"scripted-smoke\"\n",
    )
    .expect("config");
    let cwd = temp.path().join("repo");
    fs::create_dir_all(&cwd).expect("repo");
    let state = create_run(
        &paths,
        RunOptions {
            goal: "smart default status".to_string(),
            cwd: cwd.clone(),
            sandbox: "none".to_string(),
            provider: Some("smoke".to_string()),
            skill_name: "default-coding".to_string(),
            max_spend_usd: Some(10.0),
            max_wall_seconds: None,
            run_id: None,
            codebase: None,
        },
    )
    .expect("run");

    let output = deadreckon(&paths)
        .current_dir(&cwd)
        .output()
        .expect("bare deadreckon");

    assert_success(&output);
    let out = stdout(&output);
    assert!(out.contains("deadreckon status"), "{out}");
    assert!(out.contains(&state.run_id[..8]), "{out}");
}

#[test]
fn bare_invocation_first_run_welcome_lists_detected_agent_clis() {
    let temp = repo_tempdir();
    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::from_home(temp.path().join("home"));
    // A stub agent CLI on PATH must show up in the welcome's detection list.
    let bin = temp.path().join("fake-bin");
    fs::create_dir_all(&bin).expect("bin");
    let stub = bin.join("opencode");
    fs::write(&stub, "#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n").expect("stub");
    #[cfg(unix)]
    {
        use std::os::unix::fs::PermissionsExt;
        fs::set_permissions(&stub, fs::Permissions::from_mode(0o755)).expect("chmod");
    }

    let output = deadreckon(&paths)
        .current_dir(temp.path())
        .env(
            "PATH",
            format!(
                "{}:{}",
                bin.display(),
                std::env::var("PATH").unwrap_or_default()
            ),
        )
        .output()
        .expect("bare deadreckon");

    assert_success(&output);
    let out = stdout(&output);
    assert!(out.contains("OpenCode (opencode)"), "{out}");
}

218	/// Colorize a normalized, already-truncated select-menu row. Color is applied

221	fn style_menu_row(line: &str, ordinal: usize, selected: bool) -> String {
222	    if !ui::enabled(Stream::Stdout) {
223	        return line.to_string();

230	/// Pure painter for a select-menu row: splits the line into `lead | [n] | body`
231	/// and applies `paint` to the marker, ordinal, and (for the selected row) the
232	/// label, dimming the trailing detail. `paint` only ever wraps tokens, so the
233	/// visible width equals the input — stripping the result yields `line` again.
234	fn paint_menu_row(
235	    line: &str,
236	    ordinal: usize,
237	    selected: bool,
238	    paint: impl Fn(Tone, &str) -> String,
239	) -> String {
240	    let token = format!("[{ordinal}]");
241	    let Some(at) = line.find(&token) else {
242	        return line.to_string();
243	    };
244	    let lead = &line[..at];
245	    let rest = &line[at + token.len()..];
246	    let lead = if selected {
247	        lead.replacen('>', &paint(Tone::Prompt, ">"), 1)
248	    } else {
249	        lead.to_string()
250	    };
251	    let number = paint(Tone::Command, &token);
252	    let body = match rest.split_once(" - ") {
253	        Some((label, detail)) => {
254	            let label = if selected {
255	                paint(Tone::Heading, label)
256	            } else {
257	                label.to_string()
258	            };
259	            format!("{label} - {}", paint(Tone::Muted, detail))
260	        }
261	        None if selected => paint(Tone::Heading, rest),
262	        None => rest.to_string(),
263	    };
264	    format!("{lead}{number}{body}")
265	}

321	#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
322	enum DigitResolution {
323	    Commit(usize),
324	    Accumulate,
325	    OutOfRange,
326	}
327	
328	/// Resolve an accumulated digit `buffer` against a menu of `len` choices. Commits
329	/// as soon as no longer prefix could be valid, so single-digit menus feel instant
330	/// while menus with 10+ choices accept multi-digit entry.
331	fn resolve_digit_selection(buffer: &str, len: usize) -> DigitResolution {
332	    let Ok(value) = buffer.parse::<usize>() else {
333	        return DigitResolution::OutOfRange;
334	    };
335	    if value == 0 || value > len {
336	        return DigitResolution::OutOfRange;
337	    }
338	    if value.saturating_mul(10) > len {
339	        DigitResolution::Commit(value - 1)
340	    } else {
341	        DigitResolution::Accumulate
342	    }
343	}
344	
345	#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
346	enum MenuStep {
347	    Move(usize),
348	    Commit(usize),
349	    Accumulate,
350	    Reject,
351	    Cancel,
352	    Interrupt,
353	    Ignore,
354	}
355	
356	/// Pure key-dispatch for the selectable menu, factored out so the keyboard and
357	/// number-input behavior is unit-testable without a real TTY. `buffer` holds the
358	/// in-progress multi-digit selection and is mutated as digits arrive.
359	fn menu_step(
360	    choice_count: usize,
361	    selected: usize,
362	    cancel_index: Option<usize>,
363	    buffer: &mut String,
364	    key: KeyEvent,
365	) -> MenuStep {
366	    if matches!(key.kind, KeyEventKind::Release) {
367	        return MenuStep::Ignore;
368	    }
369	    match key.code {
370	        KeyCode::Char('c') if key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL) => MenuStep::Interrupt,
371	        KeyCode::Char('j' | 'm') if key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL) => {
372	            MenuStep::Commit(selected)
373	        }
374	        KeyCode::Enter => {
375	            if !buffer.is_empty()
376	                && let Ok(value) = buffer.parse::<usize>()
377	                && (1..=choice_count).contains(&value)
378	            {
379	                return MenuStep::Commit(value - 1);
380	            }
381	            MenuStep::Commit(selected)
382	        }
383	        KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Char('k') if key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
384	            MenuStep::Move(selected.saturating_sub(1))
385	        }
386	        KeyCode::Down | KeyCode::Char('j') if key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
387	            MenuStep::Move((selected + 1).min(choice_count.saturating_sub(1)))
388	        }
389	        KeyCode::Home => MenuStep::Move(0),
390	        KeyCode::End => MenuStep::Move(choice_count.saturating_sub(1)),
391	        KeyCode::Char(value) if key.modifiers.is_empty() && value.is_ascii_digit() => {
392	            buffer.push(value);
393	            match resolve_digit_selection(buffer, choice_count) {
394	                DigitResolution::Commit(index) => MenuStep::Commit(index),
395	                DigitResolution::Accumulate => MenuStep::Accumulate,
396	                DigitResolution::OutOfRange => {
397	                    buffer.clear();
398	                    MenuStep::Reject
399	                }
400	            }

//! One prompt engine for every interactive surface.
//!
//! On a TTY (and unless `DEADRECKON_PROMPT_LINE_MODE` is set) prompts render
//! through `inquire` — arrow-key selects with hints, styled confirms, and
//! text inputs themed to the shared [`Tone`] palette. Off-TTY, in line mode,
//! and under `--plain`-style gating, everything falls back to the original
//! numbered line prompts so scripts and tests keep byte-stable behavior.
//! Esc cancels: a menu with a choice whose id is `"cancel"` resolves to that
//! choice; otherwise the prompt errors with `Interrupted`, which callers
//! surface as a blocked verdict.

use std::fmt;
use std::io::{self, IsTerminal as _, Write as _};

use crate::Result;
use crate::ui::{self, Stream, Tone};
use inquire::InquireError;
use inquire::ui::{Attributes, Color, RenderConfig, StyleSheet, Styled};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct SelectChoice {
    pub(crate) id: String,
    pub(crate) label: String,
    pub(crate) detail: Option<String>,
}

impl SelectChoice {
    pub(crate) fn new(id: impl Into<String>, label: impl Into<String>) -> Self {
        Self {
            id: id.into(),
            label: label.into(),
            detail: None,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) fn with_detail(
        id: impl Into<String>,
        label: impl Into<String>,
        detail: impl Into<String>,
    ) -> Self {
        Self {
            id: id.into(),
            label: label.into(),
            detail: Some(detail.into()),
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub(crate) struct SelectPrompt {
    pub(crate) title: String,
    pub(crate) help: Option<String>,
    pub(crate) choices: Vec<SelectChoice>,
    pub(crate) default_index: usize,
}

/// How a [`SelectChoice`] renders inside an inquire menu: `label — detail`.
#[derive(Clone)]
struct ChoiceItem {
    index: usize,
    text: String,
}

impl fmt::Display for ChoiceItem {
    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        f.write_str(&self.text)
    }
}

fn choice_item(index: usize, choice: &SelectChoice) -> ChoiceItem {
    let text = match choice.detail.as_deref().filter(|d| !d.trim().is_empty()) {
        Some(detail) => format!("{} — {detail}", choice.label),
        None => choice.label.clone(),
    };
    ChoiceItem { index, text }
}

/// The shared inquire theme, derived from the [`Tone`] palette: cyan prompt
/// marker and selection, dim help text. Colorless when the stdout color gate
/// (`--plain`, `NO_COLOR`, dumb terminal) is off.
fn render_config() -> RenderConfig<'static> {
    if !ui::enabled(Stream::Stdout) {
        return RenderConfig::empty();
    }
    RenderConfig::default_colored()
        .with_prompt_prefix(Styled::new("?").with_fg(Color::LightCyan))
        .with_answered_prompt_prefix(Styled::new("✓").with_fg(Color::LightGreen))
        .with_highlighted_option_prefix(Styled::new("›").with_fg(Color::LightCyan))
        .with_selected_option(Some(
            StyleSheet::new()
                .with_fg(Color::LightCyan)
                .with_attr(Attributes::BOLD),
        ))
        .with_help_message(StyleSheet::new().with_fg(Color::DarkGrey))
        .with_answer(StyleSheet::new().with_fg(Color::LightCyan))
}

fn interactive() -> bool {
    io::stdin().is_terminal()
        && io::stdout().is_terminal()
        && std::env::var_os("DEADRECKON_PROMPT_LINE_MODE").is_none()
}

fn cancelled() -> crate::CliError {
    io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted, "prompt cancelled").into()
}

pub(crate) fn open(message: &str, _default: Option<&str>) -> Result<String> {
    if interactive() {
        let trimmed = message.trim_end().trim_end_matches(':').trim_end();
        return match inquire::Text::new(trimmed)
            .with_render_config(render_config())
            .prompt()
        {
            Ok(value) => Ok(value.trim().to_string()),
            Err(InquireError::OperationCanceled | InquireError::OperationInterrupted) => {
                Err(cancelled())
            }
            Err(err) => Err(io::Error::other(err.to_string()).into()),
        };
    }
    print!("{}", ui::render(Stream::Stdout, Tone::Prompt, "?"));
    print!(" {message}");
    io::stdout().flush()?;
    let mut input = String::new();
    io::stdin().read_line(&mut input)?;
    Ok(input.trim_end_matches(&['\r', '\n'][..]).to_string())
}

pub(crate) fn select_one(prompt: &SelectPrompt) -> Result<SelectChoice> {
    if prompt.choices.is_empty() {
        return Err(
            io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::InvalidInput, "select prompt has no choices").into(),
        );
    }
    if interactive() {
        return select_one_interactive(prompt);
    }
    select_one_line(prompt)
}

fn select_one_interactive(prompt: &SelectPrompt) -> Result<SelectChoice> {
    let items = prompt
        .choices
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(index, choice)| choice_item(index, choice))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let default_index = prompt
        .default_index
        .min(prompt.choices.len().saturating_sub(1));
    let mut select = inquire::Select::new(&prompt.title, items)
        .with_render_config(render_config())
        .with_starting_cursor(default_index)
        .with_page_size(12);
    if let Some(help) = prompt
        .help
        .as_deref()
        .filter(|help| !help.trim().is_empty())
    {
        select = select.with_help_message(help);
    }
    match select.prompt() {
        Ok(item) => Ok(prompt.choices[item.index].clone()),
        Err(InquireError::OperationCanceled) => match cancel_choice_index(prompt) {
            Some(index) => Ok(prompt.choices[index].clone()),
            None => Err(cancelled()),
        },
        Err(InquireError::OperationInterrupted) => Err(cancelled()),
        Err(err) => Err(io::Error::other(err.to_string()).into()),
    }
}

fn select_one_line(prompt: &SelectPrompt) -> Result<SelectChoice> {
    print_select_header(prompt);
    for (index, choice) in prompt.choices.iter().enumerate() {
        let ordinal = index + 1;
        let number = ui::render(Stream::Stdout, Tone::Command, format!("[{ordinal}]"));
        match choice.detail.as_deref() {
            Some(detail) if !detail.trim().is_empty() => {
                println!(
                    "  {number} {} - {}",
                    choice.label,
                    ui::render(Stream::Stdout, Tone::Muted, detail)
                );
            }
            _ => println!("  {number} {}", choice.label),
        }
    }
    let default = prompt
        .default_index
        .min(prompt.choices.len().saturating_sub(1))
        + 1;
    loop {
        let answer = open_line(&format!("choose [{default}]: "))?;
        if let Some(index) = parse_select_answer(&answer, default, prompt.choices.len()) {
            return Ok(prompt.choices[index].clone());
        }
        println!("Please choose a number from 1 to {}.", prompt.choices.len());
    }
}

/// Plain line input regardless of TTY: used inside line-mode loops where the
/// numbered header has already been printed.
fn open_line(message: &str) -> Result<String> {
    print!("{}", ui::render(Stream::Stdout, Tone::Prompt, "?"));
    print!(" {message}");
    io::stdout().flush()?;
    let mut input = String::new();
    io::stdin().read_line(&mut input)?;
    Ok(input.trim_end_matches(&['\r', '\n'][..]).to_string())
}

fn print_select_header(prompt: &SelectPrompt) {
    println!(
        "{}",
        ui::render(Stream::Stdout, Tone::Heading, &prompt.title)
    );
    if let Some(help) = prompt
        .help
        .as_deref()
        .filter(|help| !help.trim().is_empty())
    {
        println!("  {}", ui::render(Stream::Stdout, Tone::Muted, help));
    }
}

fn cancel_choice_index(prompt: &SelectPrompt) -> Option<usize> {
    prompt
        .choices
        .iter()
        .position(|choice| choice.id == "cancel")
}

pub(crate) fn confirm(question: &str, default_yes: bool) -> Result<bool> {
    if interactive() {
        return match inquire::Confirm::new(question)
            .with_render_config(render_config())
            .with_default(default_yes)
            .prompt()
        {
            Ok(value) => Ok(value),
            Err(InquireError::OperationCanceled | InquireError::OperationInterrupted) => {
                Err(cancelled())
            }
            Err(err) => Err(io::Error::other(err.to_string()).into()),
        };
    }
    let marker = if default_yes { "[Y/n]" } else { "[y/N]" };
    loop {
        let answer = open_line(&format!("{question} {marker}: "))?;
        if let Some(value) = parse_confirm_answer(&answer, default_yes) {
            return Ok(value);
        }
        println!("Please answer y or n.");
    }
}

fn parse_select_answer(answer: &str, default: usize, len: usize) -> Option<usize> {
    if len == 0 {
        return None;
    }
    let trimmed = answer.trim();
    if trimmed.is_empty() {
        return Some(default.saturating_sub(1).min(len - 1));
    }
    let value = trimmed.parse::<usize>().ok()?;
    if (1..=len).contains(&value) {
        Some(value - 1)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

fn parse_confirm_answer(answer: &str, default_yes: bool) -> Option<bool> {
    let trimmed = answer.trim();
    if trimmed.is_empty() {
        return Some(default_yes);
    }
    match trimmed.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
        "y" | "yes" => Some(true),
        "n" | "no" => Some(false),
        _ => None,
    }
}

/// Prompt for a number in `range`, re-prompting (never erroring) on empty input
/// (which takes `default`), non-numeric input, or an out-of-range value. Use this
/// for count-style prompts instead of `open(...).parse()?`, which aborts the whole
/// command on a typo.
pub(crate) fn ask_number(
    label: &str,
    range: std::ops::RangeInclusive<usize>,
    default: usize,
) -> Result<usize> {
    if interactive() {
        let start = *range.start();
        let end = *range.end();
        return match inquire::CustomType::<usize>::new(label)
            .with_render_config(render_config())
            .with_default(default)
            .with_help_message(&format!("{start} to {end}"))
            .with_validator(move |value: &usize| {
                if (start..=end).contains(value) {
                    Ok(inquire::validator::Validation::Valid)
                } else {
                    Ok(inquire::validator::Validation::Invalid(
                        format!("enter a number from {start} to {end}").into(),
                    ))
                }
            })
            .prompt()
        {
            Ok(value) => Ok(value),
            Err(InquireError::OperationCanceled | InquireError::OperationInterrupted) => {
                Err(cancelled())
            }
            Err(err) => Err(io::Error::other(err.to_string()).into()),
        };
    }
    loop {
        let answer = open_line(&format!("{label} [{default}]: "))?;
        if let Some(value) = parse_number_in_range(&answer, &range, default) {
            return Ok(value);
        }
        println!(
            "Please enter a number from {} to {}.",
            range.start(),
            range.end()
        );
    }
}

fn parse_number_in_range(
    answer: &str,
    range: &std::ops::RangeInclusive<usize>,
    default: usize,
) -> Option<usize> {
    let trimmed = answer.trim();
    if trimmed.is_empty() {
        return Some(default);
    }
    let value = trimmed.parse::<usize>().ok()?;
    if range.contains(&value) {
        Some(value)
    } else {
        None
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::{
        SelectChoice, SelectPrompt, cancel_choice_index, choice_item, parse_confirm_answer,
        parse_number_in_range, parse_select_answer,
    };

    fn prompt_with(choices: Vec<SelectChoice>) -> SelectPrompt {
        SelectPrompt {
            title: "Choose".to_string(),
            help: None,
            choices,
            default_index: 0,
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn choice_items_render_label_with_dimmable_detail() {
        let plain = choice_item(0, &SelectChoice::new("run", "New run"));
        assert_eq!(plain.text, "New run");
        let detailed = choice_item(
            1,
            &SelectChoice::with_detail("run", "New run", "equivalent to --mode run"),
        );
        assert_eq!(detailed.text, "New run — equivalent to --mode run");
        // Whitespace-only detail renders like no detail at all.
        let blank = choice_item(2, &SelectChoice::with_detail("run", "New run", "  "));
        assert_eq!(blank.text, "New run");
    }

    #[test]
    fn esc_maps_to_the_cancel_choice_when_present() {
        let with_cancel = prompt_with(vec![
            SelectChoice::new("run", "New run"),
            SelectChoice::new("cancel", "Cancel"),
        ]);
        assert_eq!(cancel_choice_index(&with_cancel), Some(1));
        let without = prompt_with(vec![SelectChoice::new("run", "New run")]);
        assert_eq!(cancel_choice_index(&without), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn line_mode_select_parsing_accepts_default_number_and_rejects_garbage() {
        assert_eq!(parse_select_answer("", 2, 3), Some(1));
        assert_eq!(parse_select_answer("3", 1, 3), Some(2));
        assert_eq!(parse_select_answer("0", 1, 3), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_select_answer("4", 1, 3), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_select_answer("x", 1, 3), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_select_answer("", 1, 0), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn confirm_parsing_accepts_y_n_yes_no_and_default() {
        assert_eq!(parse_confirm_answer("", true), Some(true));
        assert_eq!(parse_confirm_answer("", false), Some(false));
        assert_eq!(parse_confirm_answer("y", false), Some(true));
        assert_eq!(parse_confirm_answer("YES", false), Some(true));
        assert_eq!(parse_confirm_answer("n", true), Some(false));
        assert_eq!(parse_confirm_answer("maybe", true), None);
    }

    #[test]
    fn number_parsing_defaults_and_bounds() {
        let range = 2..=6;
        assert_eq!(parse_number_in_range("", &range, 3), Some(3));
        assert_eq!(parse_number_in_range("4", &range, 3), Some(4));
        assert_eq!(parse_number_in_range("7", &range, 3), None);
        assert_eq!(parse_number_in_range("one", &range, 3), None);
    }
}

new='''/// Pick a provider with a menu that already knows the machine: detected
/// subscription CLIs lead (probed for login state), API routes show whether a
/// key is already in the environment, and a free-input escape hatch keeps
/// every route reachable. Probe-before-ask: the detection is in the hints,
/// the best candidate is preselected.
fn prompt_provider() -> Result<String> {
    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
    let registry = ProviderRegistry::with_overrides(paths.home())?;
    let mut choices = Vec::new();
    for descriptor in registry.iter() {
        if descriptor.kind != deadreckon_providers::registry::DescriptorKind::Cli
            || !descriptor.subscription
        {
            continue;
        }
        let Some(binary) = descriptor.default_binary.as_deref() else {
            continue;
        };
        if !command_exists(binary) {
            continue;
        }
        let detail = match descriptor
            .auth_probe
            .as_ref()
            .map(|probe| deadreckon_providers::probe_cli_auth(binary, probe))
        {
            Some(deadreckon_providers::CliAuthStatus::LoggedIn) => {
                "installed, logged in".to_string()
            }
            Some(deadreckon_providers::CliAuthStatus::NotLoggedIn { .. }) => {
                format!("installed, not logged in (run `{binary} login` before starting)")
            }
            _ => "installed".to_string(),
        };
        choices.push(prompt::SelectChoice::with_detail(
            &descriptor.id,
            format!("{} ({})", descriptor.display_name, descriptor.id),
            detail,
        ));
    }
    for (id, label, env_key) in [
        ("anthropic", "Anthropic API", "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"),
        ("openai", "OpenAI API", "OPENAI_API_KEY"),
    ] {
        let detail = if std::env::var_os(env_key).is_some() {
            format!("{env_key} found in environment")
        } else {
            format!("needs an API key ({env_key} or typed next)")
        };
        choices.push(prompt::SelectChoice::with_detail(
            id,
            format!("{label} ({id})"),
            detail,
        ));
    }
    choices.push(prompt::SelectChoice::with_detail(
        "openai-compatible",
        "OpenAI-compatible endpoint (openai-compatible)",
        "any local or hosted compatible API (base URL + key)",
    ));
    choices.push(prompt::SelectChoice::with_detail(
        "other",
        "Type another provider route",
        "for example a providers.d descriptor id",
    ));
    let selection = prompt::select_one(&prompt::SelectPrompt {
        title: "Choose a provider".to_string(),
        help: Some("detected agent CLIs first; everything stays changeable via deadreckon config provider".to_string()),
        choices,
        default_index: 0,
    })?;
    if selection.id == "other" {
        let typed = prompt::open("provider route: ", None)?;
        if typed.trim().is_empty() {
            return Ok(auto_subscription_cli_provider(&registry)
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "anthropic".to_string()));
        }
        return Ok(typed.trim().to_string());
    }
    Ok(selection.id)
}'''

new='''    assert_success(&output);
    // The PTY colorizes menu ordinals; assert on the ANSI-stripped text.
    let text = strip_ansi(&format!("{}{}", stdout(&output), stderr(&output)));
    assert!(text.contains("No git repo here"), "{text}");
    assert!(
        text.contains("[1] Initialize git and use worktree mode (recommended)"),
        "{text}"
    );
    assert!(text.contains("adds .git here"), "{text}");
    assert!(text.contains("[2] Use copy mode"), "{text}");
    assert!(text.contains("leaves this folder alone"), "{text}");
    assert!(text.contains("[3] Cancel"), "{text}");
    assert!(text.contains("choose [1]:"), "{text}");
    assert!(!source.join(".git").exists());
    assert!(list_runs(&paths, None).expect("runs").is_empty());
}

fn strip_ansi(text: &str) -> String {
    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
    let mut chars = text.chars();
    while let Some(c) = chars.next() {
        if c == '\\u{1b}' {
            if chars.next() == Some('[') {
                for next in chars.by_ref() {
                    if ('@'..='~').contains(&next) {
                        break;
                    }
                }
            }
            continue;
        }
        out.push(c);
    }
    out
}'''

While the full suite runs (it'll ping me when done), here's where everything stands:

## Release thread
- **rc.8**: cleared verify and **all five signed platform builds** for the first time, then failed closed in the trust stage — on my own new basename-conflict guard, which caught yet another latent bug: the artifact tree's extracted per-target directories (loose `deadreckon` binaries, never published) were being swept into `SHA256SUMS` — rc.7's sums had been listing junk users could never download. Fixed: trust artifacts are now scoped to exactly the shapes the publish step uploads, with the conflict guard still fail-closed for real clashes.
- **rc.9**: I caught my own mistake minutes after tagging — the version-bump commit's lockfile had picked up `inquire` from the in-flight UX work while no pushed manifest referenced it, which would have failed `--locked` verify. Cancelled the run; rc.10 ships next from a coherent tree.

## UX overhaul (phases 1–4 committed)
1. **Gradient wordmark banner** on help surfaces — figlet art, per-character 256-color gradient, 12 palettes picked per invocation, version tagline. TTY-only; pipes stay byte-clean.
2. **Smart bare invocation** — no config → first-run welcome (detected agent CLIs, get-going commands, on-TTY offer to run guided setup immediately); configured but runless directory → orientation; runs present → status. Four integration tests pin the routes.
3. **One prompt engine** — `inquire` behind the existing prompt API: arrow-key selects with dim hints, styled confirms, validated number input, Tone-palette theming, colorless under `--plain`/`NO_COLOR`, and the numbered line-mode fallback byte-stable for scripts/tests. Every existing picker (start, campaign, orchestrate, config) inherited the upgrade through the shared API; ~540 lines of bespoke raw-mode terminal code deleted.
4. **Probe-before-ask provider menu** in init — detected subscription CLIs lead with **live login-state hints** ("installed, logged in" vs "run `claude login` before starting"), API routes show whether their key is already exported; the legacy hand-rolled stderr non-git menu unified into the engine.

Once the suite reports green: rc.10 tag, and on publish the full `curl | sh` end-to-end proof with the installer transcript you asked about.

  `config.toml` → `first_run_welcome` (detected agent CLIs from
  `KNOWN_AGENT_CLIS`, the three get-going commands, and an on-TTY confirm

  `ask_number` / `open` — with two render paths. Interactive (stdin+stdout

  styled confirms, validated `CustomType` number input, and text prompts,
